chunks.title: Dograh Integration
chunks.text:
Connect Plivo Audio Streaming with Dograh to power self-hosted voice AI agents

[Dograh](https://www.dograh.com/) is an open-source, self-hostable voice AI platform for building phone agents. Plivo Audio Streaming bridges a phone call to a Dograh voice agent over a WebSocket.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
chunks.text:
Call flow Dograh
  1. Phone Call Plivo Audio Stream WebSocket WebSocket server Dograh Voice agent
Dograh handles the Plivo setup. It creates a Plivo Application and points the Application's **Answer URL** to a Dograh endpoint, so hosting an Answer URL is not required. The Dograh endpoint hosts the WebSocket server that streams the call's audio. On a call, Plivo requests the Answer URL of the auto-created Application and connects to Dograh's WebSocket server, then streams the live call audio in both directions. Dograh's voice agent transcribes the caller, generates a response, and streams the reply back as speech to Plivo over the same WebSocket.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
chunks.text:
| Requirement | Description |
| - | - |
| **Plivo account** | [Sign up](https://cx.plivo.com/signup) and copy the Auth ID and Auth Token from the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/home) |
| **Phone number** | A [voice-enabled Plivo number](https://cx.plivo.com/phone-numbers) in E.164 format |
| **Dograh** | Dograh Cloud, or a self-hosted deployment reachable over HTTPS |

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
chunks.text: For outbound calls, Dograh dials out with a caller ID from the Plivo configuration. No Plivo console changes are required.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
chunks.section: Outbound call setup › 1. Get the Plivo credentials
chunks.text: Sign in to the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com) and copy the **Auth ID** and **Auth Token** from the dashboard.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
Dograh Integration
chunks.text:
1. In Dograh, go to **/telephony-configurations** and select **Add configuration**.
2. Choose **Plivo** as the provider and enter the Auth ID and Auth Token.
3. Leave **Application ID** blank. Dograh creates a Plivo Application when the configuration is saved.
4. Select **Save Configuration**.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
chunks.section: Outbound call setup › 3. Add the default caller ID
chunks.text: Add a **phone number** to the saved configuration in E.164 format, for example `+14150000001`. This is the **From number** (the caller ID) for outbound calls.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
Dograh Integration
chunks.text:
1. Open the saved configuration in Dograh.
2. In the **Phone numbers** section, add the number in E.164 format.

The number then serves as the default caller ID for outbound calls.

> [!NOTE]
>
> This number is not linked to a specific agent. Any agent can use this number as its caller ID when the call is started in Dograh.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
chunks.section: Outbound call setup › 4. Place an outbound call
chunks.text: Trigger a Dograh agent to call a destination number. The call dials from the default caller ID set above.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
Dograh Integration
chunks.text:
1. In Dograh, open the agent that should place the call.
2. Select **Phone Call** in the top toolbar.
3. In the dialog, choose the Plivo **Telephony configuration** and the **Caller ID (from)**, then enter the destination number in E.164 format.
4. Select **Start Call**.

> [!NOTE]
>
> On a **self-hosted** deployment, Dograh must be reachable at a public URL so Plivo can fetch the Answer URL and open the call's media WebSocket. See [Self-hosted setup](#self-hosted-setup) for how to set this up.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
chunks.text: For inbound calls, an external caller dials the Plivo number. The number must route to the Plivo Application that holds Dograh's Answer URL, and it needs an inbound workflow that decides which agent answers.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
chunks.section: Inbound call setup › 1. Get the Plivo credentials
chunks.text: Sign in to the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com) and copy the **Auth ID** and **Auth Token** from the dashboard.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
Dograh Integration
chunks.text:
1. In Dograh, go to **/telephony-configurations** and select **Add configuration**.
2. Choose **Plivo** as the provider and enter the Auth ID and Auth Token.
3. Leave **Application ID** blank. Dograh creates a Plivo Application when the configuration is saved and sets its Answer URL automatically.

   To use an existing application instead, paste its Application ID.
4. Select **Save Configuration**.
5. Open the saved configuration and add the inbound **phone number** in E.164 format, for example `+14150000001`.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
chunks.section: Inbound call setup › 3. Link the number to the Plivo Application
chunks.text: Dograh creates the Plivo Application but does not attach numbers to it. The inbound number should be manually linked to the Plivo application.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
Dograh Integration
chunks.text:
1. Sign in to the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/).
2. Navigate to **Phone Numbers → Your Numbers** and open the inbound number.
3. Set its **Application** to the `dograh-<random>` application shown on the Dograh saved configuration, then save the number.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
chunks.section: Inbound call setup › 4. Assign an inbound workflow
chunks.text: Each inbound number needs an inbound workflow, which is the agent that answers calls to the number.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
Dograh Integration
chunks.text:
1. In Dograh, go to **/telephony-configurations** and open the saved Plivo configuration.
2. In the **Phone numbers** section, find the inbound number and select **Edit**.
3. Set **Inbound workflow** to the agent that should answer when that number is dialed.
4. Save the number.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
chunks.section: Inbound call setup › 5. Receive an inbound call
chunks.text:
Once the workflow is saved, calls to this number are answered by the assigned agent.

> [!NOTE]
>
> A single Plivo configuration can hold multiple phone numbers, each with its own **Inbound workflow**.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
chunks.text:
The Plivo integration works the same on Dograh Cloud and on a self-hosted instance. The only difference is that Plivo has to reach the self-hosted instance directly, so it needs a public HTTPS address.

**Dograh handles this automatically.** Its [self-hosting guide](https://docs.dograh.com/getting-started#setting-up) starts the whole stack with a single Docker command, and this command brings up a Cloudflare tunnel that exposes the instance at a public HTTPS URL.

This default tunnel needs no Cloudflare account or token but the tunnel's subdomain changes each time it restarts. Dograh uses the URL as the base of the Answer URL that Plivo fetches, for example `https://<random>.trycloudflare.com/api/v1/telephony/inbound/run`.

For a stable hostname, run a named Cloudflare tunnel. This requires a Cloudflare account, and the same [guide](https://docs.dograh.com/getting-started#setting-up) walks through the setup.

Once Dograh is reachable at its public URL, the outbound and inbound setup is identical to Dograh Cloud.

chunks.title: Dograh Integration
chunks.text:
| Issue | Solution |
| - | - |
| Authentication failed | Confirm the Auth ID and Auth Token match the values in the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com). |
| Inbound call is not answered | Confirm the number is linked to the Plivo Application configured in Dograh, the number has an inbound workflow assigned, and the Answer URL was set without a warning on save. |
| Call connects but has no audio | The bundled Docker tunnel handles reachability automatically. On a self-hosted custom-domain deployment, confirm Dograh is reachable at its public URL per [Dograh's self-hosting guide](https://docs.dograh.com/getting-started#setting-up). |
| Webhook signature validation failing | Confirm the Auth Token in Dograh matches the Plivo console and that no proxy rewrites the inbound request. |

chunks.title: Use the Plivo CLI with a coding agent
chunks.text:
Give Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity or any agent a reliable way to drive Plivo: one prompt to start, the Plivo skills as files or plugins, and the rules agents follow.

Give your coding agent the CLI reference so it can find commands and work with your Plivo account. A skill is a `SKILL.md` reference file that the agent loads when it needs instructions.

chunks.title: Use the Plivo CLI with a coding agent
chunks.text:
Paste this into Claude Code, Cursor or Codex:

```text Prompt theme={null}
Install the Plivo CLI: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plivo/plivo-cli/main/install.sh | bash. Then run plivo skill install all and use the plivo CLI for my Plivo tasks.
```

You complete the browser sign-in. The skills ask you before anything that spends money or changes your account.

> [!NOTE]
>
> For Codex, run `plivo skill install cli --agent codex`. For Windows and other installation methods, use [Install and log in](/docs/cli/install). To install the skills as a plugin or extension instead, see [below](#install-as-a-plugin-or-extension).

chunks.title: Use the Plivo CLI with a coding agent
chunks.text:
Skills ship inside the CLI, so installing one needs no network call. Install the CLI reference first, then the task skill you need.

| Skill | What it covers | Guide |
| - | - | - |
| `cli` | The CLI itself: every command, the JSON and error shapes, the exit codes and the safety rules. Installed when you give no name. | This page |
| `audio-streaming` | Checks credit, know your customer (KYC) compliance and numbers; sets up an echo, Pipecat or existing voice agent; connects it through a tunnel, application and number; then places a test call. | [Build with a coding agent](/docs/audio-streaming/integration-guides/ai-coding-agent) |
| `sip-trunking` | Connecting an AI voice platform such as LiveKit, ElevenLabs, Retell or Vapi over SIP trunking. | [SIP trunking skill](/docs/voice-agents/sip-trunking/integration-guides/ai-coding-agent) |
| `voice-xml` | Writing and fixing Plivo Voice XML. | [Voice XML skill](/docs/voice/xml/ai-coding-agent) |

chunks.title: Use the Plivo CLI with a coding agent
chunks.text:
Run `plivo login` inside Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, and after you sign in it offers to install the Plivo skills where that agent reads them: `Install the Plivo skills for Claude Code? (Y/n)`

* It asks once per machine, whatever the answer, and not at all when current copies are installed.
* Without a terminal to ask on, such as an agent's own shell, it prints the command instead: `Install the Plivo skills for Claude Code with: plivo skill install all`.
* `plivo login --yes` installs them without asking; `plivo login --quiet` skips the offer. The offer never fails the login. If an install fails, it prints a warning and the command to retry.

chunks.title: Use the Plivo CLI with a coding agent
chunks.text:
```bash theme={null}
plivo skill install                     # the CLI skill → ~/.claude/skills/plivo-cli/SKILL.md (default --agent claude: read by Claude Code and Cursor)
plivo skill install audio-streaming     # → ~/.claude/skills/plivo-audio-streaming/
plivo skill install all                 # every skill
plivo skill install all --agent codex   # → ~/.agents/skills/, where Codex reads skills
plivo skill install all --project       # → <repo>/.claude/skills/ in this git repo, for everyone who clones it
plivo skill install --dir ./my-agent/skills/plivo-cli   # a folder you choose; one skill at a time
plivo skill install --print             # write to stdout for any other tool; one skill at a time
plivo skill install all --dry-run       # show where each would go, write nothing
plivo skill list                        # every skill and whether it is installed
plivo skill list --agent codex          # the same, in ~/.agents/skills
```

* `--agent` can't be combined with `--dir` or `--project`. `--project` is refused outside a git repository. `plivo skill list --project` works from any folder in the repository and shows each skill as `installed`, `installed (differs from bundled)` or `not installed`.
* **Edited copies are kept.** A copy that matches no released version holds someone's edits. `skill install` keeps it and exits `5` unless you add `--force`. The other skills are still installed.

chunks.title: Use the Plivo CLI with a coding agent
chunks.section: Install options › Keep the skills up to date
chunks.text:
A newer CLI brings newer skills. [Upgrade the CLI](/docs/cli/install#upgrade), then run:

```bash theme={null}
plivo skill update --dry-run    # show what would change, write nothing
plivo skill update              # update what is installed
plivo skill update --force      # also replace copies you edited
```

`skill update` looks in `~/.claude/skills` (Claude Code and Cursor), `~/.agents/skills` (Codex) and, inside a git repository, the same two folders under `<repo>`. It replaces a copy only when it matches a released version; anything else counts as your edit and is kept unless you add `--force`. Skills that aren't installed stay that way.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The `first-agent` skill is retired: the `audio-streaming` skill's guided flow replaces it. Installing `audio-streaming` into the default skills folder renames an old `plivo-first-agent` skill's file to `SKILL.md.retired`, so nothing you wrote is lost. `plivo skill update` reports one still installed, with the command that removes it.

chunks.title: Use the Plivo CLI with a coding agent
chunks.section: Install as a plugin or extension
chunks.text:
Some agents install the Plivo skills as a plugin or extension, kept current with the [Plivo CLI repository](https://github.com/plivo/plivo-cli). The skills still run the Plivo CLI, so install it and run `plivo login` once. **Cursor** reads the skills that `plivo skill install` writes to `~/.claude/skills`.

| Agent | Install |
| - | - |
| Claude Code 2.1.275 or later | Inside Claude Code: `/plugin install plivo --marketplace plivo/plivo-cli` |
| Older Claude Code | `/plugin marketplace add plivo/plivo-cli`, then `/plugin install plivo@plivo` |
| Gemini CLI | `gemini extensions install https://github.com/plivo/plivo-cli` |
| Codex | `codex plugin marketplace add plivo/plivo-cli`, then `codex plugin add plivo@plivo` |
| Google Antigravity (app, IDE and CLI) | `agy plugin install https://github.com/plivo/plivo-cli/tree/main/antigravity/plivo` |

Owners of a Claude organization can add `https://github.com/plivo/plivo-cli` under **Organization settings > Plugins & skills** to give every member the skills.

chunks.title: Use the Plivo CLI with a coding agent
chunks.text:
Help, the command map, schemas and docs need no login. `plivo ask` needs a saved profile.

| To learn | Run |
| - | - |
| The flags of one command | `plivo <command> --help` |
| Every command, argument and flag, as JSON | `plivo --map`, such as `plivo --map --query 'data.commands[].path'` |
| One command as JSON, with response fields where the CLI reads them | `plivo <command> --schema`, such as `plivo sip connect plan --schema` |
| What a docs page says | `plivo docs search <keywords>`, `plivo docs show <page>`. See [Read the docs from the terminal](/docs/cli/configure#read-the-docs-from-the-terminal) |
| A how-to answer, with sources | `plivo ask "<question>"`. See [Ask a question](/docs/cli/apis/help#ask-a-question) |

chunks.title: Use the Plivo CLI with a coding agent
chunks.text:
Selected actions require `--yes`, but some billed operations, such as `lookup`, do not. Approval must come from the user, not from assuming the CLI gates every change.

* **Use structured output.** With `-o json`, most commands return `data` on success and `error.code` on failure. `ask -o json` emits JSON Lines, so parse it one line at a time. Action commands such as hangups, updates and deletes print a result too. The local tools (`streams test`, `streams forward`, `upgrade`) send progress to stderr, so stdout stays parseable.
* **Preview changes with `--dry-run`.** Some previews still read account data. Get approval for spending or account changes, then add `--yes` where the command requires it.
* **Branch on the exit code.** `0` success, `1` bad input, `2` login, `3` network, `4` rate limited, `5` refused for safety, `6` CLI too old. See [Exit codes](/docs/cli/configure#exit-codes).
* **Retry only when `retryable` is `true`.** A network failure on a write is `retryable: false`, because the request may have gone through. Read the resource back before you send it again.
* **Don't invent flags.** `--help`, `--schema` and `plivo --map` are the source of truth. An unknown flag is refused, and a mistyped subcommand fails with `BAD_INPUT` and a suggestion.
* **Diagnose before guessing.** Use [`plivo ask`](/docs/cli/apis/help#ask-a-question) for how-to questions and [`plivo … diagnose`](/docs/cli/voice-agent/diagnose-call) for a failed call or message. Both are rate-limited per account. With `-o json`, `diagnose` returns one result with fixed fields; see [Read the result in a script](/docs/cli/voice-agent/diagnose-call#read-the-result-in-a-script).
* **Read only what you need.** `--query` picks fields and `--all` reads every page of a list. See [Pick fields with JMESPath](/docs/cli/configure#pick-fields-with-jmespath).
* **Log in once, by a person.** There is no headless login and no credentials from the environment. A person runs `plivo login` once on the machine the agent uses. Set `PLIVO_FEEDBACK_PROMPT=0` and `CI=1` to turn off prompts. See [Run in CI and from agents](/docs/cli/install#run-in-ci-and-from-agents).
* **Report CLI bugs.** After a command fails unexpectedly, `plivo feedback --bug --dry-run` shows a bug report you can send.

chunks.title: Account, Verify and Lookup
chunks.text:
Account details and balance, usage and spend, subaccounts, OTP verification sessions, and carrier lookup.

Check your account balance and usage, manage subaccounts, verify phone numbers, or look up their carriers. After [logging in](/docs/cli/install#log-in-with-a-browser), start with your account details:

```bash theme={null}
plivo account get
```

* Applications (the webhook URLs a number points at) are on [Connect a number](/docs/cli/voice-agent/connect-number).
* Replace `<values>` with your own and omit `[flags]` unless adding options.
* Paged lists take `--limit`, `--offset` and `--all`. Global flags: see [Configuration](/docs/cli/configure).

chunks.title: Account, Verify and Lookup
chunks.text:
| Usage | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo account get` | Get account details (name, billing mode, credits, address) |
| `plivo account update [flags]` | Update account profile fields |
| `plivo account usage [flags]` | Show usage and spend for a date window. See [Usage and spend](#usage-and-spend). |

> [accordion] plivo account update
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--address <value>` | billing address |
> | `--city <value>` | city |
> | `--name <value>` | account name |
> | `--timezone <value>` | IANA timezone (e.g. Asia/Kolkata) |

chunks.title: Account, Verify and Lookup
chunks.text:
`plivo account usage` shows what the account used and spent over a date window. It needs CLI v1.3.0 or later and reads Plivo's [Usage Summary API](/docs/account/api/usage-summary). Use it for any question about spend: adding up call or message records gives a different, incomplete number. To check the balance instead, use `plivo auth whoami` or `plivo account get`.

It prints a usage row per period, product, type, country and direction; other charges (number rentals, number lookups, fees, taxes); and the total spend with its currency. The `CAUSE` column appears when rows carry an error code or a hangup cause.

```bash theme={null}
plivo account usage --since 2026-10-01 --until 2026-11-01 --granularity month
```

```text theme={null}
PERIOD   PRODUCT  TYPE  COUNTRY  DIRECTION  UNITS  DURATION  AMOUNT   CAUSE
2026-10  message  sms   US       outbound   259              2.0461
2026-10  message  sms   US       outbound   4                0.0316   1000 Unknown error
2026-10  voice    pstn  US       inbound    2      359       0.0510
2026-10  voice    pstn  US       outbound   2      359       0.0840

PERIOD   OTHER CHARGE    UNITS  AMOUNT
2026-10  Number Lookup   8      0.0320
2026-10  Number Charges  2      1.0000

total_spend:  3.2447
currency:     USD
```

chunks.title: Account, Verify and Lookup
chunks.section: Usage and spend › The date window
chunks.text:
* `--since` and `--until` are UTC dates, `YYYY-MM-DD`. `--from-date` and `--to-date` are the same flags.
* `--until` is exclusive: `--until 2026-11-01` ends with October 31. The call and message lists differ: there a bare `--until` date includes that whole day.
* Without `--since`, the window is the 7 days before `--until`. Without `--until`, the window ends at the start of today in UTC. With no dates you get the previous seven complete days.
* A window that holds no day, such as an `--until` that isn't after `--since`, is refused before any request.

`--granularity` sets the period of each row. Plivo limits the window for each:

| `--granularity` | Longest window |
| - | - |
| `hour` | 7 days |
| `day` (Plivo's default) | 92 days |
| `month` | 24 months |
| `year` | no limit |

The CLI doesn't check a longer window. The API refuses it with a 400, printed as a `VALIDATION_ERROR` (exit code `1`), for example `granularity=day supports a max window of 92 days (requested 122 days); use granularity=month for larger windows`.

chunks.title: Account, Verify and Lookup
chunks.text:
| Flag | Values |
| - | - |
| `--product` | `message`, `voice`, `zentrunk` (SIP trunking), `transcription` or `other`. Repeat it, or give a comma-separated list. |
| `--direction` | `inbound` or `outbound`, lower case |
| `--country` | A two-letter country code, such as `US` or `IN` |
| `--subaccount` | A subaccount's auth ID |
| `--hangup-cause` | Voice and SIP trunk rows with this hangup cause |
| `--error-code` | Message rows with this error code |

A value outside these is refused with `BAD_FLAG` before any request. Other charges are left out with `--subaccount`, or when `--product` leaves out `other`. `total_spend` then covers only the matching usage rows.

chunks.title: Account, Verify and Lookup
chunks.section: Usage and spend › Pages and output
chunks.text:
`--limit` sets usage rows per page, from 1 to 1000 (default 100). There is no `--offset`. `--all` reads every page of usage rows; the totals and other charges come with the first page and already cover the whole window. Plivo allows 20 requests a minute on this API, so `--limit 1000 --all` needs the fewest requests.

| `-o` | What you get |
| - | - |
| `table` | The usage rows, the other charges, then `total_spend` and `currency` |
| `json`, `yaml` | The API response under `data`: `meta` (window, currency, `total_spend`), `usage[]` and `other_charges[]` |
| `jsonl`, `csv` | One record per usage row. The totals and other charges are only in `json`, `yaml` and the table. |

```bash theme={null}
plivo account usage                                                   # the last 7 days, by day
plivo account usage --since 2026-10-01 --product voice --direction outbound --all -o json
plivo account usage --since 2026-10-01 --until 2026-11-01 --granularity month --query 'data.meta.total_spend'
plivo account usage --since 2026-10-01 --granularity day --all --limit 1000 -o csv > usage.csv
```

chunks.title: Account, Verify and Lookup
chunks.text:
A subaccount separates resources under your main Plivo account. Its `auth_token` and `new_auth_token` read `[REDACTED]` in every output format. `create` still shows the new token once. Add `--show-secrets` to see them in other output.

| Usage | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo account subaccounts create [flags]` | Create a subaccount |
| `plivo account subaccounts list [flags]` | List subaccounts |
| `plivo account subaccounts get <subauth_id>` | Get a subaccount by auth_id |
| `plivo account subaccounts update <subauth_id> [flags]` | Update a subaccount |
| `plivo account subaccounts delete <subauth_id>` | Delete a subaccount (requires --yes) |

> [accordion] plivo account subaccounts create
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--enabled` | enable on creation (default true) |
> | `--name <value>` | subaccount name (required) |

> [accordion] plivo account subaccounts update
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--enabled <value>` | true\|false |
> | `--name <value>` | new name |

chunks.title: Account, Verify and Lookup
chunks.text:
Send a one-time password (OTP) and validate the code the recipient enters. Enable Verify and create a Verify application first; use its ID as `--app-uuid`. See the [Verify API](/docs/programmable-api/verify/api-overview).

```bash theme={null}
plivo verify sessions create --app-uuid "<app_uuid>" \
  --recipient +14155550101 --channel sms --dry-run
```

Swap `--dry-run` for `--yes` to send the code. Then submit the received code with `plivo verify sessions validate "<session_uuid>" --otp "<code>"`.

| Usage | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo verify sessions create [flags]` | Create a Verify session (spends money: requires --yes) |
| `plivo verify sessions validate <session_uuid> [flags]` | Submit the OTP (`--otp <value>`, required) to validate a session |
| `plivo verify sessions get <session_uuid>` | Get a Verify session by uuid |
| `plivo verify sessions list [flags]` | List Verify sessions |

> [accordion] plivo verify sessions create
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--app-uuid <value>` | Verify application uuid (required) |
> | `--channel <value>` | delivery channel: sms\|voice\|whatsapp (default "sms") |
> | `--explain` | narrate in plain English before executing |
> | `--locale <value>` | language and region code, such as `en-US` (BCP-47) |
> | `--method <value>` | HTTP method for callback URL |
> | `--recipient <value>` | E.164 destination number (required) |
> | `--url <value>` | callback URL for session status events |

> [accordion] plivo verify sessions list
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--status <value>` | filter by status: in-progress\|verified\|expired |
>
> The API puts the rows at `data.sessions`. `--all`, `-o jsonl` and `-o csv` read them there.

chunks.title: Account, Verify and Lookup
chunks.text:
Look up the carrier, number type and formatting for an E.164 number (country code plus number, such as `+14155550101`) through lookup.plivo.com.

```text theme={null}
plivo lookup <number> [flags]
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--type <value>` | lookup type (currently only 'carrier' is supported by Plivo) (default "carrier") |

> [!WARNING]
>
> Each lookup is billed, USD 0.004 per request, and the CLI notes the charge on stderr on each run. It takes no `--yes`, so it runs without confirmation. Preview with `plivo lookup +14155550101 --dry-run`, which prints the request without sending it.

chunks.title: Any REST endpoint
chunks.text:
Call any Plivo REST endpoint the CLI does not wrap yet.

Call a Plivo REST endpoint using the profile saved by [browser login](/docs/cli/install#log-in-with-a-browser). Environment credentials are not read. Start with a read of your account's numbers:

```bash theme={null}
plivo api GET /Number/ --query limit=5
```

chunks.title: Any REST endpoint
chunks.text:
Paths such as `/Number/` are relative to `/v1/Account/<auth_id>/`. Full paths beginning with `/v1/Account/` are used as given. Keep the trailing slash.

`GET` and `HEAD` do not need `--yes`. Writes with `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` require it; `--dry-run` previews the request. For example, create `msg.json` with your sender and recipient:

```json msg.json theme={null}
{"src":"14155550100","dst":"14155550101","text":"Hello from Plivo"}
```

```bash theme={null}
plivo api POST /Message/ --body @msg.json --dry-run
# Sends a billed message:
plivo api POST /Message/ --body @msg.json --yes
```

`--body @-` reads JSON from standard input. With `--method`, omit the positional method:

```bash theme={null}
cat msg.json | plivo api --method POST /Message/ --body @- --dry-run
```

Here `--query` adds a URL parameter, not a JSON filter. Repeat it for multiple parameters.

* **Errors.** An HTTP error gets the same code and exit code as on any other command: a 404 is `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (exit `1`), a 401 exits `2` and a 429 exits `4`. The HTTP status stays in `status_code`, and the API's own body in `context.upstream`. See [Exit codes](/docs/cli/configure#exit-codes).
* **Redirects.** A redirect is not followed. A 3xx exits `3` and names where it pointed, which is usually a missing trailing slash on the path.
* **Secrets.** Auth tokens and passwords in the response read `[REDACTED]` unless you add `--show-secrets`.
* **Paths.** A path with a control character in it is refused before any request.

| Command | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo api` | Call a REST path without a dedicated CLI command |

> [accordion] plivo api
>
> **Usage**
>
> ```text theme={null}
> plivo api <method> <path> [flags]
> ```
>
> **Flags**
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--body <string>` | request body: literal JSON, @path/to/file, or @- for stdin |
> | `--explain` | narrate in plain English before executing |
> | `--header <stringArray>` | extra header as 'Key: Value' (repeatable; overrides defaults) |
> | `--method <string>` | HTTP method (alternative to the positional arg; useful when piping) |
> | `--query <stringArray>` | URL query param as key=value (repeatable; not a JMESPath filter here) |

chunks.title: Get help
chunks.text:
Ask Plivo's AI assistant a question from the terminal, and see your support escalations.

Ask a question about Plivo without leaving the terminal. After [logging in](/docs/cli/install#log-in-with-a-browser), run:

```bash theme={null}
plivo ask "How do I record a call?"
```

To find out why a specific call failed, use `diagnose` instead: see [Diagnose a call](/docs/cli/voice-agent/diagnose-call) or [Check and diagnose a SIP call](/docs/cli/voice-agent/sip-diagnose-call). For messages, see [Diagnose a message](/docs/cli/apis/messaging#diagnose-a-message). To search and read the docs themselves, see [Read the docs from the terminal](/docs/cli/configure#read-the-docs-from-the-terminal).

chunks.title: Get help
chunks.text:
Ask Plivo's AI assistant a question without leaving the terminal. The assistant searches the Plivo documentation, reads the relevant pages, and streams an answer with source links.

**Command:** `plivo ask "<question>"`

**Flags**

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `-i, --interactive` | Keep context between turns. Commands: `/reset`, `/help`, `/exit`. Use `-o table` when input is piped. |
| `--call-uuid <uuid>` | Give the assistant a call to analyze with your question. |
| `--verbose` | Show the assistant's tool calls and results on stderr. |
| `--debug-stream` | Log each raw Server-Sent Events (SSE) frame to stderr for troubleshooting. |
| `-o json` or `-o jsonl` | Emit one JSON event per line: start, tool_call, tool_output, token or final. |
| `--timeout <seconds>` | End an answer after this many seconds with `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT` and exit `3`. Without it, the answer has no time limit. |

Both JSON output options produce JSON Lines, not one JSON document. Read them one line at a time. An error event exits `3`. The stream has no single result, so `-o yaml`, `-o csv` and `--query` are refused.

An answer that stops before it finishes also exits with code `3`. Ctrl-C cancels with exit `130`. Each one-shot question starts fresh; only `--interactive` keeps conversation history.

**Examples**

```bash theme={null}
plivo ask "What hangup cause does Plivo return when the callee is busy?"
plivo ask "Do I need 10DLC registration to send SMS to US numbers?" -o json
plivo ask "How do I record a call?" --timeout 120
plivo ask -i
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> `ask` and `diagnose` share a limit of 5 requests per 60 seconds per account. If you see `RATE_LIMITED` (exit code `4`), wait for the retry interval shown in the error.

#### `plivo support`

List support escalations, which are requests passed from the assistant to support. They are scoped to the person who raised them and require browser login:

```bash theme={null}
plivo support
```

chunks.title: Messaging
chunks.text:
Send and list SMS, MMS and WhatsApp messages; manage 10DLC and Powerpacks.

Send SMS, MMS or WhatsApp messages and check delivery. After [logging in](/docs/cli/install#log-in-with-a-browser), replace the example numbers with an enabled sender and your test recipient:

```bash theme={null}
plivo messaging sms send --src 14155550100 --dst 14155550101 \
  --text "Hello from Plivo" --dry-run
```

Replace `--dry-run` with `--yes` to send the billed message. Check delivery with `plivo messaging get "<message_uuid>"`, using the message UUID the send returns.

SMS is text messaging; MMS adds media. Numbers use E.164 format with a country code, such as `+14155550100`. US application-to-person (A2P) messaging from a ten-digit local number needs 10DLC registration before you send.

Command syntax: replace `<values>` and omit `[flags]` unless adding options. Global flags (`-o`, `--query`, `--dry-run`, `--yes`, `--schema`) and the paging flags `--all`, `--limit` and `--offset` on every list: see [Configuration](/docs/cli/configure).

chunks.title: Messaging
chunks.text:
`plivo messaging sms list`, `mms list` and `whatsapp list` take the same flags (dates below are examples):

```bash theme={null}
plivo messaging sms list --since 2026-10-01
plivo messaging whatsapp list --since 2026-10-01 --until 2026-10-07 --all -o json
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--since <value>` | sent or received at or after this UTC time (`YYYY-MM-DD[ HH:MM[:SS]]`), within the last 90 days. Same as `--from-date` |
| `--until <value>` | sent or received at or before this UTC time. A bare date includes the whole day. Needs `--since`. Same as `--to-date` |
| `--direction <value>` | inbound\|outbound |
| `--state <value>` | queued\|sent\|delivered\|undelivered\|failed\|received |

Plivo searches only the last 90 days. A range starting earlier is refused before any request, with the earliest date you can use.

The Message API can't filter by number, so `--from` and `--to` are refused with `BAD_FLAG`. Use `--query` with `--all` instead:

```bash theme={null}
plivo messaging sms list --since 2026-10-01 --all --query "data.objects[?from_number=='14155550100']"
```

chunks.title: Messaging
chunks.text:
Send multimedia messages in the US or Canada from an MMS-enabled sender, with a publicly reachable media URL:

```bash theme={null}
plivo messaging mms send --src 14155550100 --dst 14155550101 \
  --text "Your image" --media-url https://example.com/image.jpg --dry-run
```

| Command | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo messaging mms list [flags]` | List MMS messages. Flags: see [Filter message lists by date](#filter-message-lists-by-date) |
| `plivo messaging mms send [flags]` | Send an MMS (requires --yes; spends money: use --dry-run to preview) |

`mms send` takes the [`sms send` flags](#send-and-list-sms) plus `--media-url <value>`: URL of a hosted image or media file to attach (repeatable, up to 10).

chunks.title: Messaging
chunks.text:
Use a sender connected to Plivo's WhatsApp Business API. The CLI sends text with `--text`; it has no template flag. For a text reply allowed by your WhatsApp conversation:

```bash theme={null}
plivo messaging whatsapp send --src 14155550100 --dst 14155550101 \
  --text "Thanks for your message" --dry-run
```

For template payloads, use [Any REST endpoint](/docs/cli/apis/api) with the [Message API](/docs/messaging/api/message/send-a-message).

| Command | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo messaging whatsapp list [flags]` | List WhatsApp messages. Flags: see [Filter message lists by date](#filter-message-lists-by-date) |
| `plivo messaging whatsapp send [flags]` | Send a WhatsApp message (requires --yes; spends money: use --dry-run to preview). Same flags as [`sms send`](#send-and-list-sms) |

chunks.title: Messaging
chunks.text:
Give the CLI a message UUID and it explains why the message failed: the error code, the carrier response, and what to change. Find IDs with the `list` commands above.

| Command | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo messaging sms diagnose <message_uuid>` | Explain what happened to an SMS |
| `plivo messaging mms diagnose <message_uuid>` | Explain what happened to an MMS |
| `plivo messaging whatsapp diagnose <message_uuid>` | Explain what happened to a WhatsApp message |

Answers usually take 30 to 120 seconds. Only messages on your own account can be diagnosed. `diagnose` and `plivo ask` share a limit of 5 requests per 60 seconds per account. With `-o json` it prints one result with fixed fields, and it exits `3` if the analysis fails or stops early; see [Read the result in a script](/docs/cli/voice-agent/diagnose-call#read-the-result-in-a-script).

chunks.title: Messaging
chunks.text:
| Command | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo messaging get <message_uuid>` | Get a message by UUID (works for SMS, MMS, and WhatsApp) |

chunks.title: Numbers
chunks.text:
Search, buy, attach and release phone numbers; compliance applications (including India KYC); number masking.

Find a phone number to rent, manage numbers you own, and submit compliance documents. After [logging in](/docs/cli/install#log-in-with-a-browser), search for a US number, then preview and confirm the rental:

```bash theme={null}
plivo numbers search --country US --limit 5
plivo numbers buy "<number>" --dry-run
plivo numbers buy "<number>" --yes
```

* Phone numbers use international format with the country code. Replace `<values>` with your own and omit `[flags]` unless adding options.
* Buying a number spends money and needs `--yes`. In India a number can only be rented (and used for calls) once a compliance application (KYC, know your customer) is `accepted`.
* Paged lists take `--limit`, `--offset` and `--all`. Global flags: see [Configuration](/docs/cli/configure).

chunks.title: Numbers
chunks.section: Compliance when you buy or route a number
chunks.text:
* `plivo numbers buy --compliance-application-id <id>` attaches a specific compliance application. Without it, Plivo picks your most recent applicable one. Use it when you keep one application per end customer, or for an India number when Plivo has none to attach by itself. A malformed ID is refused before any request.
* `plivo numbers update --app-id` or `--trunk-id` on an India (+91) number reads its compliance application first. The update is refused when no application is attached, when it isn't `accepted`, or when it can't be read. `--dry-run` runs the same check. `--force` skips only this local check: Plivo still enforces KYC on its side, so file KYC rather than forcing it. Changing only `--alias` or `--subaccount` isn't checked.
* `--trunk-id` routes the number to an inbound SIP trunk instead of an application; see [SIP trunking](/docs/cli/apis/sip#route-a-number-to-a-trunk). It warns when the trunk is disabled, because no call reaches the number until you run `plivo sip trunks update <trunk_id> --status enabled`. An outbound trunk is refused.
* A number that isn't on your account is refused with a hint to run `plivo numbers list`. A malformed number is refused before any request.

A refusal for a number with no KYC exits with code `1`. The hint lists the KYC steps as CLI commands, and `docs_url` links the India KYC guide:

```json theme={null}
{ "error": { "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
             "message": "refusing to route 91XXXXXXXXXX: This number has no KYC. File KYC first at https://cx.plivo.com/phone-numbers?tab=compliance",
             "hint": "India numbers need an accepted compliance application (KYC): 1) `plivo numbers compliance list --country IN` lists your applications; 2) `plivo numbers compliance create --data @app.json --file 'documents[0].file=@doc.pdf'` submits one (`plivo numbers compliance update <compliance_id>` with the same flags resubmits a rejected one); 3) `plivo numbers compliance link --link 91XXXXXXXXXX=<compliance_id>` attaches an accepted one.",
             "docs_url": "https://www.plivo.com/docs/numbers/rent-india-numbers",
             "retryable": false } }
```

When an application is attached but not accepted, the message names its status, and step 1 of the hint becomes `plivo numbers compliance get <compliance_id>`, which shows the status and any rejection reason.

chunks.title: Numbers
chunks.text:
Look up the documents and fields required for a country and number type:

```bash theme={null}
plivo numbers compliance requirements --country IN --number-type local --user-type business
```

Use those requirements and the [India number guide](/docs/numbers/rent-india-numbers) to write `app.json`. The `@` prefix tells the CLI to read a file. Upload field names must match the document entries in that JSON. `create` submits automatically; check the application status before linking a number. `update` works only on a rejected application and replaces its whole document set.

| Usage | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo numbers compliance requirements [flags]` | List documents/fields required to activate a regulated number |
| `plivo numbers compliance create [flags]` | Create and submit a compliance application (multipart) |
| `plivo numbers compliance list [flags]` | List compliance applications |
| `plivo numbers compliance get <compliance_id> [flags]` | Get a compliance application by ID |
| `plivo numbers compliance update <compliance_id> [flags]` | Update and resubmit a rejected compliance application (multipart) |
| `plivo numbers compliance link [flags]` | Bulk-link numbers to accepted compliance applications |
| `plivo numbers compliance delete <compliance_id>` | Delete a compliance application (requires --yes) |

> | Flag | Description |

> [accordion] plivo numbers compliance create

>   --file 'documents[1].file=@address-proof.pdf'

> [accordion] plivo numbers compliance list
>

> | - | - |
> | `--alias <value>` | filter by alias |
> | `--country <value>` | filter by ISO country code |
> | `--number-type <value>` | filter by number type: local\|mobile\|tollfree\|national |
> | `--status <value>` | filter by status: draft\|submitted\|accepted\|rejected\|suspended\|expired |
> | `--user-type <value>` | filter by user type: individual\|business |

> [accordion] plivo numbers compliance get
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--expand <value>` | comma-separated: end_user,documents,linked_numbers |

> [accordion] plivo numbers compliance update
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--data <value>` | updated application JSON; inline or @file.json (required) |
> | `--file <value>` | document upload as field=path (repeatable; replaces all documents) |

> [accordion] plivo numbers compliance link
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--data <value>` | full link JSON body; inline or @file.json (alternative to --link) |
> | `--link <value>` | number=compliance_application_id (repeatable) |
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> plivo numbers compliance link --link +14155551234="<compliance_id>" --link +14155556789="<compliance_id>"
> ```

chunks.title: Numbers
chunks.text:
A masking session connects two parties through a Plivo number so they don't see each other's phone numbers.

| Usage | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo numbers masking sessions create [flags]` | Create a masking session (spends money: requires --yes) |
| `plivo numbers masking sessions list [flags]` | List masking sessions |
| `plivo numbers masking sessions get <session_uuid>` | Get a masking session by uuid |
| `plivo numbers masking sessions delete <session_uuid>` | End a masking session (requires --yes) |

The API puts list rows at `data.response.objects`, and `--all`, `-o jsonl` and `-o csv` read them there. `get` returns the session under `response`.

> [accordion] plivo numbers masking sessions create
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--call-time-limit <integer>` | max per-call duration in seconds |
> | `--first-party <value>` | first party E.164 (required) |
> | `--record` | record calls in this session |
> | `--second-party <value>` | second party E.164 (required) |
> | `--session-expiry <integer>` | session lifetime in seconds |

chunks.title: SIP trunking
chunks.text:
Create and manage SIP trunks, origination URIs, credentials and IP access control lists, route a number to a trunk, and inspect trunk calls.

Manage Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) [trunks](/docs/voice-agents/sip-trunking/overview), which carry calls between Plivo and your phone system or voice-agent platform, and the calls that went over them. `plivo sip-trunking` is the same command as `plivo sip`. After [logging in](/docs/cli/install#log-in-with-a-browser), list your trunks:

```bash theme={null}
plivo sip trunks list
```

A working setup has four parts. To connect LiveKit, ElevenLabs, Retell or Vapi step by step, see [Connect a SIP voice-agent platform](/docs/cli/voice-agent/connect-sip-platform).

| Part | What it is | Command |
| - | - | - |
| Origination URI | Where Plivo sends inbound calls, such as your voice-agent platform's SIP host | `plivo sip uris create` |
| Credential or IP access control list | How Plivo knows an outbound call really comes from your platform | `plivo sip credentials create` or `plivo sip ip-acl create` |
| Trunk | An inbound trunk points at a URI; an outbound trunk uses a credential or an IP list | `plivo sip trunks create` |
| Number | Routed to the inbound trunk | `plivo numbers update <number> --trunk-id <trunk_id>` |

> [!NOTE]
>
> SIP endpoints (registered devices and usernames) are a different product, under `plivo voice endpoints` on the [Voice](/docs/cli/apis/voice) page.

Command syntax: replace `<values>` and omit `[flags]` unless adding options. Repeat a flag marked `repeatable` for each value. Global flags, and the paging flags `--all`, `--limit` and `--offset` on every list: see [Configuration](/docs/cli/configure).

chunks.title: SIP trunking
chunks.text:
* `--dry-run` previews changes. Dependency checks can still read account resources; no change is applied.
* Passwords are read from stdin only (`--password-stdin`); there is no `--password` flag, and the CLI never prints the password back. Supply stdin from a secret manager or a variable populated without shell history, and avoid shell tracing.
* Values are checked before any request. A `--uri` with a space, a bad port, an unknown transport, a malformed host or a password in it (`user:password@host`) is refused, and so is an `--ip` that is not one address or CIDR range. Repeat `--ip` for more than one; a comma-separated list is refused.
* Plivo accepts IPv4 only, so an IPv6 address in a URI or an IP access control list is refused.
* Plivo can never reach a private, loopback, link-local, carrier-grade NAT, benchmarking, multicast or reserved address. Such an address is refused as a URI host and in `sip ip-acl create` and `update`. A range that allows the whole internet is only warned about.
* A trunk ID must be digits. A SIP call ID, and a URI, credential or IP access control list ID, must be a UUID. Any other value is refused before any request.
* `create` needs `--name` on URIs, trunks and IP access control lists.
* A delete needs `--yes`, and first reads everything that depends on the object: every number routed to a trunk, every trunk using a URI, credential or IP list. If something depends on it, the delete is refused with exit code `5` unless you add `--force` to `--yes`. If the check can't read every page, the delete is refused.
* `--dry-run` alone previews a delete. For an object something depends on, `--dry-run` lists the dependents and exits `5`; `--dry-run --force` previews the delete.

Every `delete` below takes `--force`: delete even though something depends on it (with `--yes`).

> [!WARNING]
>
> Deleting a URI that is a trunk's primary URI also deletes that trunk. Deleting a URI that is a trunk's fallback URI only clears the fallback; the trunk stays. Deleting a trunk detaches every number routed to it, so inbound calls to those numbers stop.

chunks.title: SIP trunking
chunks.text:
An inbound trunk needs a primary URI. An outbound trunk needs a credential or an IP access control list. After `create`, the CLI reads the trunk back and prints its `trunk_domain`: paste that into your platform for outbound calls.

`--secure` turns on Transport Layer Security (TLS) for signaling and Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (SRTP) for audio. Secure trunking is billed per minute.

`sip trunks update` flags take an explicit value so they can be reversed, for example `--secure=false` or `--status disabled`. It keeps an inbound trunk's fallback URI when you change something else; pass `--fallback-uri ""` to remove it. Flags that don't fit the trunk's direction, such as `--fallback-uri` on an outbound trunk, and a `--status` other than `enabled` or `disabled`, are refused before any request.

| Command | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo sip trunks create [flags]` | Create a trunk |
| `plivo sip trunks delete <trunk_id> [flags]` | Delete a trunk (requires --yes) |
| `plivo sip trunks get <trunk_id>` | Get one trunk by ID |
| `plivo sip trunks list [flags]` | List trunks. `--direction inbound\|outbound` filters |
| `plivo sip trunks update <trunk_id> [flags]` | Update a trunk |

> [accordion] plivo sip trunks create
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--credential <value>` | credential uuid (outbound) |
> | `--direction <value>` | inbound\|outbound (required) |
> | `--fallback-uri <value>` | fallback origination URI uuid |
> | `--ip-acl <value>` | IP access control list uuid (outbound) |
> | `--name <value>` | trunk name (required) |
> | `--platform <value>` | check against a platform's guide: livekit\|elevenlabs\|retell\|vapi |
> | `--secure` | enable TLS/SRTP |
> | `--uri <value>` | primary origination URI uuid (inbound) |
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> plivo sip trunks create --name my-trunk --direction inbound --uri "<uri_uuid>"
> plivo sip trunks create --name agent-out --direction outbound --platform livekit --credential "<uuid>" --secure
> ```

> [accordion] plivo sip trunks update
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--credential <value>` | credential uuid |
> | `--direction <value>` | inbound\|outbound (read from the trunk when omitted) |
> | `--fallback-uri <value>` | fallback origination URI uuid ("" removes it) |
> | `--ip-acl <value>` | IP access control list uuid |
> | `--name <value>` | trunk name |
> | `--secure` | enable TLS/SRTP (takes a value: --secure=false) |
> | `--status <value>` | enabled\|disabled |
> | `--uri <value>` | primary origination URI uuid |

chunks.title: SIP trunking
chunks.text:
Give `--uri` as `host[:port][;transport=tcp|tls]`, for example `sip.example.com:5060;transport=tcp`. With no transport, the URI uses UDP. Quote a URI that contains `;`, or the shell cuts the command there. `--transport` adds `;transport=` for you.

A `sip:` or `sips:` prefix is rewritten to the host form, because the API refuses both schemes. `sip:` is dropped. `sips:` becomes `;transport=tls`, on port 5061 when you give no port; `sips:` with another transport is refused. The CLI prints the URI it sent on stderr:

```text theme={null}
--uri is rewritten to sip.example.com:5061;transport=tls: the API refuses the sips: scheme.
```

A URI with a user part, such as `sip:user@host`, is refused; give the host alone. A URI never holds a password: when the platform needs authentication, pass `--authentication-needed`, `--username` and the password on stdin with `--password-stdin`.

| Command | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo sip uris create [flags]` | Create an origination URI |
| `plivo sip uris delete <uri_uuid> [flags]` | Delete an origination URI (requires --yes) |
| `plivo sip uris get <uri_uuid>` | Get one origination URI |
| `plivo sip uris list [flags]` | List origination URIs |
| `plivo sip uris update <uri_uuid> [flags]` | Update an origination URI |

After a URI delete, each trunk that used the URI is read back. The result says which trunks were deleted with it and which are still there. With `-o json` they are in `trunks_deleted` and `trunks_kept`, and any that could not be read are in `trunks_unchecked`.

> [accordion] plivo sip uris create and update
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--authentication-needed` | require authentication (takes a value on `update`) |
> | `--name <value>` | URI name (required on `create`) |
> | `--password-stdin` | read the URI password from stdin |
> | `--platform <value>` | `create` only: fill in a platform's published values: livekit\|elevenlabs\|retell\|vapi |
> | `--transport <value>` | `create` only: udp\|tcp\|tls, added to --uri as ;transport= |
> | `--uri <value>` | host, host:port, host;transport=…, or sip:host |
> | `--username <value>` | username when authentication is needed |
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> plivo sip uris create --name eleven --uri "sip.rtc.elevenlabs.io:5060;transport=tcp"
> plivo sip uris create --name eleven --platform elevenlabs
> plivo sip uris create --name agent --platform livekit --uri "<project>.sip.livekit.cloud"
> ```

chunks.title: SIP trunking
chunks.text:
Pass the password on stdin; the CLI does not generate one. Plivo's rules are checked before any request: the username is 5 to 20 letters and digits, and the password is 5 to 20 characters with at least one of `~!@#$%^&*()_+`.

```bash theme={null}
printf '%s' "$SIP_PASSWORD" | plivo sip credentials create --name c1 --username sipuser1 --password-stdin
```

| Command | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo sip credentials create [flags]` | Create a credential |
| `plivo sip credentials delete <credential_uuid> [flags]` | Delete a credential (requires --yes) |
| `plivo sip credentials get <credential_uuid>` | Get one credential |
| `plivo sip credentials list [flags]` | List credentials |
| `plivo sip credentials update <credential_uuid> [flags]` | Update a credential |

Flags on `create` and `update`: `--name <value>` (credential name), `--username <value>` (SIP username, required on `create`) and `--password-stdin` (required on both: every update rewrites the password).

chunks.title: SIP trunking
chunks.text:
An IP access control list (ACL) allows calls from specified addresses. `--ip` takes IPv4 addresses or Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) ranges (repeatable). On `update` it replaces the whole list, so pass every address you want to keep.

```bash theme={null}
plivo sip ip-acl create --name platform --ip "<platform_ip>" --ip "<platform_cidr>"
plivo sip ip-acl create --name vapi --platform vapi
```

| Command | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo sip ip-acl create [flags]` | Create an IP access control list. Flags: `--name` (required), `--ip`, `--platform vapi` (fills `--ip` with the platform's published addresses) |
| `plivo sip ip-acl delete <ipacl_uuid> [flags]` | Delete an IP access control list (requires --yes) |
| `plivo sip ip-acl get <ipacl_uuid>` | Get one IP access control list by UUID |
| `plivo sip ip-acl list [flags]` | List IP access control lists |
| `plivo sip ip-acl update <ipacl_uuid> [flags]` | Update an IP access control list. Flags: `--name`, `--ip` (replaces the list) |

chunks.title: SIP trunking
chunks.section: Route a number to a trunk
chunks.text:
`plivo numbers update --trunk-id` routes a number to an inbound trunk, taking it off the application it was attached to. It warns when the trunk is disabled, and refuses an outbound trunk. For an India (+91) number the CLI checks its compliance application first, and refuses a number without accepted know your customer (KYC) compliance; see [Numbers](/docs/cli/apis/numbers#compliance-when-you-buy-or-route-a-number).

```bash theme={null}
plivo numbers update 14155551234 --trunk-id "<trunk_id>" --dry-run
plivo numbers update 14155551234 --trunk-id "<trunk_id>"
```

chunks.title: SIP trunking
chunks.text:
| Command | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo sip calls diagnose <call_uuid>` | Diagnose what happened on a SIP Trunking call (AI-powered) |
| `plivo sip calls get <call_uuid>` | Get one SIP Trunking call by UUID |
| `plivo sip calls insights <call_uuid>` | Show the call quality Plivo measured on a SIP Trunking call |
| `plivo sip calls list [flags]` | List SIP Trunking calls |

* `get` and `insights` end with which side hung up: Plivo's hangup cause, code and source. The platform's final SIP response shows as "not available", because no API returns it; the console's SIP logs have it.
* `insights` shows round-trip time, jitter, packet loss, post-dial delay and the Plivo quality score, with the carrier and region of each leg, as the API returns them.
* `diagnose` asks Plivo's AI assistant to explain the call. It reads trunk calls only; for a Voice API call use `plivo voice calls diagnose`. See [Diagnose a call](/docs/cli/voice-agent/diagnose-call) for the JSON result and exit codes.

```bash theme={null}
plivo sip calls diagnose 8f3c1a2e-0d44-4a6f-9c31-2b7e5a90d1f7
plivo sip calls list --direction outbound --since 2026-09-01
plivo sip calls list --hangup-source carrier -o json
```

> [accordion] plivo sip calls list
>
> Without `--until`, the search runs to now. `--until` needs `--since` and must come after it. A malformed `--from-number` or `--to-number` is refused before any request.
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--direction <value>` | inbound\|outbound |
> | `--from-number <value>` | filter by caller ID |
> | `--hangup-cause-code <integer>` | filter by numeric hangup cause code |
> | `--hangup-source <value>` | who ended the call: customer\|carrier\|zentrunk |
> | `--since <value>` | calls ending at or after this UTC time (YYYY-MM-DD[ HH:MM[:SS]]). Same as `--from-date` |
> | `--stir-verification <value>` | "Verified"\|"Not Verified"\|"Not Applicable" |
> | `--to-number <value>` | filter by destination |
> | `--until <value>` | calls ending at or before this UTC time (YYYY-MM-DD[ HH:MM[:SS]]); defaults to now when --since is given. Same as `--to-date` |

chunks.title: SIP trunking
chunks.text:
`plivo sip test --uri <value>` checks from your machine that a SIP host answers, before you send calls to it. It needs no login and never sends an INVITE, so no call is placed. `--uri` (required) is the SIP URI to test, e.g. "sip.example.com;transport=tcp".

When you give a host without a port and it publishes a SIP SRV record, the test warns and names the record's target, with the `--uri` to test it. It still tests the host you gave. See [Check that the platform answers](/docs/cli/voice-agent/connect-sip-platform#check-that-the-platform-answers).

```bash theme={null}
plivo sip test --uri "agent.example.com:5061;transport=tls"
plivo sip test --uri "sip.example.com:5060;transport=tcp" -o json
```

chunks.title: Voice
chunks.text:
Conferences, multiparty calls, recordings and SIP endpoints from the terminal.

Inspect conferences, manage group calls, retrieve recordings and configure SIP endpoints. Calls and live-call streams are on [Make and control calls](/docs/cli/voice-agent/calls). After [logging in](/docs/cli/install#log-in-with-a-browser), list active conferences:

```bash theme={null}
plivo voice conferences list
```

* Hangups, kicks, deletes and `stop-record` need `--yes`. Preview them with `--dry-run` alone. With `-o json`, every action on this page prints a result on stdout.
* Replace `<values>` with your own and omit `[flags]` unless adding options. TTS means text-to-speech.
* Paged lists take `--limit`, `--offset` and `--all`. Global flags: see [Configuration](/docs/cli/configure).

chunks.title: Voice
chunks.text:
Run `plivo voice conferences get "<conference_name>"` to find member IDs.

| Usage | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo voice conferences list` | List active conference names |
| `plivo voice conferences get <conference_name>` | Get conference details (members, run time) |
| `plivo voice conferences hangup <conference_name>` | End the entire conference (requires --yes) |
| `plivo voice conferences record <conference_name> [flags]` | Start recording a conference |
| `plivo voice conferences stop-record <conference_name> --yes` | Stop the active recording on a conference |
| `plivo voice conferences member deaf <conference_name> <member_id>` | Deafen a member (they can't hear) |
| `plivo voice conferences member undeaf <conference_name> <member_id>` | Undeafen a member |
| `plivo voice conferences member mute <conference_name> <member_id>` | Mute a member |
| `plivo voice conferences member unmute <conference_name> <member_id>` | Unmute a member |
| `plivo voice conferences member kick <conference_name> <member_id> --yes` | Remove the member from the conference. It doesn't hang up the member's call. |
| `plivo voice conferences member play <conference_name> <member_id> [flags]` | Play an audio file into a member's channel |
| `plivo voice conferences member stop-play <conference_name> <member_id>` | Stop audio playback to a member |
| `plivo voice conferences member speak <conference_name> <member_id> [flags]` | Speak TTS text to a member |
| `plivo voice conferences member stop-speak <conference_name> <member_id>` | Stop TTS playback to a member |

> [accordion] plivo voice conferences record
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--callback-url <value>` | URL hit when recording finishes |
> | `--file-format <value>` | mp3\|wav (default "mp3") |
> | `--time-limit <integer>` | max recording length in seconds (default 60) |
> | `--transcription-type <value>` | transcription type: auto (results go to --transcription-url) |
> | `--transcription-url <value>` | URL the transcription is sent to |

> [accordion] plivo voice conferences member play
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--url <value>` | URL of the .mp3 or .wav file to play (required) |

> [accordion] plivo voice conferences member speak
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--language <value>` | language code such as `en-US` (BCP-47) (default "en-US") |
> | `--text <value>` | TTS text (required) |
> | `--voice <value>` | MAN\|WOMAN (default "WOMAN") |

chunks.title: Voice
chunks.text:
A multiparty call (MPC) is a group voice room. There is no create step: a room starts when you add its first participant. `participant add` dials out, spends money and requires `--yes`:

```bash theme={null}
plivo voice multiparty participant add support-room \
  --from +14155550100 --to +14155550101 --role customer --dry-run
```

Replace the numbers with your caller ID and test recipient, then swap `--dry-run` for `--yes` to dial. `participant list` shows participant IDs.

| Usage | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo voice multiparty list [flags]` | List multiparty calls |
| `plivo voice multiparty get <mpc_uuid_or_name>` | Get an MPC by uuid or friendly_name |
| `plivo voice multiparty end <mpc_uuid_or_name>` | End the MPC and hang up all participants (requires --yes) |
| `plivo voice multiparty participant add <mpc_uuid_or_name> [flags]` | Add a participant by dialing out (spends money: requires --yes) |
| `plivo voice multiparty participant list <mpc_uuid_or_name>` | List all participants at once (no paging flags) |
| `plivo voice multiparty participant hold <mpc_uuid_or_name> <participant_id>` | Put a participant on hold |
| `plivo voice multiparty participant unhold <mpc_uuid_or_name> <participant_id>` | Take a participant off hold |
| `plivo voice multiparty participant mute <mpc_uuid_or_name> <participant_id>` | Mute a participant |
| `plivo voice multiparty participant unmute <mpc_uuid_or_name> <participant_id>` | Unmute a participant |
| `plivo voice multiparty participant kick <mpc_uuid_or_name> <participant_id>` | Remove a participant (requires --yes) |

> [accordion] plivo voice multiparty list
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--status <value>` | filter by status: active\|initialized\|ended |

> [accordion] plivo voice multiparty participant add
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--from <value>` | source number for the dial-out (required) |
> | `--role <value>` | participant role: agent\|supervisor\|customer (default "agent") |
> | `--to <value>` | destination number to add (required) |

chunks.title: Voice
chunks.text:
List recordings (by call UUID, conference or time range), fetch one, or delete one.

```bash theme={null}
plivo voice recordings list --since 2026-10-01 --until 2026-10-07 -o json
```

* `list` filters on when a recording was added. Without `--since`, Plivo returns the last 7 days.
* `--since` and `--until` take UTC times as `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM[:SS]`. A bare `--until` date includes that day. `--until` needs `--since`. A range can cover at most 31 days.
* `--from-date` and `--to-date` are the same flags. The older `--from-time` and `--to-time` still work under the same rules but are deprecated.

| Usage | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo voice recordings list [flags]` | List recordings |
| `plivo voice recordings get <recording_id>` | Get a recording by ID |
| `plivo voice recordings delete <recording_id>` | Delete a recording (requires --yes) |

> [accordion] plivo voice recordings list
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--call-uuid <value>` | filter by call uuid |
> | `--conference-name <value>` | filter by conference name |
> | `--since <value>` | recordings added at or after this UTC time (YYYY-MM-DD[ HH:MM[:SS]]), at most 31 days per request |
> | `--until <value>` | recordings added at or before this UTC time (YYYY-MM-DD[ HH:MM[:SS]]) |
> | `--from-date <value>` | same as --since |
> | `--to-date <value>` | same as --until |

chunks.title: Voice
chunks.text:
SIP endpoints are credentials that let a software phone or private branch exchange (PBX) register with Plivo. For platform trunks, use [SIP trunking](/docs/cli/apis/sip). An endpoint's `password` reads `[REDACTED]` in every output format unless you add `--show-secrets`.

| Usage | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo voice endpoints create [flags]` | Create a SIP endpoint |
| `plivo voice endpoints list [flags]` | List SIP endpoints |
| `plivo voice endpoints get <endpoint_id>` | Get an endpoint by ID |
| `plivo voice endpoints update <endpoint_id> [flags]` | Update a SIP endpoint |
| `plivo voice endpoints delete <endpoint_id>` | Delete a SIP endpoint (requires --yes) |

> [accordion] plivo voice endpoints create
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--alias <value>` | human-friendly label (required) |
> | `--app-id <value>` | application to attach |
> | `--password <value>` | SIP password (required) |
> | `--username <value>` | SIP username (required) |

> [accordion] plivo voice endpoints update
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--alias <value>` | new alias |
> | `--app-id <value>` | new application id |
> | `--password <value>` | new password |

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.text:
Global flags, output formats and JMESPath queries, paging, exit codes, config keys, reading the docs and opening the console from the terminal, reporting a bug, telemetry, and fixes for common errors.

Flags, output formats and exit codes that apply to every command, plus settings and fixes. For errors, jump to [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting).

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.text:
These flags work on any command (`plivo <command> [flags]`), with the exceptions noted. `--map` and `--version` belong on the root command.

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `-o, --output <format>` | output format: `table`, `json`, `jsonl`, `yaml` or `csv`. Defaults to `table` on a terminal and `json` when piped. See [Output formats](/docs/cli/configure#output-formats). |
| `--query <expression>` | filter the JSON output with a [JMESPath](https://jmespath.org) expression, such as `--query 'data.objects[].number'`. Implies `-o json`. See [Pick fields with --query](/docs/cli/configure#pick-fields-with-jmespath). |
| `-y, --yes` | confirm a gated action, such as sending a message, buying a number or deleting a resource. A missing confirmation exits `5`. Some billed operations, including `lookup`, are not gated. |
| `--dry-run` | preview requests or local changes. It needs no `--yes`. Some commands still make account reads; see [Safety](#safety). |
| `--profile <name>` | run under a named profile from `~/.plivo/config.toml` instead of the active one. |
| `--timeout <duration>` | request timeout, in seconds or as a duration such as `90s` or `2m` (default `30s`). A value of 0 or less is refused. On `ask` and `diagnose`, a `--timeout` you pass also ends an answer that stalls, with `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT` and exit code `3`. |
| `--map` | print every command with its arguments and flags as JSON. Needs no login. |
| `--schema` | describe the command (arguments, flags and, where the CLI reads them, response fields) instead of running it. For the diagnose commands, `sip test`, `voice streams test` and `sip connect plan`, it describes the result they print with `-o json`. Needs no login. |
| `--show-secrets` | show auth tokens and passwords in API responses. Without it they read `[REDACTED]`. See [Secrets in output](/docs/cli/configure#secrets-in-output). |
| `--log-level <level>` | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, or `none` (default `warn`). `debug` prints every HTTP request and response to stderr. |
| `-q, --quiet` | suppress non-data output. |
| `--no-color` | disable colored output. |
| `-h, --help` | help for any command. |
| `-v, --version` | print the CLI version. Root command only, not after a subcommand. |

`--explain` is not a global flag. It narrates in plain English what a command will do before running it, and exists only on `api`, `account applications create`, `auth whoami`, `voice calls make`, `messaging sms send`, `messaging whatsapp send`, `messaging mms send`, `numbers buy`, `numbers release` and `verify sessions create`. Every other command rejects it.

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.text: Most commands return a success object or an error object. Streaming commands are the exception: `ask -o json` and `ask -o jsonl` both emit JSON Lines, while `diagnose -o json` emits one result and `diagnose -o jsonl` emits events. See [Get help](/docs/cli/apis/help) and [Diagnose a call](/docs/cli/voice-agent/diagnose-call).

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.section: Output and exit codes › Output formats
chunks.text:
| `-o` | What you get |
| - | - |
| `table` | A readable table with a curated set of fields. The default on a terminal. |
| `json` | The full JSON envelope described below. The default when output is piped. |
| `jsonl` | One JSON record per line: each object of a list, or the one result. |
| `yaml` | The whole JSON envelope as YAML. |
| `csv` | One row per record, with a header row. A cell a spreadsheet would run as a formula is prefixed with `'`; `+` phone numbers and negative numbers are kept as they are. |

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.section: Output and exit codes › Pick fields with JMESPath
chunks.text:
`--query` runs a [JMESPath](https://jmespath.org) expression (a query language for selecting fields in JSON) on the JSON envelope before it is printed, and implies `-o json`. It also works with `-o jsonl`, `-o yaml` and `-o csv`. On `plivo api`, `--query` keeps its own meaning: a URL parameter as `key=value`.

```bash theme={null}
plivo numbers list --query 'data.objects[].number'
plivo voice calls list --since 2026-10-01 --until 2026-10-07 --query 'data.objects[].{uuid: call_uuid, cause: hangup_cause_name}'
```

* The dates are examples: a call range must be within the last 90 days and no longer than 31 days.
* An invalid expression is refused with `BAD_FLAG` and exit code `1`, before any request. An expression whose result grows too large, or that runs too long, ends with an error.
* An expression that fails only on the result: after a send, buy, create or other write, the request has already gone through, so the CLI prints the unfiltered result with a warning on stderr and exits `0`. Don't run the command again. On a read, it exits `1` with `BAD_FLAG`.

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.section: Output and exit codes › Lists and paging
chunks.text: Most paged lists take `--limit` (1 to 20, default 20) and `--offset` (0 or more); invalid values are refused before any request. `account usage` is an exception: its limit is 1 to 1000, defaults to 100, and it has no `--offset`. Live calls and multiparty participants have no paging flags. `--all` reads every page into one result, and `meta.next` is `null` once every page is read. It stops after 100 pages (2,000 rows at `--limit 20`) with a warning and sets `meta.truncated: true`. A rate-limited page is retried for up to 61 seconds; if it still fails, the rows read so far are printed with `meta.truncated: true` and the command exits `4`. `--all` can't be combined with `--offset`, and `numbers search` doesn't take it. A filter value a list doesn't accept, such as a mistyped `--status` or `--direction`, is refused with the allowed values instead of returning an empty list. Date filters are described on the [Voice](/docs/cli/apis/voice#recordings), [Messaging](/docs/cli/apis/messaging) and [Make and control calls](/docs/cli/voice-agent/calls) pages.

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.section: Output and exit codes › Success envelope

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.section: Output and exit codes › Secrets in output
chunks.text: Auth tokens and passwords read `[REDACTED]` in every output format and in `plivo api` output: a subaccount's `auth_token` and `new_auth_token`, and an endpoint's `password`. Keys and their order stay the same. `account subaccounts create` still shows the new token once. Add `--show-secrets` to see the values.

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.section: Output and exit codes › Error envelope
chunks.text:
Errors go to stderr as JSON and the process exits non-zero:

```json theme={null}
{ "error": { "code": "RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND", "message": "CDR for call uuid … not found",
             "hint": "List available resources with the matching `... list` command.",
             "status_code": 404, "request_id": "…", "retryable": false } }
```

* Switch on `code`, never on message text. The HTTP status decides the code. When the API rejected the request, `context.upstream` holds its own response as `{status, body}`.
* `retryable` says whether sending the same request again is safe. A network failure (`NETWORK_ERROR`: connection refused, DNS, connection cut) or timeout (`UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`) exits `3`, and is `retryable: true` only on a read (`GET`). After a failed write the request may have gone through, so check before sending it again.
* The CLI doesn't follow redirects: a 3xx exits `3` and names where it pointed. A mistyped subcommand or a stray argument fails with `BAD_INPUT` and a suggestion, even with `--help`.

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.section: Output and exit codes › Exit codes
chunks.text:
| Exit | Meaning | Typical `code` values |
| - | - | - |
| `0` | success | None |
| `1` | bad input, or the API rejected the request | `USER_ERROR`, `BAD_INPUT`, `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, `UPSTREAM_ERROR` |
| `2` | authentication; also a WebSocket endpoint that refused `streams test` with 401 or 403 | `AUTH_MISSING`, `AUTH_INVALID`, `AUTH_FORBIDDEN`, `AUTH_EXPIRED` |
| `3` | network failure, timeout or Plivo-side failure, or a redirect (3xx); also an AI analysis that failed, stopped early or ran past `--timeout`, an unreachable `sip test`, a `streams test` endpoint that closed early, and a `streams forward` tunnel that stopped | `NETWORK_ERROR`, `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`, `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`, `UPSTREAM_ERROR`, `INTERNAL_ERROR` |
| `4` | rate limited | `RATE_LIMITED` |
| `5` | refused for safety | `DESTRUCTIVE_REFUSED`: a spend or delete command without `--yes`, or a delete of something another object depends on without `--force` |
| `6` | this CLI version is too old for the API | `CLI_TOO_OLD`; run `plivo upgrade` |
| `130` | interrupted (Ctrl-C) | None |

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.text:
* `voice calls make`, `messaging * send`, `numbers buy`, `numbers release`, resource deletes and mutating `plivo api` calls require `--yes`, checked locally. `--yes` is not a universal billing or account-change gate: `lookup` is billed without it, and updates can change routing without it.
* `--dry-run` previews a change without applying it. Some previews still read account data: `voice streams readiness --dry-run` runs account checks but doesn't request the answer URL, and SIP delete previews read dependent resources.
* Local commands preview too: `auth use`, `auth remove`, `logout`, `config set`, `config telemetry`, `login`, `upgrade`, `voice streams test` and `docs --refresh` describe the action without changing local state. `ask -i` refuses `--dry-run`.
* SIP trunking deletes read everything that depends on the object first, and refuse to delete something in use unless you add `--force` to `--yes`. Preview such a delete with `--dry-run --force`. See [SIP trunking](/docs/cli/apis/sip#safety-rules).

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.text:
`plivo config <subcommand>` views and changes settings in `~/.plivo/config.toml`. Two commands changing the file at once don't lose a change: each waits up to 10 seconds for the other.

| Command or environment variable | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo config telemetry on\|off\|status` | Turn identity telemetry on or off, or show its state. See [Telemetry](/docs/cli/configure#telemetry). |
| `plivo config get <key>` / `plivo config set <key> <value>` | Read or write one setting. Supported key: `telemetry`. |
| `PLIVO_CLI_TELEMETRY=0` | disable identity telemetry for this shell or CI job. Wins over the config file. |
| `PLIVO_FEEDBACK_PROMPT=0` | silence the post-command feedback prompt. |
| `PLIVO_FEEDBACK_TELEMETRY=0` | disable `plivo feedback` submission entirely. |
| `PLIVO_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` | silence the "newer version available" hint. |
| `PLIVO_API_URL=<url>` | send every API request to a server on this machine, to see exactly what the CLI sends, such as `PLIVO_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18555/v1/cli/api`. The host must be `localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8` or `::1`, over http or https, with no user, query or fragment. Anything else is refused. |

The feedback switches take `0`, `false`, `off` or `no`. The feedback prompt never shows when output is piped, or while telemetry or feedback sending is off.

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.section: Read the docs from the terminal
chunks.text:
`plivo docs` reads the Plivo documentation from the shell. It needs no login, so it works before you log in, in CI containers, and in coding agents. For an answer with sources, use [`plivo ask`](/docs/cli/apis/help#ask-a-question).

| Command | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo docs search <keywords...>` | Search the full text of every page. A page matches only if it has **all** the keywords, ranked by how often they appear. Matching ignores case and finds parts of words, so API field names work too. `--limit` sets the number of results (default 10). |
| `plivo docs list` | List every page. |
| `plivo docs show <path-or-title>` | Print one page in full. Give a URL, part of a path such as `voice/api/call`, or a page title. The most specific match wins. |

```bash theme={null}
plivo docs search 10dlc brand registration -o json
plivo docs show "Account API"
```

Text is cached under `~/.plivo/cache` for a day.
