If the network is down, the CLI serves the old cache. `--refresh` skips the cache, on `plivo docs` and all three subcommands; if a refresh fails, the CLI names the error and the cache's age. Without the CLI, add `.md` to any docs URL for plain Markdown. Two index files, which `plivo docs` also reads, cover the whole site for LLMs and agents:

```bash theme={null}
curl -s https://www.plivo.com/docs/llms.txt               # every page, with a one-line summary
curl -s https://www.plivo.com/docs/llms-full.txt          # every page, in one file
curl -s https://www.plivo.com/docs/voice/quickstart/quickstart.md
```

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.text:
`plivo open` opens the matching console or docs page in your browser, and prints the URL first in case no browser opens. No login is needed: the browser's console session applies. `--dry-run` prints the URL and opens nothing; `-o json` returns `{url, opened}`.

| Command | Opens |
| - | - |
| `plivo open` or `plivo open console` | The console home |
| `plivo open calls` | The voice call logs |
| `plivo open call <call_uuid>` | One voice call, with its Call Insights |
| `plivo open sip-call <call_uuid>` | One SIP trunking call |
| `plivo open numbers` | Your phone numbers |
| `plivo open docs [path]` | The docs home, or one page, such as `plivo open docs voice/api/calls` |

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.text:
`plivo feedback` sends a 1 to 5 rating and an optional comment, interactively or with `--rating` and `--message`. Phone numbers, emails, card numbers, IP addresses, bearer tokens, and Indian PAN and Aadhaar numbers are removed from comments before sending. Don't type other personal data or secrets into a comment. `plivo feedback --bug` sends your comment plus the last failed command, kept in `~/.plivo/last-error.json`: its command path, exit code, error code, request ID, CLI version and OS, never its arguments or the error text. The report is printed exactly as it will be sent, and you confirm first. Without a terminal pass `--yes`, or `--dry-run` to only print it. If sending fails, the CLI prints a prefilled GitHub issue link.

```bash theme={null}
plivo feedback --bug --dry-run                       # see what would be sent
plivo feedback --bug --message "what I expected" --yes
```

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.text:
The CLI sends a little usage data with each request so Plivo can see which commands are used, what fails, and which versions are in use. It is **on by default**; you can turn the identity part off at any time.

**Sent on every request:**

* CLI version, operating system and architecture (for the upgrade hint and compatibility), plus `Client-Type: cli` and `Client-Version` headers. These are sent even with telemetry off; they name the client, not you.
* The command name (for example `voice calls list`), never its arguments or flag values.
* With identity telemetry on: the account's Auth ID, the logged-in user's email, the account region, and a user identifier, to see usage per person within an organization.
* `plivo feedback` also sends the rating and comment you type.

**Never sent:** your auth token, API keys or passwords; phone numbers, call or message UUIDs, message bodies, audio or recordings; URLs you pass to commands (answer, WebSocket, callback); flag values, file contents, or anything from your Plivo account data.

**Turn it off:**

```bash theme={null}
plivo config telemetry off        # persistent, stored in ~/.plivo/config.toml
plivo config telemetry status
PLIVO_CLI_TELEMETRY=0 plivo voice calls list   # one shell or CI job; wins over the config file
```

`PLIVO_FEEDBACK_TELEMETRY=0` also disables `plivo feedback` submission.

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.text:
| You see | It means | Do this |
| - | - | - |
| `AUTH_MISSING`, `AUTH_INVALID` or `AUTH_EXPIRED` (exit 2) | No credentials found, or they are wrong or expired | Run `plivo login`. The CLI does not read credentials from the environment |
| `DESTRUCTIVE_REFUSED` (exit 5) | A spend or delete command ran without `--yes` | Add `--yes`, or use `--dry-run` alone to preview |
| `RATE_LIMITED` on `ask` / `diagnose` | Per-account limit on assistant requests | Wait for the interval in the message |
| `NETWORK_ERROR` or `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT` (exit 3) | Could not reach Plivo, or no answer in time | Check connectivity or VPN; `--log-level debug` shows the request. Retry only when `retryable` is `true` (a read). After a write, check whether it went through before sending it again |
| A warning that `--query` failed, with exit 0 | The expression failed on the result of a write that already went through | Don't run the command again. Fix the expression and use it on a read, such as the matching `get` |
| `RATE_LIMITED` (exit 4) on a list with `--all`, or in a loop | Too many requests in a short time | Wait a few seconds and retry; narrow the list with `--since` and `--until` instead of reading every page |
| `BAD_INPUT` (exit 1) with a suggestion | A mistyped subcommand or a stray argument | Use the suggested command; `plivo <command> --help` lists the real ones |
| A value refused before any request (exit 1) | An empty or blank value for a required flag, or an ID that is empty, `.` or `..` | Pass the real value |
| A redirect error (exit 3) | The API answered with a 3xx, which the CLI doesn't follow. The error names where it pointed | Check the path. A missing trailing slash is the usual cause |
| `BAD_FLAG` (exit 1) on `--limit`, `--offset`, `--status` or `--direction` | The value is outside what the API accepts (`--limit` is 1 to 20) | Use one of the allowed values printed in the error |
| `BAD_FLAG` (exit 1) on `--from` or `--to` of `messaging sms list`, `mms list` or `whatsapp list` | The Message API can't filter by number, so every message would come back | Use the `--query` filter the error suggests, with `--all` to read every page |
| A date range refused before any request (exit 1) | The range is longer than 31 days (calls, recordings) or starts more than 90 days ago | Run the ranges, or use the start date, that the error suggests |
| `CLI_TOO_OLD` (exit 6) | This CLI version is too old for the API | Run `plivo upgrade` (or `brew upgrade plivo`) |
| `interactive mode (-i) can't be combined with -o json` | Input is piped, so JSON output was selected | Add `-o table` |
| Table output looks truncated | Tables show a curated subset of fields | Use `-o json` for the full API response |

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.text:
| You see | It means | Do this |
| - | - | - |
| A `sip` command refused before any request (exit 1) | The value breaks a Plivo rule: a credential username that isn't 5 to 20 letters and digits, a password that isn't 5 to 20 characters with one of `~!@#$%^&*()_+`, an IPv6 address, an address Plivo can never reach (private, loopback and similar), an ID that isn't a UUID (or a trunk ID that isn't digits), a user part or a password inside a URI, or no `--name` on `create` | Fix the value as the error says. Give a URI as `host`, `host:port`, or `host:port;transport=tcp` (or `tls`) |
| `numbers update` or `sip connect plan` refused on an India (+91) number | The number has no KYC (compliance application) attached, or its application isn't `accepted`, or couldn't be read | Follow the KYC steps in the hint: file KYC, or check the application with `plivo numbers compliance get <id>`, then link it and retry. See [Numbers](/docs/cli/apis/numbers#compliance-when-you-buy-or-route-a-number) |
| `DESTRUCTIVE_REFUSED` (exit 5) on a `sip … delete` with `--yes` | Something depends on the object: a number routed to the trunk, or a trunk using the URI, credential or IP list | Move or delete the dependents first, or add `--force` if you mean to break them. See [SIP trunking](/docs/cli/apis/sip#safety-rules) |
| `sip connect plan` refused for an Indian number on Vapi | Vapi doesn't support Indian numbers | Use LiveKit or ElevenLabs; see [Connect a SIP platform](/docs/cli/voice-agent/connect-sip-platform#indian-numbers) |
| `sip test` exits 3 with `unknown` | A UDP host didn't answer the SIP OPTIONS request; hosted platforms often ignore SIP from addresses they don't know | Not proof that calls will fail. Test the TCP or TLS URI if the platform has one |
| `sip test` exits 3 with `unreachable` | DNS failed or the port is closed from your network | Check the host and port against the platform's guide, and your firewall |
| `sip test` warns about a SIP SRV record | The host has no port, and its DNS names another SIP target | Test that target with the `--uri` the warning gives |

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.text:
| You see | It means | Do this |
| - | - | - |
| `voice calls get` returns not found for a call in progress | The call record is written when the call ends | Add `--live` to read the call while it is in progress |
| `diagnose` or `ask` exits 3 | The analysis failed, escalated or stopped early, or ran past the `--timeout` you passed (`UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`) | Retry once; otherwise read the raw record with `plivo voice calls get <uuid>` or open it with `plivo open call <uuid>` |
| `voice streams test --expect-audio` exits 1 | Your voice agent sent no `playAudio` back | The test sends a tone, not speech: test with an echo agent, or make your agent speak first |
| `voice streams simulate` or `readiness` fails a check (exit 1) | Your answer URL, its XML or its `<Stream>` isn't what Plivo needs | Read the failed check in the table, or `checks[]` with `-o json`. See [Test your voice agent](/docs/cli/voice-agent/test-websocket) |
| `voice streams test` exits 3 with a close code | Your endpoint closed the stream before the `stop` frame | Read the close code and reason in the error, and check your voice agent's logs |
| `voice streams test` fails with `AUTH_FORBIDDEN` (exit 2) | Your endpoint refused the WebSocket upgrade with 401 or 403 | Log in so the test signs the upgrade, or use `--profile` for the account your voice agent checks |
| `voice streams forward` exits 3 | The tunnel stopped. The application's answer URL was restored | Run `forward` again; try `--tunnel ngrok` or `--tunnel localhost.run` |
| `ssh not found, needed for the localhost.run tunnel` on `streams forward` | The default tunnel shells out to `ssh`, which is missing | Install an ssh client, or use `--tunnel ngrok` |
| The tunnel never comes up on `streams forward` | localhost.run was unreachable or refused the connection | Retry, or use `--tunnel ngrok` (needs ngrok on `PATH`) |

chunks.title: Configuration and troubleshooting
chunks.text: Ask with `plivo ask "<what you see>"`. To report a CLI bug, run `plivo feedback --bug`, which attaches the last failed command (never its arguments). Send other feedback with `plivo feedback`, or open an issue on the [issue tracker](https://github.com/plivo/plivo-cli/issues). The CLI is open source under the Apache-2.0 license: [github.com/plivo/plivo-cli](https://github.com/plivo/plivo-cli).

chunks.title: Install and log in
chunks.text:
Install the Plivo CLI on macOS, Linux or Windows, log in, use it in CI and from agents, switch accounts, upgrade, and turn on shell completion.

Install `plivo`, sign in through your browser with `plivo login`, and confirm which account the CLI will use with `plivo auth whoami`.

chunks.title: Install and log in
chunks.text: The one-line installer detects your OS and architecture, downloads the matching release binary, verifies its SHA-256 checksum, and places it in a user-owned directory on your `PATH`: no `sudo`.

chunks.title: Install and log in
chunks.text:
```bash theme={null}
brew install plivo/tap/plivo
```

Without Homebrew, or on WSL, use the install script:

```bash theme={null}
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plivo/plivo-cli/main/install.sh | bash
```

chunks.title: Install and log in
chunks.text:
```powershell theme={null}
scoop bucket add plivo https://github.com/plivo/homebrew-tap
scoop install plivo
```

Without Scoop, use the install script in PowerShell:

```powershell theme={null}
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plivo/plivo-cli/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

To build from source (Go 1.26 or later): `git clone https://github.com/plivo/plivo-cli && cd plivo-cli && go build -o plivo .`

Then [log in](#log-in-with-a-browser). If a coding agent will drive the CLI, also install the [Plivo skills](/docs/cli/agents).

| Installer setting | Description |
| - | - |
| `PLIVO_CLI_VERSION` | install a specific release tag instead of the latest (for example `v1.3.2`). |
| `PLIVO_INSTALL_DIR` | install into this directory instead of the first user-owned directory on `PATH`. |

**Verify a release.** Binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows (amd64 and arm64), `SHA256SUMS` and its signature are on the [GitHub releases page](https://github.com/plivo/plivo-cli/releases). The checksums are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/installation/) in keyless mode; `install.sh`, `install.ps1` and `plivo upgrade` verify that signature when cosign is installed. To check by hand:

```bash theme={null}
V=v1.3.2
for f in SHA256SUMS SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS.pem; do
  curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/plivo/plivo-cli/releases/download/$V/$f"
done
cosign verify-blob SHA256SUMS \
  --signature SHA256SUMS.sig --certificate SHA256SUMS.pem \
  --certificate-identity cx-tech@plivo.com \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com
```

`Verified OK` means the checksums were signed by that Plivo identity. Pin both the identity and the issuer: without them any valid Sigstore signature would pass.

chunks.title: Install and log in
chunks.text:
`plivo login` is the only way to sign in. It opens the Plivo Console in your browser, where you sign in and approve access, so your password never touches the CLI. The CLI saves a named **profile** in `~/.plivo/config.toml` and puts the auth token in your OS credential store (Keychain on macOS, Credential Manager on Windows, Secret Service on Linux). Only when no credential store is available is the token written into `~/.plivo/config.toml`, readable by you alone.

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `-n, --name <profile>` | name to save the profile under. When omitted, login derives it from your organization; the flag default is `default`. |
| `--no-verify` | skip the check request to `GET /Account/` after login (offline or mock use only). |
| `-y, --yes` | inside a coding agent, install the Plivo skills without asking. See [Skills offer inside a coding agent](#skills-offer-inside-a-coding-agent). |
| `-q, --quiet` | skip the skills offer. |

```bash theme={null}
plivo login --name staging
```

**Browser can't reach the terminal?** In a container, WSL, a VM or over SSH, the page the browser opens after you approve may fail to load. Copy the full URL from the address bar and paste it into the terminal. The CLI accepts only the URL of this login.

chunks.title: Install and log in
chunks.section: Log in with a browser › Skills offer inside a coding agent
chunks.text: Run `plivo login` inside Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, and after sign-in it offers to install the Plivo skills where that agent reads them. `--yes` installs them without asking; `--quiet` skips the offer. See [Offer after login](/docs/cli/agents#offer-after-login).

chunks.title: Install and log in
chunks.section: Run in CI and from agents
chunks.text:
There is no headless login, and `PLIVO_AUTH_ID` and `PLIVO_AUTH_TOKEN` are not read from the environment. For a CI runner, a container or a coding agent, a person must run `plivo login` once in the environment that will run commands; later commands use that saved profile and its credential store. Copying `config.toml` alone does not copy a token stored in the OS keychain, so use a persistent runner with access to the same profile and credential store, then confirm with `plivo auth whoami`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> A saved profile grants access to your account. For automated use, select the intended account, use [subaccounts](/docs/cli/apis/account#subaccounts) to separate resources where appropriate, and protect the machine that holds the profile.

Useful settings in scripts (see [Telemetry](/docs/cli/configure#telemetry) for what the last one turns off):

```bash theme={null}
export PLIVO_FEEDBACK_PROMPT=0    # never show the "rate the CLI?" prompt
export CI=1                       # turn off all prompts that need a terminal
export PLIVO_CLI_TELEMETRY=0      # see Telemetry
```

chunks.title: Install and log in
chunks.text:
A profile is a saved login. Keep one profile per account or subaccount and switch between them. Logging in to a different organization saves a second profile, named after it, instead of replacing the first.

| Command | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo auth list` | List saved profiles and show which one is active |
| `plivo auth use <name>` | Make a profile the active one for later commands |
| `plivo auth whoami` | Show the account behind the active profile (add `-o json` for JSON) |
| `plivo auth remove <name>` | Delete a profile and its stored token |

The CLI picks credentials from the `--profile` flag, then the active profile. Use `--profile` to run one command under another profile without switching:

```bash theme={null}
plivo --profile staging numbers list
```

chunks.title: Install and log in
chunks.text:
`plivo logout [profile]` removes a saved profile and deletes its token from the credential store.

```bash theme={null}
plivo logout            # the active profile
plivo logout staging
```

chunks.title: Install and log in
chunks.text:
`plivo upgrade` fetches the latest release, verifies the binary against the release's `SHA256SUMS` (and, when cosign is installed, the signature on those checksums), then atomically replaces the running executable. With `-o json` it prints one summary on stdout and progress on stderr.

A binary installed by Homebrew (it lives in a Homebrew Cellar) is refused, with a pointer to `brew upgrade plivo`, so the two don't fight over the same file. A binary from the install script works with `plivo upgrade`, even in a Homebrew `bin` folder.

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--check` | report whether a newer release exists without installing it. |
| `--version <tag>` | install a specific release tag instead of the latest. |
| `--force` | reinstall even if you are already on the target release. |

```bash theme={null}
plivo upgrade            # install the latest release
plivo upgrade --check    # check only
plivo upgrade --version v1.3.2
```

On a terminal, the CLI prints a one-line hint on stderr when a newer version is available, at most once every 24 hours. Set `PLIVO_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` to silence it.

chunks.title: Install and log in
chunks.text:
`plivo completion <shell>` generates a completion script so commands, subcommands and flags tab-complete. Run `plivo completion <shell> --help` for shell-specific notes.

```bash theme={null}
plivo completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_plivo"                     # zsh
source <(plivo completion bash)                                  # bash: enable in this shell
mkdir -p ~/.config/fish/completions                              # fish
plivo completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/plivo.fish
plivo completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression   # PowerShell
```

chunks.title: Plivo CLI
chunks.text:
Build, test and debug voice agents, calls and messaging on Plivo from your terminal, yourself or through a coding agent.

The Plivo CLI lets you work with Plivo from your terminal. Connect a voice agent to a phone number, make a test call, find out why a call failed, send a message or check what you spent, without opening the console or writing API code. You can run the commands yourself, or connect the CLI to your coding agent, such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, and ask for what you need in plain English.

```bash theme={null}
brew install plivo/tap/plivo
plivo login
plivo numbers list
```

Homebrew works on macOS and Linux. For Windows and other installers, see [Install and log in](/docs/cli/install).

chunks.title: Plivo CLI
chunks.text:
* [Use it with a coding agent](/docs/cli/agents): paste one prompt into your coding agent. It installs the CLI and the Plivo skills, then does the work, asking you before anything that spends money.
* [Use it yourself](/docs/cli/install): install with one command, log in through your browser, and list your numbers.

chunks.title: Plivo CLI
chunks.text:
* [Voice agents over Audio Streaming](/docs/cli/voice-agent/test-websocket): test your WebSocket connection without a phone, connect your voice agent to a number and take real calls.
* [Voice agents over SIP trunking](/docs/cli/voice-agent/connect-sip-platform): connect LiveKit, ElevenLabs, Retell, Vapi or your own SIP platform to a number.
* [Debug a call](/docs/cli/voice-agent/diagnose-call): get a plain-English explanation of why a call failed, who hung up, and how to fix it.

You can also use it for [calls](/docs/cli/voice-agent/calls), [messaging](/docs/cli/apis/messaging), [numbers](/docs/cli/apis/numbers), [account and usage](/docs/cli/apis/account), [questions to Plivo's AI assistant](/docs/cli/apis/help) and [any other Plivo API](/docs/cli/apis/api).

chunks.title: Plivo CLI
chunks.text:
* **Confirm gated actions.** Buying a number, placing a call and deleting account resources require `--yes`. This is not a universal billing gate: [number lookup](/docs/cli/apis/account#lookup) is billed without it.
* **Preview first.** `--dry-run` previews changes. Some checks still read account data, such as `voice streams readiness`.
* **Easy to script.** Most commands return one JSON document with `-o json`. `ask` streams JSON Lines. Exit codes describe failures.
* **Secrets are redacted.** Auth tokens and passwords normally read `[REDACTED]`. Creating a subaccount shows its new token once; `--show-secrets` reveals other redacted values.

See [Configuration and troubleshooting](/docs/cli/configure) for every flag, output format and exit code.

chunks.title: Make and control calls
chunks.text:
Place outbound calls to your agent, transfer a live call to a human, play or record, and start or stop a stream on a live call.

Place an outbound call, inspect it, or control its audio while it is active. [Log in](/docs/cli/install#log-in-with-a-browser), use a caller number on your account, and choose a test recipient:

```bash theme={null}
plivo voice calls make --from +14155550100 --to +14155550101 --dry-run
```

This previews a call that plays Plivo's hello demo. Replace `--dry-run` with `--yes` to place the billed call. To call your voice agent instead, supply its public answer URL, which returns `<Stream>` XML:

```bash theme={null}
plivo voice calls make --from +14155550100 --to +14155550101 \
  --answer-url https://agent.example.com/answer --answer-method POST --dry-run
```

For human handoff, run `plivo voice calls transfer "<call_uuid>" --legs aleg --aleg-url "<url>"`, where the new URL returns `<Dial>` XML.

* Find a call UUID with `plivo voice calls list` after the call ends, or `plivo voice calls list --live` while it is active. A call leg is one side of a connected call (aleg is the caller, bleg the callee). DTMF means keypad tones, and TTS means text-to-speech.
* Replace example numbers, URLs and `<values>` with yours. Omit `[flags]` unless adding options.
* Global flags: see [Configuration](/docs/cli/configure).

chunks.title: Make and control calls
chunks.text: `voice calls make` spends money and requires `--yes`. Live-call controls (`play`, `speak`, `record`, `dtmf`, `transfer`, `stop-*`) act on an established call and don't need it. `hangup` needs `--yes`, and previews with `--dry-run` alone. With `-o json`, the live-call controls and `hangup` print a result on stdout, such as `{"data": {"call_uuid": "<call_uuid>", "hung_up": true}}`.

chunks.title: Make and control calls
chunks.section: Calls › Read a call in progress
chunks.text:
`voice calls get` reads the call record, which Plivo writes when the call ends. Add `--live` to read a call still in progress. If the call has already ended, `--live` returns not found.

`voice calls list --live` lists the calls in progress. Plivo returns only their UUIDs, with no filter or paging, so `--live` takes no other list flag. With `-o json` the UUIDs are in `data.calls`.

```bash theme={null}
plivo voice calls get "<call_uuid>" --live
plivo voice calls list --live
```

chunks.title: Make and control calls
chunks.section: Calls › Filter the call list by date
chunks.text:
`plivo voice calls list` shows the newest calls first. Without a date, Plivo returns the last 7 days.

```bash theme={null}
plivo voice calls list --since 2026-10-01 --until 2026-10-07
plivo voice calls list --since "2026-10-01 09:00" --until 2026-10-07 -o json
plivo voice calls list --since 2026-10-01 --until 2026-10-07 --all          # every page, not just the first 20 rows
```

* `--since` and `--until` filter on when a call ended, in UTC, as `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM[:SS]`. `--from-date` and `--to-date` are the same flags.
* A bare `--until` date includes that whole day. `--until` needs `--since`.
* Plivo searches only the last 90 days, at most 31 days per request. A range outside either limit is refused before any request, and the error says what to run instead, such as the ranges to split it into.

| Usage | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo voice calls make [flags]` | Make an outbound call (requires --yes; spends money: use --dry-run to preview) |
| `plivo voice calls list [flags]` | List calls (paged with `--limit`, `--offset`, `--all`) |
| `plivo voice calls get <call_uuid> [flags]` | Get a call by UUID. `--live` gets a call in progress, not its record. |
| `plivo voice calls hangup <call_uuid>` | Hang up a live call (requires --yes) |
| `plivo voice calls transfer <call_uuid> [flags]` | Transfer one or both legs of a live call to new PlivoXML URLs |
| `plivo voice calls play <call_uuid> [flags]` | Play audio file(s) into a live call |
| `plivo voice calls stop-play <call_uuid>` | Stop any audio playing in a live call |
| `plivo voice calls speak <call_uuid> [flags]` | Speak text into a live call via TTS |
| `plivo voice calls stop-speak <call_uuid>` | Stop any TTS playing in a live call |
| `plivo voice calls record <call_uuid> [flags]` | Start recording a live call |
| `plivo voice calls stop-record <call_uuid>` | Stop the active recording on a live call |
| `plivo voice calls dtmf <call_uuid> [flags]` | Send DTMF tones into a live call |

> [accordion] plivo voice calls make
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--answer-method <value>` | GET\|POST (default: GET for the hello demo, else Plivo's POST) |
> | `--answer-url <value>` | URL returning PlivoXML to play on answer (default: Plivo's hello demo) (default "[https://s3.amazonaws.com/static.plivo.com/answer.xml](https://s3.amazonaws.com/static.plivo.com/answer.xml)") |
> | `--explain` | narrate in plain English before executing |
> | `--from <value>` | source number in international format, such as `+14155550100`; must be on your account (required) |
> | `--hangup-url <value>` | URL hit when call ends |
> | `--machine-detection <value>` | answering-machine detection: true\|hangup (off when omitted) |
> | `--ring-url <value>` | URL hit when call starts ringing |
> | `--to <value>` | destination: an international number with country code or a `sip:` URI; quote multiple destinations joined by `<` (required) |
>
> A `--from` that isn't an E.164 number, or a `--to` part that is neither an E.164 number nor a `sip:` URI, is refused before any request.

chunks.title: Make and control calls
chunks.section: Calls › Filter the call list by date
chunks.text:
> [accordion] plivo voice calls list
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--direction <value>` | inbound\|outbound |
> | `--from <value>` | filter by from_number |
> | `--to <value>` | filter by to_number |
> | `--live` | list the UUIDs of the calls in progress, not call records (takes no other list flag) |
> | `--since <value>` | calls ending at or after this UTC time (YYYY-MM-DD[ HH:MM[:SS]]), within the last 90 days, at most 31 days per request |
> | `--until <value>` | calls ending at or before this UTC time (YYYY-MM-DD[ HH:MM[:SS]]) |
> | `--from-date <value>` | same as --since |
> | `--to-date <value>` | same as --until |

> [accordion] plivo voice calls transfer
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--aleg-method <value>` | GET\|POST (default "POST") |
> | `--aleg-url <value>` | new URL for A-leg (caller side) |
> | `--bleg-method <value>` | GET\|POST (default "POST") |
> | `--bleg-url <value>` | new URL for B-leg (callee side) |
> | `--legs <value>` | which leg(s) to act on: aleg\|bleg\|both (default "aleg") |

> [accordion] plivo voice calls play
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--legs <value>` | aleg\|bleg\|both (default "aleg") |
> | `--length <integer>` | stop after N seconds (0 = full file) |
> | `--loop` | loop the playback |
> | `--mix` | mix with the call audio (else replace) (default true) |
> | `--urls <value>` | comma-separated list of audio file URLs to play (required) |

> [accordion] plivo voice calls speak
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--language <value>` | language code, e.g. en-US, en-GB, hi-IN (default "en-US") |
> | `--legs <value>` | aleg\|bleg\|both (default "aleg") |
> | `--mix` | mix with the call audio (else replace) (default true) |
> | `--text <value>` | text to speak via TTS (required) |
> | `--voice <value>` | voice: MAN\|WOMAN (default "WOMAN") |

> [accordion] plivo voice calls record
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--callback-method <value>` | GET\|POST (default "POST") |
> | `--callback-url <value>` | URL hit when recording finishes |
> | `--file-format <value>` | mp3\|wav (default "mp3") |
> | `--record-channel-type <value>` | mono\|stereo (stereo puts each leg on its own channel) |
> | `--time-limit <integer>` | max recording length in seconds (default 60) |
> | `--transcription-type <value>` | transcription type: auto\|hybrid\|manual (results go to --transcription-url) |
> | `--transcription-url <value>` | URL the transcription is sent to |

chunks.title: Make and control calls
chunks.section: Calls › Filter the call list by date
chunks.text:
> [accordion] plivo voice calls dtmf
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--digits <value>` | DTMF digits to send, e.g. 1234# (required) |
> | `--leg <value>` | aleg\|bleg (default "aleg") |

chunks.title: Make and control calls
chunks.text:
Start a WebSocket audio stream on an already-answered call (instead of via `<Stream>` XML), list the streams on a call, or stop them.

| Usage | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo voice calls streams start <call_uuid> [flags]` | Start a new audio stream on a call |
| `plivo voice calls streams list <call_uuid>` | List active streams on a call |
| `plivo voice calls streams get <call_uuid> <stream_id>` | Get details for one stream on a call |
| `plivo voice calls streams stop <call_uuid> [stream_id]` | Stop one stream (with id) or all streams (without id) on a call |

> [accordion] plivo voice calls streams start
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--audio-track <value>` | inbound\|outbound\|both (default "inbound") |
> | `--bidirectional` | let the WebSocket send audio back into the call (needs --audio-track inbound) |
> | `--callback-url <value>` | alias for --stream-status-callback |
> | `--content-type <value>` | audio codec content-type (default "audio/x-l16;rate=16000") |
> | `--extra-headers <value>` | comma-separated extra WebSocket headers (k1=v1,k2=v2) |
> | `--stream-status-callback <value>` | URL hit when stream starts/ends |
> | `--url <value>` | WebSocket URL to receive audio (wss\://...) (required) |

chunks.title: Connect a number to your agent
chunks.text:
Create an application that points at your answer URL and attach a Plivo number to it.

Route incoming calls to your voice agent by attaching a number to a Plivo application. An application stores webhook URLs: HTTP endpoints Plivo requests during a call. Its answer URL returns your `<Stream>` XML.

Before you start, [log in](/docs/cli/install#log-in-with-a-browser), rent a voice-enabled number, and deploy a public answer URL. Test it with [simulate](/docs/cli/voice-agent/test-websocket#simulate-a-call-to-your-answer-url). Then create the application, using your URL:

```bash theme={null}
plivo account applications create --app-name my-agent \
  --answer-url https://agent.example.com/plivo/answer --answer-method POST -o json
```

Put `data.app_id` from the result in place of `"<app_id>"`, and your rented number in place of `14155551234`:

```bash theme={null}
plivo numbers update 14155551234 --app-id "<app_id>" --dry-run
plivo numbers update 14155551234 --app-id "<app_id>"
plivo voice streams readiness 14155551234
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> The second command changes routing immediately and does not require `--yes`. The preview shows the current binding: save the previous application or trunk ID first. To restore it, run `numbers update` with the saved `--app-id` or `--trunk-id`.

The readiness check places no call. To move to a new server later, update the application's URLs; every number attached to it uses the new URL. Searching, buying and compliance are on the [Numbers](/docs/cli/apis/numbers) page.

chunks.title: Connect a number to your agent
chunks.text:
An application holds the webhook URLs Plivo calls for a number. Attach numbers with `plivo numbers update --app-id`, and update its URLs without touching the number. Global options such as `--profile` and `-o json` are in [Configuration](/docs/cli/configure#global-flags).

| Command | What it does |
| - | - |
| `plivo account applications create` | Create a new application |
| `plivo account applications delete` | Delete an application (requires --yes) |
| `plivo account applications get` | Get application details |
| `plivo account applications list` | List applications |
| `plivo account applications update` | Update an application |

> [accordion] plivo account applications create
>
> `plivo account applications create [flags]`
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--answer-method <value>` | GET\|POST (default "POST") |
> | `--answer-url <value>` | webhook for incoming calls (required) |
> | `--app-name <value>` | application name (required) |
> | `--default-number-app` | set as default for new numbers |
> | `--explain` | narrate in plain English before executing |
> | `--fallback-answer-url <value>` | backup webhook if answer-url fails |
> | `--hangup-url <value>` | webhook for call hangup |
> | `--log-incoming-messages` | log inbound SMS content (default true) |
> | `--message-url <value>` | webhook for inbound SMS |

> [accordion] plivo account applications delete
>
> `plivo account applications delete <app_id> [flags]`
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--cascade` | delete the app's endpoints too; --cascade=false keeps them (default true) |
> | `--new-endpoint-application <value>` | with --cascade=false, the app_id the endpoints move to |
>
> By default the app's endpoints are deleted with it. `--cascade=false` keeps them, detached from any app; add `--new-endpoint-application <app_id>` to move them to another app instead:
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> plivo account applications delete "<app_id>" --cascade=false --new-endpoint-application "<other_app_id>" --yes
> ```

> [accordion] plivo account applications get
>
> `plivo account applications get <app_id>`

> [accordion] plivo account applications list
>
> `plivo account applications list [flags]`
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--all` | fetch every page (stops after 100 pages) |
> | `--limit <integer>` | results per page (1-20) (default 20) |
> | `--offset <integer>` | pagination offset |

> [accordion] plivo account applications update
>
> `plivo account applications update <app_id> [flags]`
>
> | Flag | Description |
> | - | - |
> | `--answer-method <value>` | GET\|POST |
> | `--answer-url <value>` | new answer URL |
> | `--app-name <value>` | new application name |
> | `--hangup-url <value>` | new hangup URL |
> | `--message-url <value>` | new message URL |

chunks.title: Test and connect a SIP voice-agent platform
chunks.text:
Get a Plivo number ready for LiveKit, ElevenLabs, Retell or Vapi over SIP trunking: check the platform's SIP host answers, plan every step, and fill in the platform's values.

Connect a voice-agent platform such as LiveKit, ElevenLabs, Retell or Vapi over Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) with [SIP trunking](/docs/voice-agents/sip-trunking/overview): an inbound trunk sends calls to your number on to the platform, and an outbound trunk lets the platform place calls through Plivo. First, check a platform host (use yours if it isn't ElevenLabs). This needs no login and places no call:

```bash theme={null}
plivo sip test --uri "sip.rtc.elevenlabs.io:5061;transport=tls"
```

Then `plivo sip connect plan` checks your number and prints every command to run, in order, changing nothing. As you run the plan's steps, `--platform` on `sip uris create`, `sip ip-acl create` and `sip trunks create` fills in the platform's SIP host, port, transport and IP addresses from Plivo's integration guide.

chunks.title: Test and connect a SIP voice-agent platform
chunks.text:
Example output for the TLS test above, with illustrative addresses, timings and certificate dates:

```text theme={null}
CHECK  STATUS  DETAIL
dns    pass    sip.rtc.elevenlabs.io resolves to 136.112.48.140 (194 ms)
tcp    pass    connected to 136.112.48.140:5061 (271 ms)
tls    pass    TLS 1.3; certificate for sip.rtc.elevenlabs.io valid until 2026-12-07 (52 days) (297 ms)

result: reachable (TLS to sip.rtc.elevenlabs.io:5061)
A pass means the host answers, not that the platform will accept calls.
```

| Transport | What is checked |
| - | - |
| TCP | DNS lookup, then a TCP connection (port 5060 unless the URI gives one) |
| TLS (`;transport=tls`) | DNS, TCP, then the TLS handshake: the certificate is verified and its expiry shown (port 5061 unless the URI gives one) |
| UDP (also when no transport is given) | DNS, then one SIP OPTIONS request |

* Exit codes: `0` reachable; `1` the URI itself is invalid; `3` unreachable, or `unknown` (a UDP host that didn't answer the OPTIONS request).
* No INVITE is ever sent, so no call is placed. Quote a URI that contains `;`, or the shell cuts the command there.
* Hosted platforms often ignore SIP from addresses they don't know, so `unknown` on UDP doesn't mean calls will fail.
* A host given without a port that publishes a SIP service (SRV) DNS record gets a warning naming the record's target; the test still checks the host you gave.
* Each step waits up to 5 seconds, or `--timeout` when given. `-o json` returns `checks[]` (each with `name`, `status`, `detail` and `duration_ms`) and `result`.

chunks.title: Test and connect a SIP voice-agent platform
chunks.text:
```bash theme={null}
plivo sip connect plan --number +14155551234 --platform elevenlabs
```

You need to be [logged in](/docs/cli/install#log-in-with-a-browser). Both flags are required: `--number <number>`, a voice-enabled number on your account, and `--platform <name>`: `livekit`, `elevenlabs`, `retell` or `vapi`. The plan checks that the number is on this account with voice enabled, then prints the steps:

```text theme={null}
CHECK    STATUS  DETAIL
number   pass    +14155551234 is on this account
voice    pass    voice is enabled
country  info    United States
routing  info    routed to application <app_id>; step 5 takes its calls away from application <app_id> and sends them to the new inbound trunk

Steps to connect +14155551234 to elevenlabs (nothing has been changed):
  1. plivo sip uris create --name elevenlabs-in --platform elevenlabs --dry-run
  2. printf '%s' "$SIP_PASSWORD" | plivo sip credentials create --name elevenlabs-out --username <username> --password-stdin --dry-run
  3. plivo sip trunks create --name elevenlabs-in --direction inbound --platform elevenlabs --uri <uri_uuid> --dry-run
  4. plivo sip trunks create --name elevenlabs-out --direction outbound --platform elevenlabs --credential <credential_uuid> --dry-run
  5. plivo numbers update 14155551234 --trunk-id <inbound_trunk_id> --dry-run
```

After the steps it lists what to set up on the platform's side, any recommendation such as `--secure`, and a link to Plivo's guide for that platform.

* Replace placeholders before running a step. Use a SIP username of 5 to 20 letters and digits, and supply `SIP_PASSWORD` securely: 5 to 20 characters with at least one of `~!@#$%^&*()_+`.
* Preview each step, then run it without `--dry-run`. A preview creates no IDs, so use the real URI UUID from step 1 in step 3, and the real credential from step 2 in step 4.
* Step 5 changes routing immediately when you remove `--dry-run`. Save the previous application or trunk ID first so you can restore it. Then complete the platform-side steps the plan prints, including importing or assigning the number to your agent.
* With `-o json` the plan returns `checks[]`, `requests[]` and `next_actions[]`. If a check fails, the plan stops and exits non-zero; with `-o json` it prints only the error, with the checks so far under `error.context.checks`.

chunks.title: Test and connect a SIP voice-agent platform
chunks.text:
For an Indian number the plan also runs the compliance check that `plivo numbers update` runs (see [Numbers](/docs/cli/apis/numbers#compliance-when-you-buy-or-route-a-number)). A number with no know your customer (KYC) compliance attached, or with an application that isn't `accepted`, fails the `compliance` check, and the plan stops with the KYC steps in the hint. The plan also checks that the platform supports Indian numbers:

| Platform | Indian numbers |
| - | - |
| LiveKit | Supported when the LiveKit project is configured to keep calls in India (`<project>.india.sip.livekit.cloud`). The plan uses that host. |
| ElevenLabs | Supported with an ElevenLabs India deployment (`sip.rtc.in.residency.elevenlabs.io`). The plan uses that host. |
| Retell | Confirm with Retell that your deployment handles SIP traffic in India. |
| Vapi | Not supported. The plan is refused before any step is printed. |

chunks.title: Test and connect a SIP voice-agent platform
chunks.text:
Values come from Plivo's [integration guide](/docs/voice-agents/sip-trunking/integration-guides/livekit) for each platform. Flags you pass always win. A host or transport the guide doesn't list is used as given, with a warning.

| Platform | Inbound URI (`sip uris create`) | Outbound authentication | Secure trunking in the guide |
| - | - | - | - |
| LiveKit | Your project host, `<project>.sip.livekit.cloud`, passed with `--uri`; TCP | Credential | Yes |
| ElevenLabs | `sip.rtc.elevenlabs.io:5060`, TCP (TLS on 5061 with `--transport tls`) | Credential | Yes |
| Retell | `sip.retellai.com`, TCP | Credential | No |
| Vapi | `sip.vapi.ai`, UDP (EU: `sip.eu.vapi.ai`) | IP access control list | No |

```bash theme={null}
plivo sip uris create --name eleven --platform elevenlabs --dry-run
plivo sip uris create --name agent --platform livekit --uri "<project>.sip.livekit.cloud" --dry-run
plivo sip ip-acl create --name vapi --platform vapi --dry-run     # fills in Vapi's published IP addresses
```

* On `sip trunks create`, `--platform` only checks the trunk against the guide. It warns when the authentication isn't the guide's, and names the command that makes a missing URI, credential or IP list.
* Where the guide uses secure trunking (TLS for signaling, Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (SRTP) for audio), the CLI prints `recommended: --secure` but never turns it on, because **secure trunking is billed per minute**. Add `--secure` yourself if you want it, and turn it on on the platform's side too.
* Each preset records the date its values were checked against the guide. If that date is more than 90 days old, the CLI warns you to check the values against the platform's docs.
* Retell won't import a number without an outbound trunk's domain and credential, even for inbound-only use, so create the outbound trunk too.

chunks.title: Test and connect a SIP voice-agent platform
chunks.text: Once calls flow, see [Check and diagnose a call](/docs/cli/voice-agent/sip-diagnose-call) for who hung up, call quality and a plain-English explanation of any call. All SIP commands are on the [SIP trunking](/docs/cli/apis/sip) page.

chunks.title: Diagnose a call
chunks.text:
Get a plain-English explanation of what happened on any call to your voice agent (failed, cut short, or completed) and what to fix.

Find why a call failed, ended early, had one-way audio or dropped its stream. After [logging in](/docs/cli/install#log-in-with-a-browser), find the call's UUID (its unique identifier), then request an explanation:

```bash theme={null}
plivo voice calls list --limit 5                 # find the UUID
plivo voice calls diagnose "<call_uuid>"           # usually about a minute; allow 30 to 120 s
```

Replace `"<call_uuid>"` with an ID from the list. The diagnosis reports a timeline and likely causes involving your server, Plivo or the carrier. For voice agents, check the answer URL, its XML and the WebSocket connection.

A typical answer:

```text theme={null}
What happened: This inbound call was terminated because Plivo could not fetch call instructions from your answer URL.
Likely cause: The answer URL https://api.example.com/plivo/answer returned 404. The call was hung up with
              cause 7011 (Error Reaching Answer URL).
Timeline: 07:48:40.600 call received · 07:48:40.630 answer URL responded 404 · 07:48:41.016 call hung up
Suggested next step: Make sure the answer URL is deployed and returns Plivo XML with HTTP 200; every inbound call will fail until it does.
```

The hangup causes you will see most often while building a voice agent:

| Hangup cause | Meaning | Fix |
| - | - | - |
| `7011` Error reaching answer URL | Plivo could not fetch your answer URL (down, not public, tunnel closed, 4xx/5xx) | Check the URL is reachable from the internet; while developing, use [Forward calls to your voice agent](/docs/cli/voice-agent/forward-calls) |
| `8011` Invalid answer XML | The answer URL returned something that is not Plivo XML (often JSON, or an HTML error page) | Return `<Response><Stream …>` with `Content-Type: application/xml`; check with `curl -X POST "<answer_url>"` |
| `4010` End of XML instructions | Normal end; your voice agent closed the WebSocket, or the XML finished | Only a problem if the call ended earlier than you expected: check your voice agent's logs for why it closed |
| `USER_BUSY` | A busy outcome; inspect the call record and XML to identify its source | Check whether your handler deliberately rejected the call before changing it |

If the answer URL and XML are valid but the caller hears silence, test the voice agent and its audio format without a phone with [Test your voice agent](/docs/cli/voice-agent/test-websocket). For the raw record (hangup cause, source, duration) run `plivo voice calls get <call_uuid> -o json`, or `plivo open call <call_uuid>` to see the call and its Call Insights in the console. For a call over a SIP trunk, use `plivo sip calls diagnose` and `plivo sip calls insights`; see [Check and diagnose a SIP call](/docs/cli/voice-agent/sip-diagnose-call).

chunks.title: Diagnose a call
chunks.section: Read the result in a script
chunks.text:
With `-o json` (or when output is piped), `diagnose` prints one JSON result when the analysis ends:

```bash theme={null}
plivo voice calls diagnose "<call_uuid>" -o json
```

```json theme={null}
{
  "data": {
    "call_uuid": "…",
    "what_happened": "…",
    "likely_cause": "…",
    "timeline": [ { "at": "…", "event": "…", "source": "…" } ],
    "next_steps": [ "…" ],
    "hangup_cause_code": 7011,
    "hangup_source": "…",
    "confidence": "high",
    "answer": "…"
  }
}
```

| Field | What it holds |
| - | - |
| `what_happened`, `likely_cause` | The assistant's explanation, in short sentences |
| `timeline[]` | Events in order, each with `at`, `event` and `source` |
| `next_steps[]` | What to do next |
| `hangup_cause_code`, `hangup_source` | Taken from the call record, not from the assistant; `null` for a message |
| `confidence` | `high`, `medium` or `low`; `null` when the answer gives none |
| `answer` | The full prose answer |

For a message the ID field is `message_uuid` instead of `call_uuid`. `-o yaml`, `-o csv` and `--query` work on this result, for example `--query 'data.likely_cause'`. `-o jsonl` streams the assistant's raw events instead of one result.

If the analysis fails, escalates or stops early, `diagnose` exits with code `3`, so a script can tell a finished analysis from one that didn't finish. Pass `--timeout <seconds>` to put a limit on a script's wait: an analysis still running at that point ends with `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT` and exit code `3`. An unknown UUID exits `1` without using a request from your limit.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The answer is written by Plivo's AI assistant, so read the prose as an explanation; scripts should read the fields of the `-o json` result instead. `diagnose` and `plivo ask` share a limit of 5 requests per 60 seconds per account. Only calls on your own account can be diagnosed. For messages see [Diagnose a message](/docs/cli/apis/messaging#diagnose-a-message); for general questions see [Get help](/docs/cli/apis/help).

chunks.title: Forward live calls to any WebSocket
chunks.text:
Take a real inbound call on a voice agent that has no public answer URL yet (on your laptop, a staging box or a teammate's tunnel) with one command.

Route real incoming calls through a tunnel to your voice agent over its WebSocket connection while developing. First [log in](/docs/cli/install#log-in-with-a-browser), start your voice agent, and [attach a number to a dedicated test application](/docs/cli/voice-agent/connect-number). Use that number and application ID:

```bash theme={null}
plivo voice streams forward --number +14155550142 \
  --app "<app_id>" --to ws://localhost:7860/ws
```

Replace the example values, approve the routing change, then call the number from a phone. Calls use your normal Plivo billing. Keep the command running; Ctrl-C restores the saved answer URL unless you pass `--keep`.

chunks.title: Forward live calls to any WebSocket
chunks.text:
`--to` accepts a `ws://` or `wss://` URL on your laptop, a staging server or a colleague's tunnel. The tunnel runs on the CLI's machine.

`forward` saves the application's `answer_url`, starts a tunnel and local HTTP/WebSocket server, and updates the application to use that tunnel. It forwards call audio to your voice agent. On Ctrl-C or a tunnel failure, it restores the saved URL; a tunnel failure exits `3`. See the recovery behavior below for a process that is killed outright.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Every phone number attached to the application is redirected for as long as `forward` runs: the confirmation step tells you how many. Use a dedicated test application.

chunks.title: Forward live calls to any WebSocket
chunks.text:
The localhost.run tunnel needs an SSH client on `PATH` and no tunnel account. macOS and Linux commonly include SSH; install it if the CLI reports `ssh not found`. If `ngrok` is already on your `PATH` (or at `~/.plivo/bin/ngrok`) the CLI uses that instead, since a warmed-up ngrok is usually faster. `--tunnel` forces the choice: `auto` (the default) prefers ngrok when it is present and falls back to localhost.run, also when ngrok can't start; `ngrok` and `localhost.run` pin one provider.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The confirmation prompt and the `--dry-run` preview print a placeholder answer URL of the form `https://<ngrok-tunnel>/answer` whichever provider is chosen. The real tunnel URL is printed once the tunnel is up.

chunks.title: Forward live calls to any WebSocket
chunks.text:
**Usage**

```text theme={null}
plivo voice streams forward [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--app <string>` | application ID returned when you create the app; its answer URL is temporarily redirected (required) |
| `--bidirectional` | allow your voice agent to send audio back to the caller (default true) |
| `--codec <string>` | audio codec advertised to Plivo: mulaw \| l16 (default "mulaw") |
| `--insecure-skip-signature` | accept unsigned tunnel requests. Anyone with the tunnel URL can then drive your handler; leave signature checks enabled for real calls. |
| `--keep` | leave the application pointing to the tunnel on exit (advanced) |
| `--number <string>` | international number with country code, such as `+14155550142`, attached to `--app` (required) |
| `--print-payload` | dump full webhook bodies to terminal (verbose) |
| `--rate <int>` | sample rate in Hz (mulaw: 8000; l16: 8000 or 16000) (default 8000) |
| `--to <string>` | local WebSocket URL to forward call audio to, e.g. ws\://localhost:7860/ws (required) |
| `--tunnel <string>` | tunnel provider: auto \| ngrok \| localhost.run (default "auto") |
| `-y, --yes` | skip the confirmation prompt |

**Examples**

```bash theme={null}
  plivo voice streams forward \
    --number +14155550142 \
    --app "<app_id>" \
    --to ws://localhost:7860/ws
  # Don't restore answer_url on exit (advanced):
  plivo voice streams forward --number +14155550142 --app "<app_id>" --to ws://localhost:7860/ws --keep
```

`--codec` and `--rate` follow the same rules here as they do for `streams test`, and an unsupported pair is rejected before anything is redirected: see [The audio contract](/docs/cli/voice-agent/test-websocket#the-audio-contract).

Nothing is purchased, created, or deleted: the only change is one field on one application, restored on exit unless you pass `--keep`. `forward` saves the original answer URL in `~/.plivo` first. If it is killed outright (`kill -9`), the next `forward` on that application restores the real answer URL and, on macOS and Linux, stops the tunnel the killed run left behind. A second `forward` on the same application is refused while one is running.

A localhost.run or trycloudflare.com URL is not saved as the original answer URL. An ngrok URL can be saved, with a warning, because ngrok also supports fixed domains.

chunks.title: Check and diagnose a SIP call
chunks.text:
Find a call over your SIP trunk, see which side hung up, read the call quality Plivo measured, and get a plain-English explanation of what happened.

Find a SIP trunk call and inspect its result. After [logging in](/docs/cli/install#log-in-with-a-browser), list recent calls and copy a call UUID, its unique identifier:

```bash theme={null}
plivo sip calls list --limit 5
plivo sip calls insights "<call_uuid>"
```

Replace `"<call_uuid>"` with an ID from the list. SIP means Session Initiation Protocol, which controls calls between Plivo and your platform.

Once your number is connected to a voice-agent platform (see [Test and connect a platform](/docs/cli/voice-agent/connect-sip-platform)), these commands tell you what happened on any call over the trunk:

| Step | Command | What it tells you |
| - | - | - |
| 1 | `plivo sip calls list` | Finds the call and its UUID |
| 2 | `plivo sip calls get <call_uuid>` | The call record, ending with which side hung up |
| 3 | `plivo sip calls insights <call_uuid>` | Round-trip time, jitter, packet loss, post-dial delay and the quality score |
| 4 | `plivo sip calls diagnose <call_uuid>` | Plivo's AI assistant explains the call and what to fix |

chunks.title: Check and diagnose a SIP call
chunks.text:
```bash theme={null}
plivo sip calls list --since 2026-10-01
plivo sip calls list --direction inbound --hangup-source carrier --since 2026-10-14
```

`--since` and `--until` (or `--from-date` and `--to-date`) filter on when a call ended, in UTC. You can also filter by `--from-number`, `--to-number`, `--hangup-cause-code`, `--hangup-source` and `--stir-verification`. See [SIP trunking](/docs/cli/apis/sip#trunk-calls) for every flag.

chunks.title: Check and diagnose a SIP call
chunks.text:
`sip calls get` and `sip calls insights` both end with the side that ended the call:

```text theme={null}
Plivo: Normal Hangup (4000), hung up by customer (your infrastructure)
Platform's final SIP response: not available
```

| Hangup source | Means |
| - | - |
| `customer` | Your side: the voice-agent platform or your own SIP infrastructure |
| `carrier` | The phone network on the caller's or callee's side |
| `zentrunk` | Plivo's SIP trunking platform |

The platform's final SIP response always reads "not available", because no API returns it. The SIP logs in the console have it: `plivo open sip-call <call_uuid>` opens that call there.

chunks.title: Check and diagnose a SIP call
chunks.text:
```bash theme={null}
plivo sip calls insights "<call_uuid>"
```

| Field | What it holds |
| - | - |
| `rtt` | Round-trip time, in ms |
| `jitter` | Variation in packet arrival, in ms |
| `packet_loss` | Share of audio packets lost, in % |
| `post_dial_delay` | Time from dialling to ringing, in ms |
| `plivo_quality_score` | Plivo's score from 1 to 5. A value outside that range is labelled as such. |
| `from.carrier`, `from.region`, `to.carrier`, `to.region` | The carrier and region of each side of the call |

These field paths are relative to `data` in JSON output. Values are printed as the API returns them; the CLI does not calculate new quality scores. For example, use `--query 'data.from.carrier'` to select the originating carrier.

chunks.title: Check and diagnose a SIP call
chunks.text:
```bash theme={null}
plivo sip calls diagnose "<call_uuid>"      # usually about a minute
```

`diagnose` reads the trunk call and explains what happened, the likely cause and the next steps. It works on SIP trunk calls only; for a Voice API call use `plivo voice calls diagnose`.

With `-o json` it prints one result with `what_happened`, `likely_cause`, `timeline`, `next_steps`, `hangup_cause_code`, `hangup_source`, `confidence` and `answer`. It exits `3` if the analysis fails or stops early. The fields are described on [Diagnose a call](/docs/cli/voice-agent/diagnose-call#read-the-result-in-a-script).

> [!NOTE]
>
> `diagnose` and `plivo ask` share a limit of 5 requests per 60 seconds per account. Only calls on your own account can be diagnosed.

chunks.title: Test your voice agent
chunks.text:
Check your WebSocket connection, your answer URL and your number before a real call: none of these checks places a call.

Test your WebSocket connection without placing a phone call. For a voice agent listening locally on port 7860:

```bash theme={null}
plivo voice streams test --to ws://localhost:7860/ws
```

A WebSocket is a persistent connection that carries audio frames between Plivo and your voice agent. Three checks run from your machine, place no call and don't change your Plivo account:

* `plivo voice streams test`: your WebSocket endpoint, with Plivo-shaped audio frames.
* `plivo voice streams simulate`: your answer URL and its XML, as Plivo requests them, then the WebSocket in its `<Stream>`. It still requests your own webhook, so your server runs its normal handler.
* `plivo voice streams readiness`: a number, or a caller ID for an outbound call, is ready for a streamed call. Then it simulates the call.

chunks.title: Test your voice agent
chunks.text:
`plivo voice streams test [flags]` opens a WebSocket to your server and sends synthetic frames in Plivo's format: one `start` frame, a `media` frame every 20 ms for `--duration` seconds, then one `stop` frame. It reports connection latency, frames sent and, with `--bidirectional`, whether your server sent audio back and how fast. Plivo's backend is not involved, so you can run it in continuous integration (CI).

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--bidirectional` | also read frames back from the endpoint (test the agent-to-caller path) |
| `--codec <string>` | audio codec: mulaw \| l16 (default "mulaw") |
| `--duration <int>` | seconds of synthetic audio to stream (max 30) (default 3) |
| `--expect-audio` | exit 1 unless playAudio comes back (implies --bidirectional); the test audio is a tone, not speech, so only an echo-style agent or one that speaks first answers |
| `--insecure` | skip TLS verification (self-signed dev certs only) |
| `--rate <int>` | sample rate in Hz (mulaw: 8000; l16: 8000 or 16000) (default 8000) |
| `--to <string>` | WebSocket URL of the endpoint to test (ws\:// or wss\://, required) |

```bash theme={null}
plivo voice streams test --to wss://my-agent.example.com/ws
plivo voice streams test --to wss://localhost:7860/ws --insecure   # self-signed dev cert
plivo voice streams test --to wss://my-agent.example.com/ws --bidirectional
plivo voice streams test --to ws://localhost:8765/ws --expect-audio -o json   # exit 1 unless playAudio comes back: gates a CI job
```

* The input is a 1 kHz tone, not speech. If no `playAudio` returns, an agent that waits for speech may stay silent even when it works on real calls.
* A `wss://` URL that reaches a server without TLS fails with a hint to use `ws://` for a local server.
* On normal completion the test sends `stop` before closing. A failed write ends it with exit code `3`, and so does an endpoint that closes the stream before `stop`; the error gives the frame it closed at and the close code and reason.

chunks.title: Test your voice agent
chunks.section: Test a WebSocket endpoint › Signed like a real stream
chunks.text: When you are logged in, the test signs the WebSocket upgrade as Plivo signs a stream, with `X-Plivo-Signature-V3` keyed with your profile's auth token, so an endpoint that checks Plivo's signature lets it in. `--profile` signs for another account; logged out, the upgrade is unsigned. An endpoint that refuses the upgrade with 401 or 403 fails the test with `AUTH_FORBIDDEN` and exit code `2`.

chunks.title: Test your voice agent
chunks.section: Test a WebSocket endpoint › Read the result in a script or CI
chunks.text:
With `-o json`, the test prints one result on stdout and its progress on stderr. `--expect-audio` makes it exit `1` when no `playAudio` comes back, so it can gate a CI job.

| Field | What it holds |
| - | - |
| `connected`, `handshake_sent` | Whether the WebSocket opened and the `start` frame went out |
| `latency_ms` | Time to open the WebSocket connection |
| `frames_sent` | Audio frames sent |
| `frames_read_back` | Frames your server sent back (with `--bidirectional`) |
| `play_audio_frames` | `playAudio` frames that carried audio |
| `first_response_ms` | Time from the first frame sent to the first `playAudio` back; `null` when none came |
| `signed` | Whether the upgrade carried Plivo's signature |
| `warnings[]` | Anything unusual the test noticed |

chunks.title: Test your voice agent
chunks.section: Simulate a call to your answer URL
chunks.text:
`voice streams simulate` does what Plivo does when a call reaches your answer URL, without placing a call. Requires Plivo CLI v1.3.2 or later.

1. It requests `--answer-url` with the fields Plivo sends (`CallUUID`, `From`, `To`, `Direction`, `CallStatus`), signed with `X-Plivo-Signature-V3` when you are logged in.
2. It checks the reply: a 2xx within Plivo's 15 seconds, its content type, and Plivo XML with a `<Stream>`.
3. It opens the WebSocket in the `<Stream>` and streams a tone in its `contentType`, as `voice streams test` does.

```bash theme={null}
plivo voice streams simulate --answer-url https://agent.example.com/answer
plivo voice streams simulate --answer-url https://agent.example.com/answer --xml-only
plivo voice streams simulate --answer-url https://agent.example.com/answer --answer-method GET --to +14155551234 -o json
```

```text theme={null}
Simulated call <call_uuid>: POST https://agent.example.com/answer (signed)
CHECK              STATUS  DETAIL
answer_url         pass    HTTP 200 in 42 ms
content_type       pass    application/xml
xml                pass    <Response> with Stream
stream             pass    wss://agent.example.com/ws
statusCallbackUrl  warn    not set: nothing tells you when a stream drops (DroppedStream)
websocket          pass    connected in 35 ms; 150 frames sent, 150 back (150 playAudio); first playAudio after 20 ms

result: pass
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--answer-url <string>` | the answer URL to request, as Plivo would (required) |
| `--answer-method <string>` | GET\|POST, as set on the application (default "POST") |
| `--direction <string>` | inbound\|outbound, sent as Direction (default "inbound") |
| `--from <string>` | the caller, sent as From (default "+14155551234") |
| `--to <string>` | the number called, sent as To (default "+14155555678") |
| `--xml-only` | stop after the answer URL and its XML: open no WebSocket |
| `--duration`, `--expect-audio`, `--insecure` | as on `voice streams test`; `--expect-audio` fails the simulation unless playAudio comes back |

* Only the answer document is read: no `<Redirect>` or action URL is followed. A Plivo-hosted answer URL, such as a flow built in the console, is refused with nothing sent, because a request there would run it for real.
* A pass means your server answers your machine as Plivo needs. It doesn't prove that Plivo can reach your server, or that a caller hears the audio.
* Exit codes: `0` on a pass, `1` when a check fails, `2` when the WebSocket refuses the upgrade, `3` when a host can't be reached or the WebSocket closes before the `stop` frame.
* With `-o json` it prints `checks[]` and the stream summary under `stream`, with the same fields as `voice streams test`. When a check fails it prints only the error, with `checks[]` in `error.context`.

chunks.title: Test your voice agent
chunks.section: Check a number is ready for a call
chunks.text:
`voice streams readiness` checks what a streamed call needs on your account, then simulates the call as `voice streams simulate` does. It places no call and changes nothing. Requires Plivo CLI v1.3.2 or later.

**Inbound:** give the number.

```bash theme={null}
plivo voice streams readiness +14155551234
plivo voice streams readiness +14155551234 --xml-only -o json
```

It checks that the number is on your account with voice enabled, that an Indian (+91) number has an accepted compliance application, and that the number is routed to an application with an answer URL, then simulates the call with the application's method. A missing fallback answer URL or hangup URL, and a development tunnel, are warnings. A host Plivo can't reach, such as your own machine or a private address, fails.

```text theme={null}
CHECK                STATUS  DETAIL
number               pass    +14155551234 is on this account
voice                pass    voice is enabled
country              info    no country-specific check applies to United States
application          pass    routed to application "my-agent"
fallback_answer_url  warn    not set: when the answer URL fails, the call ends with 7011 instead of trying another URL
hangup_url           pass    https://agent.example.com/hangup
```

The simulated call's checks and `result: ready` follow.

**Outbound:** give the caller ID, the number to call and the answer URL.

```bash theme={null}
plivo voice streams readiness --from +14155551234 --to +14155555678 \
  --answer-url https://agent.example.com/answer --answer-method POST
```

```text theme={null}
CHECK            STATUS  DETAIL
caller_id        pass    +14155551234 is a number on this account
voice            pass    voice is enabled
country          info    no country-specific check applies to +14155551234
geo_permissions  info    not checked, as no API reports them: Voice > Geo Permissions in the console, https://cx.plivo.com/geo-permissions/voice
balance          pass    cash_credits is above 0
concurrency      info    not checked, as no API reports the concurrent call limit: Organization settings > Account limits in the console, https://cx.plivo.com/organization-settings/limits
```

The caller ID must be a number on your account with voice enabled, or a verified caller ID. An Indian caller ID needs an accepted compliance application and can call only Indian numbers. The account needs cash credits. Geo permissions and the concurrent call limit have no API, so info lines say where to check them in the console. The simulated call follows, as for inbound.

| Readiness option | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `[number]` | Inbound: your rented number. Uses the application's answer URL and method. |
| `--from <number>` | Outbound: your caller ID. Use with `--to` and `--answer-url`. |
| `--to <number>` | Outbound: the destination number. |
| `--answer-url <url>` | Outbound: your public answer URL. |
| `--answer-method <method>` | Outbound: `GET` or `POST`; default `GET`. `voice calls make` uses POST for a custom answer URL and GET for its built-in demo, so pass `--answer-method POST` to both when your handler expects POST. |
| `--xml-only`, `--duration`, `--expect-audio`, `--insecure` | As on `simulate`. |

| `result` | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `ready` | Every check passed, and so did the simulated call |
| `not_ready` | A check failed. The command exits `1` |
| `unknown` | Nothing failed, but a check could not be made or the call was not simulated. The command can exit `0`; inspect `result` as well as the exit code. |

* A Plivo-hosted answer URL, such as a flow built in the console, is not requested in either direction: the result is `unknown`. `--dry-run` makes the account reads but sends nothing to the answer URL.
* With `-o json` it prints `checks[]` and the simulation. When a check fails it prints only the error, with both in `error.context`.

chunks.title: Test your voice agent
chunks.text:
The XML attribute and the WebSocket frame spell the audio format differently, which is easy to get wrong. `<Stream>` has one combined `contentType` attribute holding the codec and sample rate. There is no `sampleRate` attribute on `<Stream>`.

```xml theme={null}
<Response>
  <Stream bidirectional="true" contentType="audio/x-mulaw;rate=8000">wss://your-agent.example.com/ws</Stream>
</Response>
```

The WebSocket `start` frame spells them out separately, under `mediaFormat`:

```json theme={null}
{"event":"start","start":{"streamId":"...","callId":"...","accountId":"...",
  "mediaFormat":{"encoding":"audio/x-mulaw","sampleRate":8000,"channels":1}}}
```

A codec defines how audio samples are encoded; the sample rate is samples per second, in hertz (Hz). The l16 media type is `audio/x-l16`, not `audio/l16`. Exactly three combinations are supported:

| `contentType` | `--codec` | `--rate` | Bytes per 20 ms frame |
| - | - | - | - |
| `audio/x-mulaw;rate=8000` | `mulaw` | `8000` | 160 |
| `audio/x-l16;rate=8000` | `l16` | `8000` | 320 |
| `audio/x-l16;rate=16000` | `l16` | `16000` | 640 |

There is no mu-law 16 kHz stream. Any other pair is rejected before the connection opens, with `BAD_FLAG` and exit code 1, so a bad combination fails on your laptop instead of as a dropped stream mid-call. `--codec l16` sends real little-endian 16-bit pulse-code modulation (PCM) audio, so an agent that decodes the payload sees a genuine waveform.

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.text:
Common questions about managing your Plivo account, subaccounts, and settings

Frequently asked questions about Plivo account setup, credentials, security, team management, and subaccounts.

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.section: How do I create a Plivo account?
chunks.text:
1. Go to [Plivo signup](https://cx.plivo.com/signup)
2. Enter your name, work email, and set a password
3. Verify your email via activation link
4. Verify your phone number

**Requirements:**

* Work email address — personal (e.g., @gmail.com, @yahoo.com) and disposable email domains are not accepted
* Valid phone number for verification
* No VPN during onboarding

> [!NOTE]
>
> Plivo validates email domains during signup. If validation fails, signup will not proceed.

To send voice or messaging traffic to countries beyond the US and India, a minimum spend agreement is required. See [Plivo Pricing](https://www.plivo.com/pricing/) for details.

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.text:
During signup, you select a **Data Region** that determines which phone numbers and services you can access.

| Data Region | Can Access | Payment Method |
| - | - | - |
| **United States** | Phone numbers in [supported countries](https://www.plivo.com/virtual-phone-numbers/coverage/), international calling | International credit/debit cards or USD Bank Transfer — **cards issued in India are not accepted** |
| **India** | Indian phone numbers only, calling within India | Indian credit/debit cards only — **cards issued outside India are not accepted** |

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Data region cannot be changed after account creation.** Card origin and data region must match:
>
> * **Card issued in India →** choose the **India** data region. US data region accounts cannot be charged with India-issued cards.
> * **Card issued outside India →** choose the **US** data region. India data region accounts cannot be charged with international cards.
>
> If you need both Indian numbers and international calling, you'll need separate accounts for each region.

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.section: What is Data Region? › When to choose India
chunks.text:
* Your business is registered in India
* You only need Indian phone numbers
* You're making calls within India

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.section: What is Data Region? › When to choose United States
chunks.text:
* You need phone numbers outside India
* You need to make international calls
* You're operating globally

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.section: What happens if my signup is delayed?
chunks.text: Plivo verifies all signups to ensure compliance with telecommunications regulations. Accounts may be placed on hold if risk assessment indicates concerns. Contact [Plivo Support](https://support.plivo.com) if delayed.

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.section: Why can't I create an account with my email?
chunks.text:
Plivo requires a **business domain email address** for account registration.

| Email Type | Accepted? | Example |
| - | - | - |
| Business domain | ✅ Yes | [john@yourcompany.com](mailto:john@yourcompany.com) |
| Personal email | ❌ No | [john@gmail.com](mailto:john@gmail.com), [john@yahoo.com](mailto:john@yahoo.com) |
| Temporary email | ❌ No | [john@tempmail.com](mailto:john@tempmail.com) |

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.section: I can't log in to my account. What should I do? › Troubleshooting steps
chunks.text:
| Issue | Solution |
| - | - |
| **Forgot password** | Click "Forgot password" on login page, check email (including spam) |
| **Password reset link expired** | Request a new reset link (links expire after 24 hours) |
| **2FA code not working** | Ensure device time is synced; try recovery codes |
| **Locked out of 2FA** | Contact [Plivo Support](https://support.plivo.com) with account verification |
| **Account suspended** | Check email for suspension notice; contact support |
| **Browser issues** | Clear cache/cookies, try incognito mode, or different browser |

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.section: I can't log in to my account. What should I do? › If password reset emails aren't arriving
chunks.text:
1. Check spam/junk folder
2. Verify you're using the correct email address
3. Add `noreply@plivo.com` to your contacts
4. Wait 5-10 minutes (email delivery can be delayed)
5. Try requesting another reset

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.section: I can't log in to my account. What should I do? › If you've lost access to 2FA
chunks.text:
1. Try using **recovery codes** (saved during 2FA setup)
2. If no recovery codes, contact [Plivo Support](https://support.plivo.com) with:
   * Account email address
   * Auth ID (if known)
   * Business verification documents

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Security verification required:** For security, Plivo requires identity verification before disabling 2FA on an account. This process may take 1-2 business days.

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.section: Why is my account disabled or suspended?
chunks.text:
Your account may be disabled for several reasons:

| Reason | Solution |
| - | - |
| **Policy violation** | Check email for violation notice, contact support |
| **Suspicious activity** | Verify identity with support |
| **Fraudulent usage detected** | Contact support with business verification |
| **AUP violation** | Review Acceptable Use Policy, contact support |
| **Inactivity** | Contact support to reactivate |

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.section: Why is my account disabled or suspended? › To reactivate a disabled account
chunks.text:
1. Check your email for any notices from Plivo
2. Log in to Console (if possible) and review any alerts
3. Contact [Plivo Support](https://support.plivo.com) with:
   * Your account email
   * Auth ID (if known)
   * Business verification documents (if requested)

> [!NOTE]
>
> Reactivation may require identity verification and can take 1-3 business days depending on the reason for suspension.

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.section: How do I close or delete my account?
chunks.text:
To close (or delete) your account, go to the [Organization settings](https://cx.plivo.com/profile/organization) page (**Profile > Organization**) and click **Delete Organization**.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Closing your account is **irreversible**. Once closed, you will no longer be able to log in, and no request to restore the account or its data will be entertained.

**After closure:**

* All applications, phone numbers, endpoints, and logs are permanently deleted
* Remaining credits are refunded within 20 business days (only recharges from the last 90 days)
* Trial credits are not refunded
* Team members lose access immediately

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.section: What are Auth ID and Auth Token?
chunks.text:
| Credential | Description |
| - | - |
| **Auth ID** | Your unique account identifier (username) — cannot be changed |
| **Auth Token** | Your API password — can be changed |

Find them at the top of the [Plivo Console](https://cx.plivo.com/home) home page.

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.section: How do I regenerate my Auth Token?
chunks.text:
1. Go to [Auth Settings](https://cx.plivo.com/profile/auth) in the Plivo console
2. Click **Generate Auth Token**
3. Select when to expire the old token:
   * **Delete immediately** — old token stops working right away
   * **Delete in 48 hours** — gives you time to update your applications
4. Type `delete auth token` to confirm

> [!WARNING]
>
> Only one Auth Token can be active at a time. After the old token expires, any application still using it will fail to authenticate. Update all integrations with the new token and test before the old token expires.

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.text:
Yes. 2FA is mandatory for all Plivo accounts.

**Available methods:**

* Phone OTP (SMS/Voice)
* Authenticator apps (Google Authenticator, 1Password, Microsoft Authenticator, Authy)
* Recovery codes

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.section: How do I set up an authenticator app for 2FA?
chunks.text:
1. Go to **Account > Settings > Security > Two-Factor Authentication**
2. Click **Add** next to Authenticator App
3. Verify with OTP sent to your phone
4. Scan the QR code with your authenticator app
5. Enter the generated code to confirm

chunks.title: Account Management
chunks.section: How do I change my phone number for 2FA?
chunks.text:
1. Navigate to **Account > Settings > Security > Two-Factor Authentication**
2. Click the 3-dot menu next to Phone Verification
3. Select **Change Number**
