chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text:
Subaccounts let you link numbers to isolate traffic across departments, customers, or use cases. Each subaccount has its own Auth ID and Token; charges deduct from the main account.

See [Subaccount API](/docs/account/api/subaccount) for details.

chunks.title: Overview
chunks.text:
A Plivo Application is assigned to numbers to define how incoming calls and messages are handled using XML instructions.

See [Application API](/docs/account/api/application) and [Voice XML](/docs/voice/xml/overview) for details.

chunks.title: Account Phone Numbers API
chunks.text:
Manage phone numbers in your Plivo account

Manage phone numbers that you've rented from Plivo or added from your carrier. List, retrieve, update, and unrent numbers.

**API Endpoint**

```bash theme={null}
https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Number/
```

chunks.title: Account Phone Numbers API
chunks.text:
**number** `string`

The phone number.

**alias** `string`

Alias for the phone number.

**subaccount** `string`

Associated subaccount (null if main account).

**added_on** `string`

Date rented. Format: `YYYY-MM-DD`.

**application** `string`

Linked application URI.

**carrier** `string`

Plivo or incoming carrier name.

**region** `string`

City and country.

**number_type** `string`

Number type. Values: `local`, `fixed`, `tollfree`, `mobile`, `national`.

**monthly_rental_rate** `string`

Monthly fee (USD).

**renewal_date** `string`

Next billing date. Format: `YYYY-MM-DD`.

**sms_enabled** `boolean`

Can receive SMS.

**sms_rate** `string`

Cost per SMS (USD).

**mms_enabled** `boolean`

Can receive MMS.

**mms_rate** `string`

Cost per MMS (USD).

**voice_enabled** `boolean`

Can receive calls.

**voice_rate** `string`

Cost per minute (USD).

**cnam_lookup** `string`

CNAM lookup status. Values: `enabled`, `disabled`, `null`.

**cnam** `string`

Caller ID name for outbound calls.

**tendlc_registration_status** `string`

10DLC status. Values: `UNREGISTERED`, `PROCESSING`, `COMPLETED`.

**tendlc_campaign_id** `string`

Linked 10DLC campaign ID.

**toll_free_sms_verification** `string`

TF SMS verification. Values: `UNVERIFIED`, `PENDING_VERIFICATION`, `VERIFIED`.

**profile_uuid** `string`

UUID of the linked business profile. `null` if no profile is linked.

**caller_reputation_status** `string`

Merged Caller Reputation status for the number across carrier networks. Values: `PENDING`, `ACTIVE`, `FAILED`, `NOT_REGISTERED`, `null`. Read `caller_reputation_by_carrier` for each network's real status.

**caller_reputation_by_carrier** `object`

Per-carrier Caller Reputation status for the number, keyed by carrier network: `at&t` and `t-mobile`, plus `verizon` when it was explicitly requested (reported as `NOT_SUPPORTED`). Each entry contains `status`, `reason_code`, `reason`, and `updated_at`. See [Status values](/docs/voice/concepts/caller-reputation#status-values).

**resource_uri** `string`

URI to the number resource.

chunks.title: Account Phone Numbers API
chunks.text:
Change the application, subaccount, or alias for a phone number.

```bash theme={null}
POST https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Number/{number}/
```

chunks.title: Account Phone Numbers API
chunks.section: Update an Account Phone Number › Arguments
chunks.text:
**app_id** `string`

Application to assign (or Zentrunk inbound trunk_id).

**subaccount** `string`

Subaccount auth_id to transfer number to.

* **Number linked to a compliance application filed for a subaccount:** it can't move to another subaccount or back to your main account. To change the owner, [unrent it](#unrent-a-number) and buy it again for the new owner. Unrenting can't be undone.
* **Exception, number still pending activation:** you can move it if the same request also passes a `compliance_application_id` filed for the destination subaccount or for your main account.

**alias** `string`

Alias for the number.

**compliance_application_id** `string`

UUID of an `accepted` compliance application to link to this number. The application must match the number's country and type. It must be filed for your main account or for the subaccount the number belongs to after this update. This parameter only takes effect while the number is **pending activation** — for numbers that are already active, use the [Bulk Link endpoint](/docs/numbers/compliance#bulk-link) instead. See the [Compliance API](/docs/numbers/compliance) for details.

**cnam_lookup** `string`

CNAM lookup. Values: `enabled`, `disabled`. US only.

**cnam** `string`

Caller ID name for outbound calls.

**cnam_callback_url** `string`

URL for CNAM registration updates.

**cnam_callback_method** `string`

HTTP method. Values: `GET`, `POST`. Default: `POST`.

**caller_reputation** `string`

Enable or disable Caller Reputation for this number. Values: `enabled`, `disabled`. When set to `enabled`, `profile_uuid` is required and the profile must have a registered business with at least one carrier network approved — the number attaches on every approved network, and the response reports each network's status. If no network is approved, the request returns a `400`. US local and toll-free numbers only. Early access beta. See [Caller Reputation](/docs/voice/concepts/caller-reputation) for the full flow.

**profile_uuid** `string`

UUID of the business profile to associate with this number. Required when `caller_reputation` is set to `enabled`.

**caller_reputation_callback_url** `string` *deprecated*

**Deprecated.** Set `url` on the profile instead — see [Status callbacks](/docs/voice/concepts/caller-reputation#status-callbacks). Plivo accepts this parameter during the migration period and ignores it after.

**caller_reputation_callback_method** `string` *deprecated*

**Deprecated.** Set `method` on the profile instead. Plivo accepts this parameter during the migration period and ignores it after.

chunks.section: Update an Account Phone Number › Example

```javascript Node.js theme={null}
    .then(response => console.log(response));
```

```ruby Ruby theme={null}
require 'plivo'

client = Plivo::RestClient.new('<auth_id>', '<auth_token>')

response = client.numbers.update('17609915566', alias: 'Main Line')
```

```bash cURL theme={null}
curl -X POST "https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Number/17609915566/" \

```

chunks.title: Account Phone Numbers API
chunks.section: Update an Account Phone Number › Response

chunks.title: Account Phone Numbers API
chunks.section: Update an Account Phone Number › Compliance Errors
chunks.text:
An update that changes `subaccount` or passes `compliance_application_id` can return these errors, each with `400 bad request`:

| Condition | Error message |
| - | - |
| Moving a number linked to a subaccount's application to another owner | `Number 912212345678 is linked to compliance application xxx, which was filed for its sub-account. Keep the number on that sub-account, or release it and rent it again for the new one.` |
| The `compliance_application_id` passed was filed for a different subaccount | `Compliance application xxx was filed for another sub-account. Use one filed for this number's sub-account, or one of the account's own.` |
| The number's linked application could not be checked (retry) | `Could not verify the compliance application linked to number 912212345678. Please try again.` |

To release a number, [unrent it](#unrent-a-number). See [India Number KYC](/docs/numbers/rent-india-numbers#using-the-api-with-subaccounts) for how compliance applications filed for subaccounts work.

chunks.title: API Overview
chunks.text:
Authentication, request format, responses, and pagination for Plivo APIs

All Plivo APIs use HTTP verbs and standard HTTP status codes. To secure requests, all APIs are served over HTTPS.

**API Endpoint**

```
https://api.plivo.com/v1/
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> The current version of the APIs is `v1`. Server SDKs are versioned as `latest` and `legacy`.

chunks.title: API Overview
API Overview
chunks.text:
Plivo only accepts input of type `application/json`.

* **POST requests**: Arguments must be passed as JSON with `Content-Type: application/json`
* **GET and DELETE requests**: Arguments must be passed in the query string

chunks.title: API Overview
API Overview
chunks.text:
Plivo uses offset-based pagination to list resources.

| Parameter | Description |
| - | - |
| `limit` | Number of results to return. Range: 1-20. Default: 20. |
| `offset` | Number of results to skip for pagination. |

For example, with 100 results, `limit=10` and `offset=50` returns objects 51-60.

chunks.title: API Overview
chunks.text:
All Plivo API requests can be made asynchronous. When an async call is made, Plivo returns a generic response with the `api_id`, and the actual response is sent to your callback URL.

| Parameter | Description |
| - | - |
| `callback_url` | URL to receive the API response. |
| `callback_method` | HTTP method for the callback. Default: `POST`. |

```json Async Response theme={null}
{
  "message": "async api spawned",
  "api_id": "63f0761a-e0ed-11e1-8ea7-12313924e3a6"
}
```

chunks.title: API Overview
chunks.text:
| Code | Description |
| - | - |
| `200` | Request executed successfully |
| `201` | Resource created |
| `202` | Resource changed |
| `204` | Resource deleted |
| `400` | Parameter missing or invalid |
| `401` | Authentication failed |
| `404` | Resource not found |
| `405` | HTTP method not allowed |
| `429` | Too many requests (rate limited) |
| `500` | Server error |

chunks.title: API Overview
CNAM Lookup
chunks.text:
Learn about CNAM (Caller ID Name) lookup for US phone numbers on Plivo.

> [!NOTE]
>
> * **What:** Display a caller's registered name on inbound US calls by querying the US LIDB.
> * **When:** Enable per number when you want caller-name display. It's US inbound only and billed per lookup.

CNAM (Caller ID Name) is a feature in the US public telephone network that associates phone numbers with registered names. When someone receives a call, their carrier queries the Line Information Database (LIDB) and displays the caller's registered name.

chunks.title: CNAM Lookup
chunks.text:
CNAM lookup on Plivo works for:

* Inbound Voice API calls on US phone numbers
* Inbound Zentrunk (SIP trunking) calls on US phone numbers

> [!NOTE]
>
> CNAM is only available for US numbers and inbound calls only.

chunks.title: CNAM Lookup
chunks.text:
1. Caller dials your Plivo US number
2. Plivo queries the LIDB for the caller's registered name
3. CNAM data is included in the call callback payload
4. Your application can display or use the caller name

chunks.title: CNAM Lookup
chunks.section: Configure CNAM settings › Set account-level default
chunks.text:
1. Navigate to **Phone Numbers > Settings**
2. Enable or disable CNAM lookup as the default
3. This setting applies to numbers rented after the change

chunks.title: CNAM Lookup
chunks.section: Configure CNAM settings › Configure during number purchase
chunks.text:
1. Go to **Phone Numbers > Buy Numbers**
2. Search for US numbers
3. During purchase, select CNAM lookup configuration
4. If you skip configuration, the account default applies

chunks.title: CNAM Lookup
chunks.section: Configure CNAM settings › Update CNAM on existing numbers
chunks.text:
**Single number:**

1. Go to **Phone Numbers > Active**
2. Click on the US phone number
3. Update CNAM lookup setting
4. Save

**Multiple numbers:**

1. Go to **Phone Numbers > Active**
2. Select numbers using checkboxes
3. Click **Choose Action > Update CNAM**
4. Apply changes

chunks.title: CNAM Lookup
chunks.text:
1. Navigate to **Phone Numbers > Active**
2. View CNAM lookup status column for US numbers
3. Use filters to show only CNAM-enabled or disabled numbers

chunks.title: CNAM Lookup
chunks.text:
Use the `cnam_lookup` parameter of the [Account Phone Numbers API](/docs/numbers/account-phone-numbers):

```
GET /v1/Account/{auth_id}/Number/{number}/
```

Response includes:

```json theme={null}
{
  "number": "14151234567",
  "cnam_lookup": true
}
```

chunks.title: CNAM Lookup
chunks.section: View CNAM status › Filter numbers by CNAM status
chunks.text:
Use the `cnam_lookup` parameter in the [List Account Phone Numbers API](/docs/numbers/account-phone-numbers#list-all-numbers):

```
GET /v1/Account/{auth_id}/Number/?cnam_lookup=true
```

chunks.title: CNAM Lookup
chunks.text:
When CNAM lookup is enabled, inbound call callbacks include:

| Parameter | Description |
| - | - |
| `cnam_lookup_result` | The caller's registered name (if found) |

> [!NOTE]
>
> CNAM data may not be available for all callers. Mobile numbers and some VoIP services may not have CNAM records.

chunks.title: CNAM Lookup
chunks.text:
CNAM lookup is charged **per inbound call** when enabled on a number.

* Charged regardless of whether a name is found
* See [Voice Pricing](https://cx.plivo.com/billing/plans-and-pricing) for current rates

chunks.title: CNAM Lookup
chunks.text:
Enable CNAM selectively on numbers where caller identification provides business value:

* Customer service lines
* Sales hotlines
* Support numbers

chunks.title: CNAM Lookup
chunks.section: When to enable CNAM › Managing costs
chunks.text:
* Disable CNAM on high-volume numbers if caller name isn't needed
* Monitor CNAM charges in your monthly invoice
* Use account-level defaults to control costs

chunks.title: CNAM Lookup
chunks.text:
Your application should gracefully handle cases where:

* CNAM lookup returns no result
* Caller has no registered name
* Database timeout occurs

chunks.title: CNAM Lookup
chunks.text:
| Limitation | Details |
| - | - |
| US only | CNAM lookup is only available for US phone numbers |
| Inbound only | Only works for incoming calls, not outbound |
| Database coverage | Not all phone numbers have CNAM records |
| Accuracy | CNAM data may be outdated or incorrect |

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.text:
Manage phone number compliance with requirements discovery and document submission

The Compliance API lets you manage phone number regulatory compliance in a single streamlined flow. Instead of creating end users, documents, and compliance applications separately, you can do it all in one API call.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Supported Countries:** The Compliance API currently supports India only. Support for additional countries will be added in future releases.

**API Endpoint**

```bash theme={null}
https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/PhoneNumber/Compliance/
```

**Authentication:** HTTP Basic Auth with your Plivo Auth ID as username and Auth Token as password.

**Subaccounts:** To file an application for one of your subaccounts, use your main account credentials and set `subaccount` in the [`data` JSON](#create). [Get](#get) and [List](#list) take the same parameter as a filter.

Every response includes an `api_id` field for request tracing.

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.text: Describes what documents and fields are needed for compliance in a specific country, number type, and user type combination. Always call this first before creating a compliance application.

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.text:
**requirement_id** `string`

UUID of the compliance requirement.

**country_iso** `string`

ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

**number_type** `string`

Type of number. Values: `local`, `mobile`, `tollfree`.

**user_type** `string`

Type of end user. Values: `individual`, `business`.

**document_types** `array`

List of required document types. Each object includes `document_type_id`, `name`, `description`, `proof_required`, and `required_fields`.

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.section: The Requirements Object › Document Type Object
chunks.text:
Each entry in `document_types`:

**document_type_id** `string`

UUID of the document type. Use this when creating a compliance application.

**name** `string`

Document type name (e.g., "Registration Certificate").

**description** `string`

Description of the document type.

**proof_required** `boolean`

`true` = file upload required, `false` = only data fields needed.

**required_fields** `array`

Data fields required for this document type.

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.section: The Requirements Object › Required Field Object
chunks.text:
Each entry in `required_fields`:

**field_name** `string`

Key to use in `documents[].data_fields`.

**friendly_name** `string`

Human-readable display name.

**help_text** `string`

Guidance on what to enter.

**field_type** `string`

Values: `string`, `date`, `enum`.

**required** `boolean`

Whether this field is mandatory.

**format** `string`

Expected format (e.g., `yyyy-mm-dd`). Empty if none.

**enums** `string`

Comma-separated allowed values for enum fields. Empty for other types.

**min_length** `integer`

Minimum character length.

**max_length** `integer`

Maximum character length.

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.text:
Query compliance requirements before creating a compliance record.

```bash theme={null}
GET https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/PhoneNumber/Compliance/Requirements
```

#### Query Parameters

**country_iso** `string` *required*

Two-letter country code (e.g., `IN`).

**number_type** `string` *required*

Values: `local`, `mobile`, `tollfree`.

**user_type** `string` *required*

#### Example

```bash cURL theme={null}
curl "https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/PhoneNumber/Compliance/Requirements?country_iso=IN&number_type=local&user_type=business" \
  -u '<auth_id>:<auth_token>'
```

#### Response (200 OK)

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.text: Represents a compliance application combining end user information and documents for regulatory review.

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.text:
**compliance_id** `string`

UUID identifier.

**alias** `string`

Friendly name for the compliance record.

**status** `string`

Current status. Values: `draft`, `submitted`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `suspended`, `expired`.

**country_iso** `string`

ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

**number_type** `string`

Type of number.

**user_type** `string`

Values: `individual`, `business`.

**subaccount** `string`

Auth ID of the subaccount this application was filed for. Not returned for applications filed for your main account, or if the subaccount has since been deleted.

**callback_url** `string`

Webhook URL for status change notifications. Present only if configured.

**callback_method** `string`

HTTP method for the callback. Values: `GET`, `POST`. Present only if configured.

**rejection_reason** `string|null`

Reason for rejection. Present only when `status` is `rejected`.

**created_at** `string`

ISO 8601 timestamp.

**updated_at** `string`

ISO 8601 timestamp.

**end_user** `object|null`

End user details (only returned with `expand=end_user`).

**documents** `array|null`

Attached documents (only returned with `expand=documents`).

**linked_numbers** `array|null`

Linked phone numbers (only returned with `expand=linked_numbers`).

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.section: The Compliance Object › End User Object
chunks.text:
Returned when using `expand=end_user`.

**end_user_id** `string`

UUID of the end user.

**type** `string`

Values: `individual`, `business`.

**name** `string`

Full name or company name.

**last_name** `string`

Last name (empty for business).

Contact email.

**address_line1** `string`

Street address line 1.

**address_line2** `string`

Street address line 2.

**city** `string`

City.

**state** `string`

State or province.

Postal or ZIP code.

Two-letter country code.

Business registration number (e.g., CIN for India).

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.text:
Returned when using `expand=documents`.

**document_id** `string`

UUID of the document.

UUID of the document type.

**document_name** `string`

Document type name.

**file_name** `string`

Original filename (empty if no file uploaded).

**meta_information** `object`

Key-value pairs submitted with the document.

**download_url** `string`

Presigned S3 URL (expires in 1 hour). Empty if no file.

**created_at** `string`

ISO 8601 timestamp.

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.section: The Compliance Object › Linked Number Object
chunks.text:
Returned when using `expand=linked_numbers`.

Phone number in E.164 format.

**number_type** `string`

Type of number.

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.text:
Create end user, upload documents, and auto-submit the compliance application in a single call.

```bash theme={null}
POST https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/PhoneNumber/Compliance/
```

**Content-Type:** `multipart/form-data`

The request consists of:

* A `data` field containing a JSON string with compliance details
* File fields using the pattern `documents[0].file`, `documents[1].file`, etc.

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.section: Create a Compliance Application › File Upload Rules
chunks.text:
* Required when the document type has `proof_required=true` (from Requirements response)
* Not needed when `proof_required=false`
* Supported formats: PDF, JPEG, PNG (validated server-side by content type, not just extension)
* Max file size: 5 MB per file
* Max filename length: 99 characters

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.section: Create a Compliance Application › The `data` JSON Structure
chunks.text:
**country_iso** `string` *required*

Two-letter country code.

**number_type** `string` *required*

Values: `local`, `mobile`, `tollfree`.

**alias** `string` *required*

Friendly name (unique per end user, max 99 characters).

**end_user** `object` *required*

End user details.

**documents** `array` *required*

Array of document objects.

**callback_url** `string`

HTTPS URL to receive status change notifications (accepted, rejected). Plivo sends a v3 signature in the request header for verification.

**callback_method** `string`

HTTP method for the callback. Values: `GET`, `POST`. Default: `POST`. Requires `callback_url` to be set.

**subaccount** `string`

Auth ID of one of your subaccounts. Files the application, and its end user, for that subaccount instead of your main account. Use your main account credentials. If omitted, the application is filed for your main account.

**end_user fields:**

**end_user.type** `string` *required*

Values: `individual`, `business`.

**end_user.name** `string` *required*

Full name or company name.

**end_user.last_name** `string`

Last name.

**end_user.email** `string`

Contact email.

**end_user.address_line1** `string`

Street address line 1.

**end_user.address_line2** `string`

Street address line 2.

**end_user.city** `string`

City.

**end_user.state** `string`

State or province.

**end_user.postal_code** `string`

Postal or ZIP code.

**end_user.country** `string`

Two-letter country code.

**end_user.registration_number** `string`

Business registration number.

**documents[] fields:**

**documents[].document_type_id** `string` *required*

UUID from the Requirements response.

**documents[].data_fields** `object`

Key-value pairs matching `required_fields[].field_name` from Requirements.

chunks.title: Compliance
Compliance
chunks.section: Create a Compliance Application › Response (201 Created)

chunks.title: Compliance
Compliance
chunks.section: Get a Compliance Application › Query Parameters
chunks.text:
**expand** `string`

Comma-separated list of objects to include. Values: `end_user`, `documents`, `linked_numbers`.

Without `expand`, only top-level fields are returned (faster response). With `expand`, the corresponding nested objects are included.

**subaccount** `string`

Auth ID of a subaccount. Use your main account credentials.

* **A subaccount's Auth ID:** returns the application only if it was filed for that subaccount; otherwise returns `404`.
* **Empty value (`subaccount=`):** returns the application only if it was filed for your main account.

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.text:
Returns a paginated list of compliance applications for the account.

```bash theme={null}
GET https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/PhoneNumber/Compliance/
```

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.text:
**limit** `integer`

Max results per page (max 100). Default: 20.

**offset** `integer`

Pagination offset. Default: 0.

**status** `string`

Filter by status. Values: `draft`, `submitted`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `suspended`, `expired`.

Filter by country code (e.g., `IN`).

Filter by number type. Values: `local`, `mobile`, `tollfree`.

Comma-separated: `end_user`, `documents`, `linked_numbers`.

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.text:

chunks.title: Compliance
Compliance
Compliance
chunks.text:
* Only applications with `status=rejected` can be updated. Any other status returns error code `compliance_not_editable`.
* `end_user.type` cannot be changed.
* `subaccount` cannot be changed. Leave it out, or pass the value the application already has.
* **Documents are fully replaced.** All previously uploaded documents are removed and new ones are created. You must re-upload all documents, not just the ones that need correction.

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.text:
**alias** `string`

**end_user** `object`

Partial end user update (same fields as Create, minus `type`).

**documents** `array`

**callback_url** `string`

Updated webhook URL (HTTPS only).

**callback_method** `string`

Updated HTTP method. Values: `GET`, `POST`.

chunks.title: Compliance

chunks.section: Update a Compliance Application › Response (200 OK)
chunks.text:
Returns the updated compliance object with `status: "submitted"` (auto-resubmitted for review).

```json theme={null}
{
  "api_id": "ef28ebe6-31a5-11f1-bf86-d2d6f5435dea",
  "message": "Compliance application updated and resubmitted for review.",
  "compliance": {
    "compliance_id": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",

    "updated_at": "2026-04-03T14:00:00Z"
```

chunks.title: Compliance
Compliance
chunks.text:
* Applications with `status=expired` cannot be deleted.
* All other statuses (`submitted`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `suspended`) can be deleted.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Deleting an `accepted` application that has linked numbers will unlink those numbers. Ensure numbers are re-linked to a different compliance application if needed.

chunks.title: Compliance

* Compliance application must be in `accepted` status

Status flow

If an application is **rejected**, update it (`PATCH`) to fix the flagged details — this auto-resubmits it for review. | Status | Description | Available Actions | | - | - | - | | `draft` | Saved but not yet submitted | Get, List, Delete | | `submitted` | Under review by the compliance team | Get, List, Delete | | `accepted` | Approved — phone numbers can be linked | Get, List, Delete, Bulk Link | | `rejected` | Not accepted — check `rejection_reason` | Get, List, Delete, Update (auto-resubmits) | | `suspended` | Suspended by the compliance team | Get, List, Delete | | `expired` | No longer valid — create a new application | Get, List |

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.text:
All error responses use a flat two-field format with `api_id` for request tracing and `error` containing an actionable message. This is consistent with the standard Plivo API error pattern.

```json theme={null}
{
  "api_id": "a407c522-31a7-11f1-ab48-d2d6f5435dea",
  "error": "country_iso is required. Use a two-letter ISO country code (e.g., IN, DE, US)."
}
```

**api_id** `string`

Unique request identifier for tracing.

**error** `string`

Human-readable, actionable error message.

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.text:
| Scenario | Error message |
| - | - |
| Missing required field | `country_iso is required. Use a two-letter ISO country code (e.g., IN, DE, US).` |
| Application not found | `Compliance application 'xxx' not found.` |
| Wrong status for update | `Compliance application must be in 'rejected' status. Current status: 'submitted'.` |
| Expired application delete | `Expired compliance applications cannot be deleted.` |
| Invalid expand value | `Invalid expand value. Allowed values: end_user, documents, linked_numbers.` |
| Number not on account | `Number not found on your account. Only rented numbers can be linked.` |
| Application not accepted for linking | `Compliance application must be in 'accepted' status. Current status: 'submitted'.` |
| Subaccount not found, or not one of yours (`404`) | `There is no subaccount with auth_id <subaccount_auth_id>` |
| `subaccount` is your main account's own Auth ID (Create, `400`) | `There is no subaccount with auth_id <auth_id>` |
| Subaccount could not be verified | `Something went wrong while verifying the subaccount. Please try again later. If the issue persists, contact support@plivo.com.` |
| Changing `subaccount` on Update | `subaccount cannot be changed on a compliance application.` |
| Bulk Link: application filed for another subaccount (in `remarks`) | `Compliance application xxx was filed for another sub-account. Use one filed for this number's sub-account, or one of the account's own.` |
| Server error while checking the subaccount (Get) | `Something went wrong while fetching the compliance application. Please try again later. If the issue persists, contact support@plivo.com.` |
| Server error while checking the subaccount (List) | `Something went wrong while listing compliance applications. Please try again later. If the issue persists, contact support@plivo.com.` |
| Server error | `Something went wrong while processing the request. Please try again later. If the issue persists, contact support@plivo.com.` |

chunks.title: Compliance
chunks.text:
When you provide a `callback_url` during creation or update, Plivo sends a webhook notification when the compliance application status changes (for example, from `submitted` to `accepted` or `rejected`).

* **Method:** Uses the `callback_method` you specified (`GET` or `POST`, default `POST`).
* **Signature:** Plivo includes a v3 signature in the request header for verification. Use [Plivo's signature validation](/docs/voice/concepts/signature-validation/) to verify the callback is authentic.
* **HTTPS required:** The `callback_url` must use HTTPS.
* **No subaccount in the payload:** Callbacks don't include `subaccount`. To route callbacks per customer, set a different `callback_url` on each subaccount's application when you create it.

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.text:
Learn how to port phone numbers to and from Plivo, including timelines, requirements, and troubleshooting.

> [!NOTE]
>
> * **What:** Transfer phone numbers to Plivo (port-in) or away from Plivo (port-out) while keeping the same number.
> * **When:** Available for US and Canada numbers only; the process takes up to 4 weeks.

Porting transfers a phone number from one service provider to another. Number porting lets you retain the same phone number while switching service providers, avoiding service interruptions and maintaining your existing user base.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Number porting is available for **US and Canada only**. Port-in is free of charge.

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.text:
| Number Type | Timeline |
| - | - |
| Local numbers | Up to 4 weeks |
| Toll-free numbers | Similar timeline |
| Project porting (100+ numbers) | May take longer; requires numbers from same carrier account |

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.section: What numbers can be ported to Plivo?
chunks.text:
* Local numbers (US and Canada)
* Toll-free numbers (US and Canada)

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.text:
You must have a Plivo Standard account to initiate a port-in request. See [Account Management FAQ](/docs/faq/account/account-management) for account requirements. Before you send the porting request, make sure you have the following documents:

| Document | Description | Required |
| - | - | - |
| **Letter of Authorization (LOA)** | Signed by the authorized user/owner of the number(s). Use our [LOA template](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6565737286e587567248583f/686fba5cfad3ae244a7aeb39_Plivo-LOA-Template.docx). | Mandatory for toll-free; optional for fixed numbers |
| **PIN** | Depending on coverage, may be required for US numbers. Include if you have one. | Optional |
| **Recent Invoice** | Copy of your most recent phone bill (within 30-60 days) showing account name, authorized username, and billing details. | Optional but recommended |

> [!WARNING]
>
> The name and address on your LOA must match exactly what your current carrier has on file. Contact your carrier to verify this information or request a Customer Service Record (CSR).

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.section: How to port your phone number to Plivo › Overview of the process
chunks.text:
1. Submit porting request documentation to Plivo
2. Plivo submits the porting request to the gaining carrier
3. The gaining carrier submits the porting request to the losing carrier
4. The losing carrier approves or rejects the request
5. If approved, Plivo notifies you of the Firm Order Commitment (FOC), or porting date
6. On the FOC date, Plivo activates the number, tests all capabilities, and notifies you that the process is complete

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.section: How to port your phone number to Plivo › Submit your port request
chunks.text:
1. Log in to the Plivo console and go to **Phone Numbers > Port-In > [New Port-In Order](https://cx.plivo.com/phone-numbers)**
2. Fill in your business details on the **User Details** screen, then click **Continue**

![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/7-odxN9fJG_Dg1dt/images/screenshot-2024-02-22-at-7-07-07-pm.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=7-odxN9fJG_Dg1dt&q=85&s=d62a4815a849553650502b0832cc655d)

3. On the **Port-In Details** screen:
   * Select the phone number type
   * Select your preferred port-in date (at least 2 business days away)
   * Add the numbers you want to port in
   * Enter the current carrier's account number and PIN (if applicable)
   * Click **Continue**

![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/7-odxN9fJG_Dg1dt/images/screenshot-2024-02-22-at-7-06-25-pm.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=7-odxN9fJG_Dg1dt&q=85&s=fec8e082c1c1ecedabf0306a140a0ea8)

4. On the **Numbers Configure** screen:
   * Select capabilities (Voice or Voice + SMS)
   * Enter an alias for identification
   * Select a subaccount (optional)
   * Enter a CNAM for caller ID branding (optional)
   * Select the [XML](/docs/voice/xml/overview), , or Zentrunk application to associate with the numbers

![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/7-odxN9fJG_Dg1dt/images/screenshot-2024-02-22-at-7-05-32-pm.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=7-odxN9fJG_Dg1dt&q=85&s=fdb7b3d4d39c9c32ae8ffd7b6ddbe458)

5. Upload supporting documents (LOA, invoice) and click **Submit**

![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/7-odxN9fJG_Dg1dt/images/screenshot-2024-02-22-at-7-04-19-pm.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=7-odxN9fJG_Dg1dt&q=85&s=fbece4a237dfbc11f98cc78e3d8a55a7)

> [!NOTE]
>
> Don't close your account with your old carrier until the porting process is complete. Keep your numbers active to avoid downtime.

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.text:
| Status | Description | Action |
| - | - | - |
| Submitted | Request received | Wait for carrier processing |
| Approved | Carrier accepted | Wait for FOC date |
| Completed | Successfully ported | Number is active on Plivo |
| Rejected | Request denied | Review rejection reason, resubmit |
| Update Required | Information needs correction | Plivo will contact you |

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.text:
If all details and documents are acceptable, Plivo submits the porting request to the gaining carrier. This takes about a day.

The gaining carrier verifies the request and forwards it to the losing carrier. The request shows as pending while the losing carrier processes it (5-20 business days).

Once processed, you'll receive a status update:

* **Approved**: Plivo receives a Firm Order Commitment (FOC) with the porting date
* **Update Required**: Plivo contacts you to re-submit corrected information
* **Rejected**: Plivo explains the rejection so you can resubmit with correct details

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.text:
Plivo sends you an email with your porting date and adds the numbers to your account two days before the FOC.

Have your application set up and ready before the FOC date to avoid service interruption. You can configure numbers at **Phone Numbers > Port-In > Configure Number**.

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.section: Handling rejected requests › Common rejection reasons
chunks.text:
| Reason | Solution |
| - | - |
| **Data mismatch** | Update LOA to match carrier records exactly |
| **Name mismatch** | Verify name with current carrier |
| **Address mismatch** | Use address from carrier's CSR |
| **Unsatisfactory business relationship** | Pay outstanding balance to current carrier |
| **Number not portable** | Contact Plivo support |

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.section: Handling rejected requests › How to fix and resubmit
chunks.text:
1. Review the rejection reason in the console or email
2. Correct the issue (usually LOA information mismatch)
3. Submit a new port request with corrected information

For more details on rejection reasons, see [this guide](https://support.plivo.com/hc/en-us/articles/360041880011).

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.section: Handling rejected requests › Escalating port-in issues
chunks.text:
If your port request is stuck or you're experiencing issues that require carrier intervention:

1. **Contact Plivo Support** at [support.plivo.com](https://support.plivo.com) with:
   * Your port request ID
   * Phone number(s) affected
   * Description of the issue
   * Any error messages received

2. **Plivo's porting team** will:
   * Review your request status with the carrier
   * Escalate to the carrier's porting department if needed
   * Provide updates on resolution timeline

> [!NOTE]
>
> Plivo cannot directly contact carriers on your behalf for account-specific issues (like outstanding balances). You may need to resolve these with your current carrier before resubmitting.

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.text:
Before carrier acceptance:

1. Navigate to Port-In orders in console
2. Select the order
3. Click **Cancel**

No cancellation fee applies before carrier acceptance.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Plivo cannot expedite the porting process as it involves multiple carriers. You can request your current carrier to release the number, which may help speed things up.

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.text:
To transfer numbers from Plivo to another carrier:

1. Contact your new carrier and submit a port-in request with your Plivo number(s)
2. New carrier validates and submits port-out request to Plivo's carriers
3. Plivo emails you to confirm the request
4. You authorize or stop the transfer
5. Number transfers on the FOC date

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.section: Porting numbers out of Plivo › How to stop or delay a port-out
chunks.text:
If you receive a port-out notification and want to stop or delay it:

**To stop a port-out:**

1. Reply to the port-out confirmation email from Plivo
2. Clearly state you want to **reject** the port-out request
3. Include the phone number(s) and reason for rejection

**To delay a port-out:**

1. Contact [Plivo Support](https://support.plivo.com) immediately
2. Provide:
   * Phone number(s) involved
   * Current FOC (porting) date
   * Requested new completion date
   * Reason for delay
3. Plivo will work with the gaining carrier to reschedule

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Time-sensitive:** Port-out stop/delay requests must be submitted **before the FOC date**. Once the FOC date passes, the port-out cannot be reversed.

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.section: Porting numbers out of Plivo › After port-out
chunks.text:
* Number loses service with Plivo on FOC date
* Number is removed from your Plivo account
* If you don't respond to the confirmation email, Plivo automatically processes the port-out

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.text:
If a number was ported away without your authorization, contact [Plivo Support](https://support.plivo.com) immediately with:

* Affected phone number(s)
* Reason for dispute
* Signed and dated LOA from the end user confirming intent to retain service

chunks.title: Number Porting
chunks.text:
* Disputes must be filed within **30 days**
* Plivo works with carriers to retrieve the number
* Resolution time varies by carrier

chunks.title: Phone Numbers API
chunks.text:
Search and buy phone numbers from Plivo's inventory

Search for and purchase phone numbers from Plivo. You can search for local, toll-free, national, mobile, and fixed phone numbers that match specific criteria.

**API Endpoint**

```bash theme={null}
https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/PhoneNumber/
```

chunks.title: Phone Numbers API
chunks.text:
**number** `string`

Phone number that can be purchased.

**prefix** `string`

Area code of the number.

**city** `string`

City of the number. Returns `null` for national numbers.

**country** `string`

Country of the number.

**region** `string`

City and country of the number.

**rate_center** `string`

Rate center. US and Canada only.

**lata** `string`

Local access and transport area. US and Canada only.

**type** `string`

Number type. Values: `fixed`, `mobile`, or `tollfree`.

**sub_type** `string`

Number subtype. Values: `fixed`, `mobile`, `tollfree`, `national`, or `local`.

**setup_rate** `string`

One-time setup fee in USD.

**monthly_rental_rate** `string`

Monthly rental fee in USD.

**sms_enabled** `boolean`

Whether the number can receive SMS.

**sms_rate** `string`

Cost per SMS received in USD.

**mms_enabled** `boolean`

Whether the number can receive MMS.

**mms_rate** `string`

Cost per MMS received in USD.

**voice_enabled** `boolean`

Whether the number can receive calls.

**voice_rate** `string`

Cost per minute for calls in USD.

**restriction** `string`

Verification requirement. Values: `city-address`, `country-address`, `terms-and-conditions`, or `null`.

**restriction_text** `string`

Description of verification requirements.

**resource_uri** `string`

URI to the phone number resource.

chunks.text:
Returns available phone numbers matching your criteria.

```bash theme={null}
GET https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/PhoneNumber/
```

chunks.title: Phone Numbers API
chunks.text:
**country_iso** `string` *required*

[ISO 3166 alpha-2 country code](https://www.iban.com/country-codes) of the country.

**type** `string`

Number type filter. Values: `tollfree`, `local`, `mobile`, `national`, or `fixed`.

**pattern** `string`

Pattern to match. For example, `415` returns numbers starting with 1415.

**npanxx** `integer`

Six-digit prefix filter. US and Canada only.

**local_calling_area** `boolean`

Expand search to local calling area of `npanxx`.

**region** `string`

Region name (e.g., `Frankfurt`). For `fixed` type only.

**city** `string`

City name. For `local` type only.

**services** `string`

Filter by capabilities. Values: `voice`, `sms`, `mms`, `voice,sms`, or `voice,sms,mms`.

**lata** `integer`

LATA filter. US and Canada only.

**rate_center** `string`

Rate center filter. US and Canada only.

**limit** `integer`

Results per page. Maximum 20, default 20.

**offset** `integer`

Pagination offset. Default 0.

chunks.title: Phone Numbers API
chunks.text:
Purchase a phone number and add it to your account.

```bash theme={null}
POST https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/PhoneNumber/{number}/
```

chunks.title: Phone Numbers API
chunks.text:
**app_id** `string`

Application to assign. Defaults to `default_number_app`.

**cnam_lookup** `string`

Enable CNAM lookup. Values: `enabled` or `disabled`. US only.

**compliance_application_id** `string`

UUID of an `accepted` compliance application to attach to the number at purchase. The application's country and number type must match the number. If the application was filed for a subaccount, buy the number for that subaccount (pass `subaccount`). See the [Compliance API](/docs/numbers/compliance).

If you omit it, Plivo auto-selects the most recent accepted application that matches the number's country and type:

* **With `subaccount`:** one filed for that subaccount first, then one of your main account's.
* **Without `subaccount`:** one of your main account's.

Plivo never auto-selects an application filed for a different subaccount.

**subaccount** `string`

Auth ID of a subaccount to assign the number to at purchase. Requires main-account credentials (see note below).

> [!NOTE]
>
> If the number requires verification documents, the number status will be `pending` until documents are approved.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Call this endpoint with **main-account credentials**. Phone numbers are billed and owned at the main-account level, so a request made with subaccount credentials returns `404 not found` even when [Search](#search-phone-numbers) works with the same credentials. To buy a number for a subaccount, call this endpoint with main-account credentials and pass the `subaccount` parameter. To move an already-rented number to a subaccount, use the [Update an Account Phone Number](/docs/numbers/account-phone-numbers#update-an-account-phone-number) endpoint's `subaccount` parameter. A number linked to a compliance application filed for a subaccount stays on that subaccount; see the `subaccount` parameter there.

chunks.title: Phone Numbers API

chunks.section: Buy a Phone Number › Compliance Errors
chunks.text:
Renting a number that requires compliance, such as an India number, needs a compliance application in `accepted` status. Requests that don't meet this condition return `400 bad request`:

| Condition | Error message |
| - | - |
| No `compliance_application_id` passed and no accepted application Plivo can auto-select for this purchase (see `compliance_application_id` above) | `compliance_application_id is required to rent this number. Refer to https://www.plivo.com/docs/numbers/rent-india-numbers for details.` |
| The `compliance_application_id` passed is not in `accepted` status | `Compliance application must be in 'accepted' status. Current status: 'submitted'.` |
| The `compliance_application_id` passed was filed for a subaccount other than the one the number is bought for | `Compliance application xxx was filed for another sub-account. Use one filed for this number's sub-account, or one of the account's own.` |

See [India Number KYC](/docs/numbers/rent-india-numbers#application-status) for how to resolve each application status.

chunks.title: India Number KYC
chunks.text:
KYC documents, compliance application process, and number rental for India

> [!NOTE]
>
> * **What:** KYC process for renting Indian numbers — India data region accounts only.
> * **You must:** Submit one valid business document: GST Certificate, COI, or Udyam Registration.
> * **If you don't:** The application is rejected.

KYC compliance is required before renting Indian phone numbers. This guide covers the documents, application process, and post-approval steps.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **India Data Region Required:** Indian phone numbers are only available to India data region organizations. If your organization is in the US data region, you cannot rent Indian numbers. Data region cannot be changed after an organization is created — create a new organization with the India data region from the organization switcher in the [Plivo Console](https://cx.plivo.com/home) (no new signup needed).

chunks.title: India Number KYC
chunks.text:
Submit any **one** of the following documents:

| Document | Issued by | Must include |
| - | - | - |
| **GST Certificate** (Goods and Services Tax registration certificate) | GST Network (GSTN) | An active GSTIN |
| **Certificate of Incorporation (COI)** | Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) | The Corporate Identification Number (CIN) |
| **Udyam Registration Certificate** | Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) | A valid Udyam Registration Number |

Plivo verifies the document against government records, so upload a current copy downloaded from the issuing portal. Business PAN alone is not accepted.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Your first compliance application must be sealed and signed.** The document must be signed by an authorized signatory and carry a visible company seal. Plivo uses this first application to fetch your billing address and GST details (if provided). You can update these details later by submitting relevant proofs on the [Organization Settings](https://cx.plivo.com/organization-settings/general) page in the Plivo console.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Common rejection reasons:**
>
> * The registration is cancelled, suspended, or inactive in government records
> * The document details don't match government records — download the latest copy from the GST, MCA, or Udyam portal and resubmit
> * The document is expired
> * The document isn't one of the three accepted types (for example, business PAN alone)
> * The upload is blurry, cropped, or incomplete
> * The first application isn't sealed and signed

chunks.title: India Number KYC
chunks.text:
1. Navigate to [**Phone Numbers > KYC**](https://cx.plivo.com/phone-numbers/compliance)
2. Click **New Application**
3. Select **India** and click **Continue**
4. Upload any one of: GST Certificate, Certificate of Incorporation, or Udyam Registration Certificate (sealed and signed if this is your first application)
5. Select business type (Direct Brand or Reseller)
6. Submit

For 080/022 numbers, review is automated — you receive an acceptance or rejection typically within 5 minutes. 140-series and 160-series numbers have a separate SLA — see [140-series provisioning](/docs/voice/concepts/140-series-provisioning) and [160-series provisioning](/docs/voice/concepts/160-series-provisioning).

To submit by API, including for a customer's subaccount, use the [Compliance API](/docs/numbers/compliance#create). Resellers, see [Using the API with subaccounts](#using-the-api-with-subaccounts).

chunks.title: India Number KYC
chunks.text:
| Type | Definition | Compliance Requirement |
| - | - | - |
| **Direct Brand** | Place calls for your own business | One compliance application |
| **Reseller** | Offer communication services to others | Separate application per customer |

chunks.title: India Number KYC
chunks.text:
Renting an India number and placing calls from an India number both require a compliance application in `accepted` status (shown as **Approved** in the Console). If an API error directed you to this page, find your application under [**Phone Numbers > KYC**](https://cx.plivo.com/phone-numbers/compliance) and follow the next steps for its status:

| Status | Meaning | Next Steps |
| - | - | - |
| Draft | Application started but not submitted | Complete and submit |
| Pending Approval | Submitted and under review | Wait for review (080/022: typically 5 minutes; 140-series and 160-series: separate SLA) |
| Approved | KYC verified | Rent numbers and place calls |
| Rejected | Documents need correction | Check the rejection email, fix the documents, and resubmit |
| Expired | Application is no longer valid | Create and submit a new application, then attach it to your numbers ([update compliance](#update-compliance-on-existing-numbers)) |
| Suspended | Blocked due to unresolved [UCC complaints](/docs/voice/concepts/ucc-management) | Submit required consent proof to resolve |

If your number has **no compliance application attached**, [submit an application](#submit-compliance-application) and attach it to the number ([update compliance](#update-compliance-on-existing-numbers)).

When an application filed for a subaccount is accepted, only that subaccount's pending numbers are activated. Accepting a main-account application activates pending numbers across your account, except numbers linked to a subaccount's application.

chunks.title: India Number KYC
chunks.text:
| Number Type | Who Can Use It | Permitted Use |
| - | - | - |
| **Landline series** (e.g., 022, 080) | Non-BFSI businesses | Service and transactional calls |
| **140 series** | Any business making promotional calls in India | Promotional voice calls only — additional setup required ([setup guide](/docs/voice/concepts/140-series-provisioning)) |
| **160 series** | BFSI businesses only | Service and transactional calls — additional setup required ([setup guide](/docs/voice/concepts/160-series-provisioning)) |

chunks.title: India Number KYC
chunks.section: Rent Numbers After Approval › Direct Brands
chunks.text:
1. Go to **Buy Number**
2. Select India
3. In the **KYC** step, pick an approved compliance application. If you have exactly one, it is selected for you. It links to the number when you buy it.

chunks.title: India Number KYC
chunks.text:
1. Ensure your customer's compliance application is approved in [**Phone Numbers > KYC**](https://cx.plivo.com/phone-numbers/compliance) 2. In the **KYC** step, pick your customer's application. The list also shows applications filed for your subaccounts, each tagged with the subaccount's name. Picking one buys the number on that subaccount, and **Sub Account** is locked to it in the **Configuration** step. Applications of disabled subaccounts can't be picked. 3. Application must be approved beforehand Your own (untagged) application works as before: pick any subaccount under **Sub Account**, and the number moves there after the purchase. #### Using the API with subaccounts
  1. Create SubaccountOne per customer
  2. Submit ApplicationFor that subaccountAccepted
  3. Buy NumbersFor that subaccount
1. [Create a subaccount](/docs/account/api/subaccount#create-a-subaccount) for each customer. 2. Submit the customer's compliance application with the [Compliance API](/docs/numbers/compliance#create). Set `subaccount` inside the `data` JSON to that subaccount's Auth ID, and use your main account credentials. 3. Once it is accepted, [buy numbers](/docs/numbers/phone-numbers#buy-a-phone-number) with `subaccount` set to the same Auth ID. Pass the application's `compliance_id` from the Create response as `compliance_application_id`. Each customer's KYC stays with their subaccount: it can back only that subaccount's numbers.

chunks.title: India Number KYC
chunks.text:
Use this when a number is transferred between customers or the business entity using the number changes.

**Option 1:**

1. Go to **Active Numbers**
2. Select numbers
3. Click **Choose Action > Update Compliance**
4. Select compliance application
5. Click **Save**

**Option 2:**

1. Click on specific number
2. Select compliance from dropdown

> [!NOTE]
>
> An application filed for a subaccount can be attached only to that subaccount's numbers. A number linked to such an application can't move to another subaccount or back to your main account. To give it to a different customer, [unrent it](/docs/numbers/account-phone-numbers#unrent-a-number) and buy it again for that customer's subaccount. Unrenting can't be undone.

chunks.title: India Number KYC
chunks.section: Frequently Asked Questions › Why do calls to my India landline number fail unless I dial 0 or +91 first?
chunks.text:
India landline numbers — the 022, 080, and other city series — consist of an STD (area) code plus a subscriber number. Under India's National Numbering Plan, the `0` is the national trunk prefix and `+91` is the country code. Neither is part of the number itself; each one tells the network that an area code follows. Without one of them, the network can't tell that the digits belong to a landline.

| Format | Example | Result |
| - | - | - |
| **E.164** (country code, no `0`) | `+918012345678` | Works from any network, in India or abroad. Use this format in every Plivo API request. |
| **National** (trunk prefix `0`, no `+91`) | `08012345678` | Works from any phone within India. |
| Neither prefix | `8012345678` | Fails. Indian mobile numbers are also 10 digits and start with 6, 7, 8, or 9, so the network reads this as a mobile number, finds no such subscriber, and rejects the call. |
| Both prefixes | `+9108012345678` | Fails. Drop the `0` when you use `+91`. |

Only a landline in the same city can dial the subscriber number on its own, because its exchange supplies the area code. A mobile handset has no local exchange to supply one, so dial the full number — with `+91` or `0` — from every mobile and every application, even from the same city.

chunks.title: India Number KYC
chunks.section: Frequently Asked Questions › Why does my call fail with "from parameter is invalid ... is not associated with your account"?
chunks.text: Calls from India numbers must originate from a number rented on your Plivo account — you can't use an arbitrary caller ID. Rent an India number (see [Rent Numbers After Approval](#rent-numbers-after-approval)) and place calls from that number.

chunks.title: India Number KYC
chunks.section: Frequently Asked Questions › Why does my call fail with "compliance application is not in 'accepted' status"?
chunks.text:
The `from` number's compliance application isn't approved yet — it's pending, submitted, rejected, expired, or no application is attached to the number. Find the application under [**Phone Numbers > KYC**](https://cx.plivo.com/phone-numbers/compliance) and follow the next steps for its status in the [Application Status](#application-status) table.

If the error says the application is `'suspended'`, the cause is unresolved UCC complaints — see [UCC Management](/docs/voice/concepts/ucc-management) for how to lift the suspension.

chunks.title: India Number KYC
chunks.section: Frequently Asked Questions › Why does renting a number fail with "compliance_application_id is required"?
chunks.text:
Plivo found no accepted compliance application it can attach automatically to this purchase. [Submit a compliance application](#submit-compliance-application), wait for approval, and retry — or pass the UUID of an accepted application in the `compliance_application_id` parameter of the [Buy a Phone Number](/docs/numbers/phone-numbers#buy-a-phone-number) request.

Which applications Plivo can attach depends on how you buy:

* **With `subaccount`:** an accepted application filed for that subaccount first, then one of your main account's.
* **Without `subaccount`:** only your main account's applications.

Plivo never attaches an application filed for a different subaccount, so this error can appear even when your other subaccounts have accepted applications.

chunks.title: India Number KYC
chunks.section: Frequently Asked Questions › Why does renting a number fail with "Compliance application must be in 'accepted' status"?
chunks.text: The application you passed in `compliance_application_id` isn't approved yet — the error shows its current status. Follow the next steps for that status in the [Application Status](#application-status) table, then retry once the application is approved.

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text:
Manage UCC complaints against your India phone numbers, submit opt-in proof, and receive events on every status change.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The UCC API lets India data region accounts manage the complaint workflow from [UCC Management](/docs/voice/concepts/ucc-management): list and retrieve complaints, submit opt-in proof, and receive an event whenever a complaint changes.

This API and the [UCC dashboard](https://cx.plivo.com/phone-numbers/ucc) act on the same records — proof submitted through either one moves the same complaint, and a verdict reached in review shows up in both. Use the API when you want complaint handling wired into your own systems instead of someone watching the Console.

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text:
```text theme={null}
https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Ucc/
```

All requests use HTTP Basic authentication with your Auth ID and Auth Token. Every response includes an `api_id` for request tracing.

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text: A UCC complaint is registered against your account when a carrier reports one of your calls. Each complaint is identified by its `reference_id` and moves through a review lifecycle: `pending` → `in_review` → `accepted` or `rejected`.

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text:
**reference_id** `string`

Unique reference ID of the complaint, in the format `PUCC-YYYY-NNNNNNNNN`. This is the same reference quoted in Plivo's complaint notification emails and on the UCC dashboard. Use this ID in all endpoint paths.

**status** `string`

Current state of the complaint. One of `pending` (no proof received yet), `in_review` (proof uploaded and under review), `accepted` (proof approved; complaint closed), or `rejected` (proof declined; see `rejection_reason` and resubmit).

**from_number** `string`

Your Plivo number that made the reported call, in E.164 format.

**to_number** `string`

The complainant's phone number, in E.164 format.

**initiation_date** `string`

Date of the reported call, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format, as reported in the carrier's complaint.

**complaint_category** `string`

Category of the complaint as reported by the carrier.

**call_uuid** `string`

Plivo Call UUID of the reported call. Use it to look up the call in your call detail records. Null when the call could not be matched.

**opt_in_proof** `string`

URL of the most recently uploaded opt-in proof. Null until the first upload.

**rejection_reason** `string`

Reason the proof was declined, in plain text. Populated only while `status` is `rejected`; null in every other state.

**created_at** `string`

Timestamp when the complaint was registered, in ISO 8601 UTC.

**updated_at** `string`

Timestamp when the complaint last changed, in ISO 8601 UTC.

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.section: The UCC Complaint Object › Example Object
chunks.text:
```json theme={null}
{
  "api_id": "aa1e6a4e-31aa-11f1-ab48-d2d6f5435dea",
  "call_uuid": "18830b47-ddda-41ba-b621-f4b4f5524264",
  "complaint_category": "Received spam call in the category: Banking/Insurance/Financial Products/Credit Card",
  "created_at": "2026-07-09T08:04:16Z",
  "from_number": "+911600123456",
  "initiation_date": "2026-07-03",
  "opt_in_proof": "https://media.example.com/ucc-proofs/PUCC-2026-990000051.pdf",
  "reference_id": "PUCC-2026-990000051",
  "rejection_reason": "The consent date is older than 6 months",
  "status": "rejected",
  "to_number": "+919876543210",
  "updated_at": "2026-07-15T09:00:13Z"
}
```

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text: Fetch a single complaint by its UCC reference ID.

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.section: Retrieve a UCC Complaint › HTTP Request
chunks.text:
`GET https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Ucc/{reference_id}/`

A `reference_id` that does not exist or belongs to another account returns a `404` error.

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text:
```bash cURL theme={null}
curl -X GET "https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Ucc/PUCC-2026-990000051/" \
  -u '<auth_id>:<auth_token>'
```

The response is the [UCC Complaint object](#the-ucc-complaint-object) shown above.

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text: Fetch complaints against your account, newest first. Use the filters to poll for open work — for example, all `rejected` complaints that need a new proof.

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text: `GET https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Ucc/`

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text:
**status** `string`

Filter by state: `pending`, `in_review`, `accepted`, or `rejected`.

**from_number** `string`

Filter by the Plivo number that made the reported call.

**created_at** `string`

Filter by complaint creation time, in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM[:ss[.uuuuuu]]` format. Supports the range variants `created_at__gt`, `created_at__gte`, `created_at__lt`, and `created_at__lte`, with the same behavior as the [List All Calls](/docs/voice/api/calls#list-all-calls) time filters.

**limit** `integer` (default: 20)

Number of results per page, from 1 to 20.

**offset** `integer` (default: 0)

Number of results to skip, for pagination.

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text:
**api_id** `string`

Unique identifier for the API request.

**meta** `object`

Pagination details: `limit`, `offset`, `total_count`, and relative `next`/`previous` page URLs (null when there is no further page).

**objects** `array`

The list of [UCC Complaint objects](#the-ucc-complaint-object) matching the filters.

```json theme={null}
{
  "api_id": "b1c2d3e4-58b6-11e1-86da-77300b68f8bb",
  "meta": {
    "limit": 20,
    "next": null,
    "offset": 0,
    "previous": null,
    "total_count": 4
  },
  "objects": [
    {
      "reference_id": "PUCC-2026-990000051",
      "status": "rejected",
      "from_number": "+911600123456",
      "to_number": "+919876543210",
      "initiation_date": "2026-07-03"
    }
  ]
}
```

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text:
```bash cURL theme={null}
curl -X GET "https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Ucc/?status=rejected&created_at__gte=2026-07-01" \
  -u '<auth_id>:<auth_token>'
```

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text: Upload an opt-in proof file against a complaint. A successful upload moves the complaint to `in_review`. Call this endpoint when a complaint is `pending`, or again after a rejection to resubmit.

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text:
`POST https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Ucc/{reference_id}/`

Send the request as `multipart/form-data`.

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text:
**file** `file` *required*

The opt-in proof document. Allowed types: PDF, PNG, and JPEG, validated by content type. Maximum size: 10 MB.

The document must show **all three** of the following, or the review declines it:

| Required element | Details |
| - | - |
| **Business logo** | The logo or identity of the business entity that made the call, so the caller's identity can be verified. |
| **Date of opt-in** | The date the recipient explicitly opted in to receive calls. Must be within 6 months before the complaint date. |
| **Complainant's phone number** | The exact number of the person who filed the complaint, confirming the opt-in was obtained for that specific number. |

> [!NOTE]
>
> The API does not validate these three elements when you upload. It checks only the file type and size, then returns `201` and moves the complaint to `in_review`. The contents are assessed later during review — a document missing any of the three is rejected, with the reason in `rejection_reason`. A successful upload is not an accepted proof.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **6-month validity window.** An opt-in acquired more than 6 months before the complaint date is not accepted. Make sure your opt-in collection system records timestamps accurately.

For the full policy, including what happens after a rejection, see [UCC Management](/docs/voice/concepts/ucc-management#1-submit-opt-in-proof).

Uploads are allowed while `status` is `pending` or `rejected`. Uploading against a complaint that is `in_review` or `accepted` returns a `400` error.

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text:
**api_id** `string`

Unique identifier for the API request.

**message** `string`

Status of the request.

**reference_id** `string`

Reference ID of the complaint the proof was submitted against.

**status** `string`

The complaint's new state: `in_review`.

**opt_in_proof** `string`

URL of the uploaded proof file.

```json theme={null}
{
  "api_id": "c407c522-31a7-11f1-ab48-d2d6f5435dea",
  "message": "proof submitted",
  "reference_id": "PUCC-2026-990000051",
  "status": "in_review",
  "opt_in_proof": "https://media.example.com/ucc-proofs/PUCC-2026-990000051.pdf"
}
```

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text:
```bash cURL theme={null}
curl -X POST "https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Ucc/PUCC-2026-990000051/" \
  -u '<auth_id>:<auth_token>' \
  -F "file=@opt-in-record.pdf"
```

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text:
Configure a callback URL on the [UCC dashboard](https://cx.plivo.com/phone-numbers/ucc) to receive an event whenever a complaint is created against your account or changes state. The URL must use HTTPS, and one URL applies to your whole account.

Plivo sends callbacks as form-encoded POST requests (`Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`), signed with the same V3 signature scheme as Voice API callbacks. Validate the signature before trusting the parameters — see [Signature Validation](/docs/voice/concepts/signature-validation).

There are four callbacks, matching the complaint lifecycle. The `Status` parameter identifies which one you received:

| `Status` | Fired when | Complaint status after |
| - | - | - |
| `created` | A new complaint is registered against your account | `pending` |
| `proof_submitted` | You upload a proof, through the API or the Console | `in_review` |
| `rejected` | Review declines the proof | `rejected` |
| `accepted` | Review approves the proof | `accepted` |

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text:
**Endpoint** `string`

Always `ucc` — identifies the resource type generating the callback.

**Status** `string`

The lifecycle event: `created`, `proof_submitted`, `rejected`, or `accepted`.

**UCCReferenceID** `string`

Reference ID of the complaint. Use it with [Retrieve a UCC Complaint](#retrieve-a-ucc-complaint) for the full record.

**FromNumber** `string`

Your Plivo number that made the reported call, in E.164 format.

**ToNumber** `string`

The complainant's phone number, in E.164 format.

**InitiationDate** `string`

Date of the reported call, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Same value as `initiation_date` on the UCC Complaint object.

**ComplaintCategory** `string`

Category of the complaint as reported by the carrier.

**CallUUID** `string`

Plivo Call UUID of the reported call. Empty when the call could not be matched.

**RejectionReason** `string`

Reason the proof was declined, in plain text. Sent only on the `rejected` callback.

**ResourceCreationTime** `string`

When the complaint was registered in Plivo's system, in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.fff +0000 UTC` format. This mirrors the object's `created_at` and is identical across all callbacks for a complaint. It is not the date of the reported call — that's `InitiationDate`.

**ResourceUpdatedTime** `string`

When this status transition fired, in `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.fff +0000 UTC` format. This mirrors the object's `updated_at` and changes with every callback.

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text:
```text theme={null}
Endpoint: ucc
Status: rejected
UCCReferenceID: PUCC-2026-990000051
FromNumber: +911600123456
ToNumber: +919876543210
InitiationDate: 2026-07-03
ComplaintCategory: Received spam call in the category: Banking/Insurance/Financial Products/Credit Card
CallUUID: 18830b47-ddda-41ba-b621-f4b4f5524264
RejectionReason: The consent date is older than 6 months
ResourceCreationTime: 2026-07-09 08:04:16.720 +0000 UTC
ResourceUpdatedTime: 2026-07-15 14:03:27.320 +0000 UTC
```

The `created`, `proof_submitted`, and `accepted` callbacks carry the same parameters without `RejectionReason`.

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text:
* Respond with an HTTP `200` within 5 seconds.
* Plivo retries failed deliveries 3 times, at 60, 120, and 240 seconds.
* Deliveries are at-least-once and unordered. Deduplicate on `UCCReferenceID` + `Status` + `ResourceUpdatedTime`, and reconcile state with [Retrieve a UCC Complaint](#retrieve-a-ucc-complaint) when in doubt.
* Callbacks are the low-latency path, not the only path. Run a daily sweep of `GET /Ucc/?status=rejected&created_at__gte=...` so a missed callback never consumes your [5-business-day response window](/docs/voice/concepts/ucc-management#what-happens-if-i-dont-submit-valid-proof).

chunks.title: UCC API
chunks.text:
| Code | Description | Solution |
| - | - | - |
| `400` | Invalid request — for example, uploading proof against an `accepted` complaint, or an unsupported file type | Check the error message; it names the parameter and the fix |
| `401` | Authentication failed | Verify your Auth ID and Auth Token |
| `404` | Complaint not found, or it belongs to another account | Check the `reference_id` |
| `429` | Rate limited | Implement exponential backoff |

Error responses use the standard Plivo format:

```json theme={null}
{
  "api_id": "97ceeb52-58b6-11e1-86da-77300b68f8bb",
  "error": "Proof cannot be submitted while the complaint is in accepted state."
}
```

chunks.text:

* [India Calling Regulations](/docs/voice/concepts/india-calling) — number series rules and TRAI requirements
