chunks.title: API Overview
chunks.text:
Authentication, request format, responses, and pagination for Plivo APIs

All Plivo APIs use HTTP verbs and standard HTTP status codes. To secure requests, all APIs are served over HTTPS.

**API Endpoint**

```
https://api.plivo.com/v1/
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> The current version of the APIs is `v1`. Server SDKs are versioned as `latest` and `legacy`.

chunks.title: API Overview
API Overview
chunks.text:
Plivo only accepts input of type `application/json`.

* **POST requests**: Arguments must be passed as JSON with `Content-Type: application/json`
* **GET and DELETE requests**: Arguments must be passed in the query string

chunks.title: API Overview
API Overview
chunks.text:
Plivo uses offset-based pagination to list resources.

| Parameter | Description |
| - | - |
| `limit` | Number of results to return. Range: 1-20. Default: 20. |
| `offset` | Number of results to skip for pagination. |

For example, with 100 results, `limit=10` and `offset=50` returns objects 51-60.

chunks.title: API Overview
chunks.text:
All Plivo API requests can be made asynchronous. When an async call is made, Plivo returns a generic response with the `api_id`, and the actual response is sent to your callback URL.

| Parameter | Description |
| - | - |
| `callback_url` | URL to receive the API response. |
| `callback_method` | HTTP method for the callback. Default: `POST`. |

```json Async Response theme={null}
{
  "message": "async api spawned",
  "api_id": "63f0761a-e0ed-11e1-8ea7-12313924e3a6"
}
```

chunks.title: API Overview
chunks.text:
| Code | Description |
| - | - |
| `200` | Request executed successfully |
| `201` | Resource created |
| `202` | Resource changed |
| `204` | Resource deleted |
| `400` | Parameter missing or invalid |
| `401` | Authentication failed |
| `404` | Resource not found |
| `405` | HTTP method not allowed |
| `429` | Too many requests (rate limited) |
| `500` | Server error |

chunks.title: API Overview
Verify Availability & Coverage
chunks.text:
How Plivo Verify is provisioned to direct brands, country coverage by Minimum Monthly Commitment (MMC) tier, and India ILDO support.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Plivo provisions Verify only to direct brands through sales, under a Minimum Monthly Commitment (MMC) — not to resellers or ISVs. Country coverage depends on your MMC tier. Unlike SMS, Verify needs no sender registration or KYC on your side.

Plivo Verify delivers OTPs for two-factor authentication over SMS and voice. This page explains eligibility requirements, available country coverage, and how coverage maps to **Minimum Monthly Commitment (MMC)** tiers.

Verify access is provisioned through our sales team. Self-service onboarding for Verify is not currently available.

[Request access →](https://www.plivo.com/contact/sales/)

chunks.title: Verify Availability & Coverage
chunks.text: Plivo Verify is available to businesses authenticating their own end users under their own brand.

chunks.title: Verify Availability & Coverage
chunks.section: Who we support › Not eligible for Verify onboarding
chunks.text:
At this time, Plivo does not onboard the following business models for Verify:

* **Resellers** that provide verification or messaging services to downstream customers.
* **Independent Software Vendors (ISVs)** sending OTPs on behalf of multiple third-party brands.
* **Aggregators or multi-tenant platforms** that consolidate traffic from multiple unrelated senders under a single account.

chunks.title: Verify Availability & Coverage
chunks.section: Who we support › Why eligibility requirements exist
chunks.text:
The global messaging ecosystem has become increasingly regulated, with carriers and regulators requiring greater transparency and accountability from message senders.

Examples include:

* **United States:** 10DLC registration, brand vetting, campaign registration, and carrier-level enforcement.
* **International markets:** Sender ID registration, brand registration, template approval, KYC requirements, and filtering of unregistered traffic in many countries.

These requirements are designed to improve message quality, reduce abuse, and ensure that messaging traffic can be traced back to the responsible sender.

Supporting direct brands allows sender registration, compliance reviews, and ongoing accountability to map directly to the organization originating the traffic.

chunks.title: Verify Availability & Coverage
chunks.section: No compliance setup on your side
chunks.text:
Verify delivers OTPs using **Plivo-registered Sender IDs**, so you do not perform sender ID registration, brand vetting, template approval, or end-user KYC yourself to start sending. This setup works globally.

Some countries may experience reduced delivery quality unless an **independent Sender ID** is registered for your brand. Independent Sender ID registration is subject to the same MMC and coverage requirements described below.

chunks.title: Verify Availability & Coverage
chunks.text:
Verify access is tied to a **Minimum Monthly Commitment (MMC)** — a monthly spend commitment across all Plivo products, **excluding any pass-through fees** such as carrier surcharges. Your MMC tier determines which destination countries are available for OTP delivery.

| MMC tier | Coverage |
| - | - |
| **USD 1,000/month** | Verify (SMS and voice) for the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Australia, and India (ILDO routes only), plus delivery to countries that do not require sender registration or pre-approval. |
| **USD 10,000/month** | Includes all coverage available in the USD 1,000 tier, plus countries that require sender registration, brand approval, template registration, or other pre-registration compliance processes before traffic can be enabled. |

chunks.title: Verify Availability & Coverage
chunks.section: Minimum Monthly Commitment (MMC) tiers › Understanding MMC
chunks.text:
The Minimum Monthly Commitment is a **monthly spend commitment across Plivo products**, excluding pass-through fees such as carrier surcharges. It is not a setup fee or connection fee. Standard per-message, per-minute, or other usage charges continue to apply.

If your total usage across products falls below the committed amount, the MMC sets the **minimum billable amount** for that month.

chunks.title: Verify Availability & Coverage
chunks.section: Minimum Monthly Commitment (MMC) tiers › Pre-registration countries
chunks.text:
A pre-registration country is a market where carriers or regulators require approval before traffic can be sent. Depending on the country, this may include:

* Brand registration
* Sender ID registration
* Message template approval
* Regulatory or operator review

Coverage for these markets is available under the **USD 10,000 MMC tier**.

> [!NOTE]
>
> To determine if a country requires pre-registration, see the [Plivo SMS Coverage page](https://www.plivo.com/sms/coverage/).

chunks.title: Verify Availability & Coverage
chunks.section: Minimum Monthly Commitment (MMC) tiers › India coverage
chunks.text:
Plivo delivers Verify traffic to India through **ILDO (International Long Distance Operator) routes**, starting at **USD 0.08 per message**.

Domestic India SMS requiring **DLT registration** is not currently available through Plivo.

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.text:
Send and validate OTPs for two-factor authentication via SMS and voice

The **Plivo Verify API** enables programmatic user authentication via **2FA** (Two-Factor Authentication) using **SMS** and **voice calls**. With just a few simple steps, you can easily integrate OTP-based verification into your applications.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Don't see Verify in your Plivo console?** Verify is not enabled by default — it's provisioned to direct brands behind a Minimum Monthly Commitment (MMC). [Read more about availability and coverage →](/docs/programmable-api/verify/availability)

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.text:
Verify is offered to **direct brands only** and requires a **Minimum Monthly Commitment (MMC)**, with country coverage that mirrors Plivo SMS: a USD 1,000/month MMC covers the US, Canada, UK, Australia, and India (ILDO), while a USD 10,000/month MMC adds pre-registration countries. Unlike SMS, Verify requires **no sender registration or KYC on your side** — Plivo delivers OTPs through its own registered Sender IDs.

See [Verify Availability & Coverage](/docs/programmable-api/verify/availability) for eligibility, MMC tiers, and India ILDO details.

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.text:
**1. Set Up an Application in Plivo Console**

To start sending OTPs, [create a Verify application](https://cx.plivo.com/verify) in the Plivo Console.

Configure these settings:

| Setting | Description |
| - | - |
| **Alias** | Friendly name for your application |
| **Brand name** | Your brand name shown in messages |
| **Code length** | Number of digits in the OTP (4-8) |
| **Expiry** | Time window before the OTP expires |
| **Attempts** | Maximum delivery attempts per session |
| **Template** | Message template (e.g., `Your ${brand} verification code is ${code}`) |
| **Android AppHash** | Hash string for automatic SMS verification on Android |

Once created, you'll receive an **Application UUID** to use in API requests.

![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/Ag15G3VhPnb9cXBm/programmable-api/verify/verifyapplication.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=Ag15G3VhPnb9cXBm&q=85&s=8dd199cc3b73d49f199ae72811a3efb6)

**2. Create a Session to Send OTPs**

Use the [Create Session API](/docs/programmable-api/verify/sessions#create-a-session) to send an OTP:

```python Python theme={null}
import plivo

client = plivo.RestClient('<auth_id>', '<auth_token>')

response = client.verify_session.create(
    recipient='<destination_number>',
    app_uuid='<verify_app_uuid>',
    channel='sms',
    url='https://your-domain.com/callback',
    method='POST'
)

print(f"Session UUID: {response.session_uuid}")
```

```javascript Node.js theme={null}
const plivo = require('plivo');

const client = new plivo.Client('<auth_id>', '<auth_token>');

client.verify_session.create({
    recipient: '<destination_number>',
    app_uuid: '<verify_app_uuid>',
    channel: 'sms',
    url: 'https://your-domain.com/callback',
    method: 'POST'
}).then(response => {
    console.log(`Session UUID: ${response.sessionUuid}`);
});
```

```ruby Ruby theme={null}
require 'plivo'

client = Plivo::RestClient.new('<auth_id>', '<auth_token>')

response = client.verify_session.create(
    recipient: '<destination_number>',
    app_uuid: '<verify_app_uuid>',
    channel: 'sms',
    url: 'https://your-domain.com/callback',
    method: 'POST'
)

puts "Session UUID: #{response.session_uuid}"
```

```bash cURL theme={null}
curl -X POST "https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Verify/Session/" \
  -u '<auth_id>:<auth_token>' \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "recipient": "<destination_number>",
    "app_uuid": "<verify_app_uuid>",
    "channel": "sms",
    "url": "https://your-domain.com/callback",
    "method": "POST"
  }'
```

Set a callback URL to receive real-time delivery status updates.

**3. Validate the OTP**

When the user enters the OTP, validate it using the [Validate Session API](/docs/programmable-api/verify/sessions#validate-a-session):

```python Python theme={null}
import plivo

client = plivo.RestClient('<auth_id>', '<auth_token>')

response = client.verify_session.validate(
    session_uuid='<session_uuid>',
    otp='<otp_code>'
)

print(f"Status: {response.message}")
```

```javascript Node.js theme={null}
const plivo = require('plivo');

const client = new plivo.Client('<auth_id>', '<auth_token>');

client.verify_session.validate({
    id: '<session_uuid>',
    otp: '<otp_code>'
}).then(response => {
    console.log(`Status: ${response}`);
});
```

```ruby Ruby theme={null}
require 'plivo'

client = Plivo::RestClient.new('<auth_id>', '<auth_token>')

response = client.verify_session.validate('<session_uuid>', '<otp_code>')

puts "Status: #{response}"
```

```bash cURL theme={null}
curl -X POST "https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Verify/Session/{session_uuid}/" \
  -u '<auth_id>:<auth_token>' \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"otp": "<otp_code>"}'
```

**4. Handle the Response**

If the OTP is valid, allow the user to proceed. If invalid, prompt them to re-enter or resend the OTP.

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.text:
The Verify API supports two delivery channels:

| Channel | When to Use |
| - | - |
| **SMS** | Default choice. Fast, familiar, works on all phones. |
| **Voice** | Users without SMS capability, accessibility needs, or as fallback when SMS fails. |

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.section: Channels: SMS vs Voice › Using Voice OTP
chunks.text:
To send OTP via voice call, set `channel` to `voice`:

```python Python theme={null}
response = client.verify_session.create(
    recipient='+14155551234',
    app_uuid='<verify_app_uuid>',
    channel='voice',  # Voice call instead of SMS
    url='https://your-domain.com/callback'
)
```

```bash cURL theme={null}
curl -X POST "https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Verify/Session/" \
  -u '<auth_id>:<auth_token>' \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "recipient": "+14155551234",
    "app_uuid": "<verify_app_uuid>",
    "channel": "voice"
  }'
```

The user receives an automated voice call that reads out their OTP code.

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.section: Channels: SMS vs Voice › Channel Fallback Strategy
chunks.text:
For critical verifications, implement fallback:

```python theme={null}
# Try SMS first
response = client.verify_session.create(
    recipient=phone,
    app_uuid=app_uuid,
    channel='sms'
)

# If SMS fails or times out, retry with voice
if response.status == 'failed':
    response = client.verify_session.create(
        recipient=phone,
        app_uuid=app_uuid,
        channel='voice'
    )
```

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.text:
A **session** represents a single verification interaction with a user. Each session can have multiple delivery attempts.

**Example:** You send an OTP at 10:00 AM with a 10-minute expiry. This creates a session that expires at 10:10 AM. All delivery attempts during this window are part of the same session and deliver the same OTP.

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.text:
1. **Created** - OTP generated and first delivery attempted
2. **In Progress** - Waiting for user to enter OTP (additional attempts possible)
3. **Verified** - User entered correct OTP
4. **Expired** - Session timed out without successful validation

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.text: Fraud Shield protects your applications from [SMS pumping](https://www.plivo.com/blog/sms-pumping/) attacks by monitoring traffic in real-time and blocking suspicious messages.

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.text:
| Level | Description |
| - | - |
| **High** | Strongest filtering, best for high-risk scenarios. May have more false positives |
| **Medium** | Balanced filtering (default). Fewer false positives |
| **Low** | Minimal filtering for apps with higher fraud tolerance |

Configure in **Console > Verify > App Settings > Fraud Shield**.

Blocked messages return **error code 452** (Potential SMS Pumping).

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.text:
1. **Skip fraud check for trusted users** - Set `check_fs=false` for known good users
2. **Create separate apps** - Use different apps for Sign Up, Sign In, and Password Reset
3. **Use a dedicated low-protection app** - For trusted user segments, create an app with Fraud Shield set to Low or Disabled

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.text: Validate that webhook requests originate from Plivo using signature verification.

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.text:
All Plivo requests include:

* `X-Plivo-Signature-V2` - Generated using account/subaccount Auth Token
* `X-Plivo-Signature-Ma-V2` - Always generated using main account Auth Token
* `X-Plivo-Signature-V2-Nonce` - Unique nonce for the request

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.text:
Calculate HMAC with:

* **Key:** Your Plivo Auth Token
* **Message:** Base URI + X-Plivo-Signature-V2-Nonce (e.g., `https://yourdomain.com/callback/05429567804466091622`)
* **Hash function:** SHA256

chunks.title: Verify Overview
Verify Overview
chunks.text:
Send verification messages in your users' preferred languages.

1. Contact [Plivo support](https://support.plivo.com/hc/en-us) to configure translations for your SMS templates
2. Pass the `locale` parameter when creating a session

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.text:
Combine language code (ISO 639-1) and optional region code (ISO 3166-1):

* `en` - English
* `en_US` - English (US)
* `es` - Spanish
* `fr_FR` - French (France)

If the specified locale is unavailable or invalid, the default locale (`en`) is used.

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.text:
Most businesses need just one Verify application. Consider multiple applications when:

* Different OTP lengths are needed (e.g., 4-digit for login, 6-digit for checkout)
* Different channels are required (SMS-only for logins, SMS+voice for payments)
* Different Fraud Shield settings are needed per use case

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.text: View and analyze your verification traffic on the Plivo console at **Verify > [Logs](https://cx.plivo.com/logs)**.

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.text:
| Field | Description |
| - | - |
| Date | When the session was created |
| UUID | Unique session identifier |
| Application Alias | Name of the application used |
| Recipient | Destination phone number |
| Status | `in-progress`, `verified`, or `expired` |

| Total Charge | Session cost including channel fees |

chunks.title: Verify Overview
chunks.text:
Filter results by subaccount, date range, status, country, phone number, or application alias.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Session data is retained for 90 days.

chunks.title: Session API
chunks.text:
Create, validate, retrieve, and list verification sessions

The Session API lets you send and validate one-time passwords (OTP) for two-factor authentication (2FA) using SMS and voice channels.

**API Endpoint**

```
https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Verify/Session/
```

chunks.title: Session API
chunks.text: The API creates a Session object once for each recipient within the code expiry time. A session can have multiple attempts to deliver the OTP.

chunks.title: Session API
chunks.text:
**session_uuid** `string`

A 36-character string that uniquely identifies a session.

**app_uuid** `string`

ID of the application used to trigger the session.

**alias** `string`

Alias of the Verify application used to trigger the session.

**recipient** `string`

The destination phone number (in E.164 format).

**destination_country_iso2** `string`

ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the destination number. Example: `IN`.

**destination_network** `string`

Carrier network detected for the destination number.

**requestor_ip** `string`

IP address from which the session creation request originated.

**status** `string`

Current status. Values: `in-progress`, `verified`, `expired`.

**channel** `string`

The last channel used for the session.

**locale** `string`

Language translation used for the session.

**otp_attempts** `object`

Details of all attempts made during a session.

**charge** `object`

Details of all charges incurred during a session.

**created_at** `string`

UTC time when the session was created.

**updated_at** `string`

UTC time when the session was last updated.

chunks.title: Session API
chunks.text:
Send an OTP via SMS or voice.

```
POST https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Verify/Session/
```

chunks.title: Session API
chunks.text:
**recipient** `string` *required*

The phone number to send the OTP to.

**app_uuid** `string`

UUID of the Verify application. Defaults to default application.

**channel** `string`

Delivery channel. Values: `sms`, `voice`. Default: `sms`.

**url** `string`

URL for status callbacks.

**method** `string`

HTTP method for callbacks. Values: `GET`, `POST`. Default: `POST`.

**locale** `string`

Language code (e.g., `en_US`, `es`, `fr_FR`). Default: `en`.

**brand_name** `string`

Brand name to replace `${brand_name}` in templates.

**app_hash** `string`

Android app hash for SMS Retriever API integration.

**code_length** `integer`

OTP length (4-8). Overrides application default.

chunks.text: Set up a server endpoint to receive real-time status updates for your verification sessions. Specify the callback URL when creating a session.

chunks.title: Session API
chunks.text:
**SessionUUID** `string`

Unique session identifier.

**SessionStatus** `string`

Session status. Values: `in-progress`, `expired`.

Unique identifier for the SMS/call attempt.

Sequence number of the attempt.

Channel used. Values: `sms`, `voice`.

Error code from the channel.

Destination phone number.

UTC time when the attempt was created.

chunks.title: Session API
chunks.text:
> [!NOTE]
>
> Plivo automatically retries webhooks three times if HTTP 200 is not returned:
>
> * First retry: 60 seconds after original attempt
> * Second retry: 120 seconds after first retry
> * Third retry: 240 seconds after second retry

Set up Plivo Zentrunk SIP trunking for inbound and outbound voice calls.

![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/V2GGXaNKq8uCbGT3/images/zentrunk-hero.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=V2GGXaNKq8uCbGT3&q=85&s=37f5a9e3d5e4d38704d4f61535725cd8)

chunks.title: Quickstart Guide
chunks.text: Zentrunk, Plivo’s SIP trunking service, provides global coverage for your outbound and inbound voice calls, working with your current cloud or on-premises communications infrastructure. Whether you’re looking to increase the capacity of your current telecom stack, increase coverage and phone number inventory, or extend your on-premises infrastructure to the cloud, Zentrunk can get you started. No minimum spends, carrier negotiations, or long-term contracts are required, and you can provision SIP trunks instantly using our console.

chunks.title: Quickstart Guide
chunks.text:
Zentrunk provides benefits such as:

**Scalability**: Zentrunk supports your organization’s growth across multiple geographic locations. By combining voice and data in a single network, SIP trunking lets your organization quickly open new sites or establish full-time remote workers. You can scale as you grow by self-provisioning local, international, mobile, and toll-free numbers in more than 70 countries, configuring them in your trunk, and terminating calls from your IP PBX. You can also make calls to more than 190 countries using Zentrunk to make your business more globally accessible.

**Cost savings**: With traditional phone service, your organization is subject to different, often variable charges for your local, long distance, and international calling. Moving from traditional telecom systems to SIP trunking helps you save on recurring costs, as you can build your entire telecom system in the cloud, and be billed on a simple per-usage basis. You can also save by forgoing the physical infrastructure and hardware investments that typically come with scaling phone lines. With Zentrunk, adding phone lines or services is as simple as purchasing an additional handset and scaling your monthly service agreement.

**Reliability**: Traditional phone systems are prone to interruptions from factors such as weather events and networking issues. SIP trunking is more reliable, since you can add failover routing if a primary IP address is not responsive. With a redundant infrastructure across multiple geographies and at least three local carrier connections across countries, Zentrunk promises 99.99% uptime.

**Easy management for your IT teams:** Your IT team will never have to wait on hold to speak to a customer service representative again. SIP trunking and VoIP phones offer easy-to-use administrative portals for on-site management, including actions like adjusting call routing, changing extensions, and adding phone lines on demand.

Plivo’s 24x7 premium support and consultative customer success team can provide you with technical guidance when you need it.

chunks.title: Quickstart Guide
chunks.text:
You need a Plivo account to start using Zentrunk. If you do not have one, [sign up](https://cx.plivo.com/signup) for one.

1. [Sign up](https://cx.plivo.com/signup) through our console with your work email address
2. Check your inbox for an activation email message from Plivo. Click on the link in the message to activate your account.
3. Enter your mobile number to complete the phone verification step.

If you have any questions about creating a Plivo account, reach out to our [support team](https://support.plivo.com/hc/en-us) for assistance.

chunks.title: Quickstart Guide
chunks.section: Getting started › Supported software and hardware
chunks.text:
Zentrunk is compatible with a broad range of software and devices. We support:

* [All major IP PBXes](/docs/sip-trunking/interconnection-guides/overview/)
* All SIP-based hardphones and softphones
* Integrations with all WebRTC clients and endpoints

chunks.title: Quickstart Guide
chunks.text:
Zentrunk supports these SIP methods: ACK, BYE, CANCEL, INVITE, OPTIONS, REFER, and UPDATE. We don’t support INFO, MESSAGE, PRACK, PUBLISH, REGISTER, or SUBSCRIBE.

REFER is used for mid-call transfers. See [SIP REFER](/docs/sip-trunking/concepts/sip-refer) for details.

chunks.title: Quickstart Guide
chunks.text: Zentrunk supports G.711 U-law (PCMU) and A-law (PCMA) codecs.

chunks.title: Quickstart Guide
chunks.text: SIP trunk calls over the internet require sufficient bandwidth to support peak concurrent call traffic. Plivo needs about 100Kbps for every successful call, so your peak bandwidth requirements can be calculated as 100Kbps * peak concurrent calls.

chunks.title: Quickstart Guide
chunks.text:
#### Outbound limitations

The calls-per-second limitation for Zentrunk SIP trunking is based on both account-level CPS and trunk-level CPS. The account-level CPS is the rate at which calls may be made from an account in a second, while the trunk-level CPS applies to each of the trunks individually in the account.

Businesses can choose different ways to allocate their account-level CPS across trunks in their account.

**Scenario 1**: A user has 25 account-level CPS and three trunks

* 2 trunks are set at 10 CPS (high-volume use cases)
* 1 trunk is set at 5 CPS (low-volume use case)

**Scenario 2**: A user has 10 account-level CPS and 10 trunks

* Each trunk has a CPS of 10
* This allows for a “free-for-all” where if one trunk is consistently initiating calls at a rate of 10 CPS, calls from other trunks would fail

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Note:** You cannot exceed the account CPS limit even if you have multiple trunks in your account. If it exceeds, then calls will fail with the error “cps_limit_reached” and error code 5180.

By default, the account-level rate is 1–2 CPS depending on your plan, and each trunk is set to 1 CPS. The account-level rate is a single pool shared with Voice API, not a SIP Trunking-only allowance — see [SIP Trunking account limits](/docs/sip-trunking/concepts/account-limits). Higher CPS is available on an Enterprise plan; to request it, ask **Buddy**, Plivo's in-console chat agent, from the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/home). For help with technical issues related to SIP Trunking, submit a ticket with the [Plivo support team](https://support.plivo.com/hc/en-us/requests/new?ticket_form_id=360000156292).

#### Inbound limitations

There are no calls-per-second constraints for inbound trunks in Zentrunk SIP trunking.

chunks.title: Quickstart Guide
chunks.text:
![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/GjxgkWYDEc2_LVPj/images/outbound-sip-trunking.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=GjxgkWYDEc2_LVPj&q=85&s=0c32acd5ea89ce0fe4bb729181c8cf6f)

Zentrunk’s outbound SIP trunks let you reach fixed and mobile phones in more than 190 countries. There are no restrictions or limitations on channels or ports. Concurrent calls are governed by your account-level concurrency limit rather than by the trunk — see [SIP Trunking account limits](/docs/sip-trunking/concepts/account-limits). You get all of the standard features of a telco (such as dynamic CLI, DTMF support, and per-second billing) and more (including secure trunking, fraud detection, and instant provisioning). You pay only for what you use, with no long-term contracts.

chunks.title: Quickstart Guide
chunks.section: Outbound trunks (termination) › Create an outbound trunk
chunks.text:
To use Zentrunk to terminate calls, you need to set up trunk authentication on the Plivo console. Authenticating your trunk ensures that Zentrunk accepts only traffic that your infrastructure sends securely. You can configure your trunk to be authenticated by an IP access control list, a credentials list, or both.

![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/Ac6PoKJHHxDx1U63/images/outbound-trunk.gif?s=0a871cdf2552c305207a15aafb8bb980)

#### To create an outbound trunk:

1. In the Plivo console, visit Zentrunk > [Outbound Trunks](https://cx.plivo.com/sip-trunking) and click **Create New Outbound Trunk**.
2. Under Trunk Details, enter a name for your trunk (for example, Plivo Test).

   > [!NOTE]
   >
   > **Note:** By default, the trunk is enabled.
3. Under Trunk Authentication, select the IP Access Control List, the Credentials List, or both.

   > [!NOTE]
   >
   > **Note:** Make sure to choose either an IP Access Control List or a Credentials List. The IP Access Control List consists of a list of the IP addresses from which a SIP Invite will be accepted for this trunk. The Credentials List provides a username and password that will be used to authenticate a SIP Invite.

   **To create an IP Access Control List:**

   1. To add a new IP Access Control List, click **+ Add New IP ACL**.
   2. In the Create New IP Access Control List window, enter the name for your IP Access Control List (for example, TestACL) and then enter the IP addresses to be whitelisted in the IP Address List field.

      > [!NOTE]
      >
      > **Note:** You can add multiple comma-separated IP addresses.
   3. Click **Create ACL** to save and add your IP Access Control List.

   **To create a Credentials List:**

   1. To add a new Credentials List, click **+ Add New Credentials List**.
   2. In the Create Credentials List window, enter a name for your Auth Group (for example, TestCredList), a username, and a password.

      > [!NOTE]
      >
      > **Note:** The username must be 5 to 20 characters, containing only alphanumeric characters. The password must be 5 to 20 characters, containing only alphanumeric characters and the special characters `~!@#$%^&*()_+`, with at least one special character.
   3. Click **Create Credentials List** to save and add your Credentials List.

   Select an IP Group, Auth Group, or both.

   Under Secure Trunking, use the Disabled/Enabled toggle button to enable secure trunking.

   > [!NOTE]
   >
   > **Note:** By default, secure trunking is disabled, but we strongly recommend you enable it, as we discuss in the next section.
4. Click **Create Trunk** to create your outbound trunk.

chunks.title: Quickstart Guide
chunks.text: To ensure that the information shared between your communication infrastructure and Zentrunk is secure, we recommend using the Secure Trunking feature. You can secure your trunk by encrypting and authenticating the signaling and media data packets involved for a SIP call over the internet.

chunks.title: Quickstart Guide
chunks.section: Secure trunking on outbound trunks › Encrypt signaling packets
chunks.text:
You can encrypt signaling by using TLS (Transport Layer Security) protocol. Communication over TLS ensures authentication between two transport endpoints over an unsecured path for the SIP messages. We support TLS versions 1.2 and 1.3.

* **If Secure Trunking is enabled**: Zentrunk will communicate with your PBX or SBC over **TLS** for **Signaling**.
* **If Secure Trunking is disabled**: The calls will be over **TCP/UDP** for **Signaling**.

chunks.title: Quickstart Guide
chunks.section: Secure trunking on outbound trunks › Encrypt media packets
chunks.text:
Zentrunk uses Secure Real-Time Protocol (SRTP) to secure RTP (media) packets.

* **If Secure Trunking is enabled**: Zentrunk will communicate with your PBX or SBC over **SRTP** for **Media**.
* **If Secure Trunking is disabled**: The calls will be over **RTP** for **Media**.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Note:** You can use SRTP regardless of the SIP signaling messages being on TCP/UDP. However, Plivo strongly recommends you enable a secure mode of communication between your infrastructure and Zentrunk.

chunks.title: Quickstart Guide
chunks.text:
![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/_fSpYHZS4fGpqS0Z/images/inbound-phone-number.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=_fSpYHZS4fGpqS0Z&q=85&s=e7bd7b93d055b6da5fd634535c383cb0)

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Only inbound trunks can be attached to phone numbers.** Outbound trunks are used by your applications to place calls through Plivo but cannot be mapped to phone numbers in the console. If you need both inbound and outbound capabilities, create separate trunks for each direction.

With Zentrunk, you can instantly access the inbound phone number DIDs in Plivo's inventory of more than 5 million phone numbers representing more than 60 countries. Concurrent calls on a phone number are governed by your account-level concurrency limit — see [SIP Trunking account limits](/docs/sip-trunking/concepts/account-limits). Zentrunk customers can also instantly search, filter, and provision fixed, mobile, toll-free, and SMS-enabled phone numbers through the Zentrunk API or user interface. Also, our carrier team can help you to port your phone numbers to Zentrunk from your current provider.

chunks.title: Quickstart Guide
chunks.section: Inbound trunks (origination) › Create an inbound trunk
chunks.text:
![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/Ac6PoKJHHxDx1U63/images/inbound-trunk.gif?s=f1dc8110e24d4029d5aa31c585034b14)

To create an inbound trunk:

1. In the Plivo console, visit Zentrunk > [Inbound Trunks](https://cx.plivo.com/sip-trunking) and click **Create New Inbound Trunk**.
2. Under Trunk Details, enter a name for your trunk (for example, Plivo Inbound).

   > [!NOTE]
   >
   > **Note:** The Enabled checkbox is selected by default.
3. Under Trunk Authentication, select the Primary URI and Fallback URI of your PBX.

   > [!NOTE]
   >
   > **Note:** The Primary URI is the FQDN or IP address to which all calls are forwarded first. If the Primary URI is unresponsive, calls will be forwarded to the Fallback URI.

   To add a new Primary or Fallback URI, click **Add New URI**.

   On the Create URI window, enter a name for your URI (for example, inbounduri), and then enter the URI (the FQDN or IP address of your VoIP infrastructure).

   To enable Authentication, click on the **Authentication** option and provide your username and password.

   Click **Create URI** to save and add your URI.
4. Once you’ve created and selected your Primary and Fallback URI, click **Create Trunk**. Your inbound trunk will be created.

chunks.title: Quickstart Guide
chunks.section: Inbound trunks (origination) › Assigning an inbound trunk to a phone number
chunks.text:
The next task is to link your trunk with phone numbers. You can link the trunk with existing phone numbers in your account or buy a new phone number to use.

1. If you wish to use existing numbers, select the phone numbers under the **Current Phone Numbers** section, and click **Link Selected Numbers**.
2. If you wish to use a new number, navigate to the **Buy New Number** section and choose the country, prefix, type, capability, and click on **Search**.
3. Select a phone number and click **Buy Number**. The number will be added to your account and linked with your inbound trunk.

To learn more about buying a Plivo phone number, visit our [Buy a Phone Number Quickstart Guide](/docs/numbers/phone-numbers#buy-a-phone-number).

chunks.title: Calls
chunks.text:
Retrieve call detail records (CDRs) and call insights for SIP trunk calls

The Calls API lets you retrieve call detail records (CDRs) and quality insights for calls made through your SIP trunks.

chunks.title: Calls
Calls
chunks.text:
**call_uuid** `string`

Unique call identifier.

**from_number** `string`

Caller ID. On India domestic calls retried through [automatic carrier failover](/docs/voice/concepts/carrier-failover), this field records the fallback caller ID used on the retry, not the number you originally sent.

**to_number** `string`

Destination number.

**call_direction** `string`

Direction. Values: `inbound`, `outbound`.

**call_duration** `integer`

Actual call duration in seconds.

**bill_duration** `integer`

Billed duration in seconds.

**billed_duration** `integer`

Billed duration (may differ based on billing interval).

**initiation_time** `string`

When call was initiated (UTC).

**answer_time** `string`

When call was answered (UTC).

**end_time** `string`

When call ended (UTC).

**hangup_cause_name** `string`

Reason for hangup.

**hangup_cause_code** `integer`

Numeric hangup cause code.

**hangup_source** `string`

Who ended the call. Values: `customer`, `carrier`, `zentrunk`.

**total_rate** `string`

Per-minute rate (USD).

**total_amount** `string`

Total cost (USD).

**trunk_domain** `string`

Trunk domain used.

**from_country** `string`

Caller's country (ISO2).

**to_country** `string`

Destination country (ISO2).

**transport_protocol** `string`

Protocol used (e.g., `udp`, `tcp`).

**srtp** `boolean`

Whether SRTP encryption was used.

**secure_trunking** `boolean`

Whether secure trunking was enabled.

**secure_trunking_rate** `string`

Secure trunking per-minute rate.

**stir_verification** `string`

STIR/SHAKEN status.

**attestation_indicator** `string`

Attestation level. Values: `A`, `B`, `C`.

chunks.title: Calls
chunks.text:
Retrieve CDRs for all calls with optional filtering.

```text theme={null}
GET https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Zentrunk/Call/
```

chunks.title: Calls
chunks.text:
**from_number** `string`

Filter by caller ID (exact or prefix).

**to_number** `string`

Filter by destination (exact or prefix).

**call_direction** `string`

Filter by direction. Values: `inbound`, `outbound`.

**hangup_cause_code** `integer`

Filter by hangup cause code.

**hangup_source** `string`

Filter by hangup source. Values: `customer`, `carrier`, `zentrunk`.

**stir_verification** `string`

Filter by STIR status. Values: `Verified`, `Not Verified`, `Not Applicable`.

**bill_duration** `integer`

Filter by duration in seconds. Supports variants: `bill_duration__gt`, `bill_duration__gte`, `bill_duration__lt`, `bill_duration__lte`.

**end_time** `string`

Filter by call end time. Format: `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM[:ss]` (UTC). Supports variants: `end_time__gt`, `end_time__gte`, `end_time__lt`, `end_time__lte`.

**limit** `integer`

Results per page. Max: 20. Default: 20.

**offset** `integer`

Pagination offset. Default: 0.

> [!NOTE]
>
> You can retrieve only calls from the last 90 days. Without an `end_time` filter, the API searches the last 30 days.

chunks.title: Calls
chunks.text:
```bash cURL theme={null}
curl -i --user AUTH_ID:AUTH_TOKEN \
    "https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Zentrunk/Call/?call_direction=outbound&end_time__gte=2024-01-01%2000:00&limit=20"
```

chunks.text:

Unique identifier for the API request.

**meta** `object`

Pagination metadata: `limit` (results per page), `offset` (items skipped), `total_count` (total matching calls).

**objects** `array`

Array of call objects — see [The Call Object](#the-call-object).

```json theme={null}
  "api_id": "a04ad809-3b78-4bbe-9baf-acfc7800b10f",
  "meta": {
    "limit": 20,
    "offset": 0,
    "total_count": 2,
    "previous": null,
    "next": null
  },
  "objects": [
    {
      "call_uuid": "90b6eb07-796c-4d86-a4fd-44ed11667ddb",
      "from_number": "+12025551111",
      "to_number": "+13125551234",
      "call_direction": "outbound",
      "call_duration": 180,
      "bill_duration": 180,
      "stir_verification": "Verified",
      "attestation_indicator": "A"
    }
  ]
}
```

chunks.title: Credentials
chunks.text:
Manage SIP credentials for digest authentication on outbound trunks

The Credentials API lets you create and manage username/password pairs for SIP digest authentication on outbound trunks.

chunks.title: Credentials
chunks.text:
```
https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Zentrunk/Credential/
```

chunks.title: Credentials
chunks.text: A credentials object contains username and password for SIP digest authentication when your PBX sends calls to Plivo.

chunks.title: Credentials
chunks.text:
**credential_uuid** `string`

Unique identifier for the credentials.

**name** `string`

Friendly name for the credentials.

**username** `string`

Username for SIP authentication. Must be 5 to 20 characters, containing only alphanumeric characters.

**password** `string`

Password for SIP authentication (only set on create/update, never returned in responses). Must be 5 to 20 characters, containing only alphanumeric characters and the special characters `~!@#$%^&*()_+`, with at least one special character.

Manage destination endpoints for inbound SIP trunks

The Origination URIs API lets you create and manage destination endpoints (your PBX/infrastructure) where Plivo sends inbound calls.

chunks.text: An origination URI represents a destination endpoint where Plivo forwards inbound calls on your SIP trunk.

FQDN or IP address of your VoIP infrastructure.

**authentication_needed** `boolean`

Whether Plivo should authenticate when sending calls.

**username** `string`

Username for authentication (if enabled).

**password** `string`

Password for authentication (only set on create/update, never returned in responses).

chunks.title: Origination URIs
chunks.text:
| Type | Purpose |
| - | - |
| **Primary URI** | Default destination for inbound calls |
| **Fallback URI** | Used when primary is unreachable or returns error |

Configure both for high availability:

1. Create two origination URIs pointing to different servers
2. Assign one as `primary_uri_uuid` and the other as `fallback_uri_uuid`
3. If primary fails, Plivo automatically routes to fallback

| FQDN | `sip.example.com` |
| FQDN with port | `sip.example.com:5060` |

chunks.title: API Overview
chunks.text:
Introduction to Plivo's SIP Trunking (Zentrunk) API

The Plivo Zentrunk API lets you programmatically manage SIP trunks, authentication, and retrieve call records. The API uses standard HTTP methods and returns JSON responses.

chunks.title: API Overview
chunks.text:
```
https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Zentrunk/
```

chunks.title: API Overview
chunks.text:
All API requests use HTTP Basic Authentication with your Plivo credentials:

* **Username**: Your Auth ID
* **Password**: Your Auth Token

Find your credentials on the [Plivo Console Dashboard](https://cx.plivo.com/home).

```bash cURL theme={null}
curl -i --user AUTH_ID:AUTH_TOKEN \
    https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Zentrunk/Trunk/
```

chunks.title: Trunks
chunks.text:
Create and manage SIP trunks for inbound and outbound voice traffic

The Trunks API lets you create and manage SIP trunks that route voice traffic between your infrastructure and Plivo's network.

chunks.title: Trunks
chunks.text:
```
https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/Zentrunk/Trunk/
```

chunks.title: Trunks
chunks.text: A trunk represents a SIP connection between your infrastructure and Plivo's network. Trunks can be inbound (receiving calls from Plivo) or outbound (sending calls to Plivo).

chunks.title: Trunks
chunks.text:
**trunk_id** `string`

Unique identifier for the trunk.

**trunk_domain** `string`

Unique address on Plivo to route SIP traffic (e.g., `21784177241578.zt.plivo.com`).

**name** `string`

Friendly name for the trunk.

**trunk_status** `string`

Status of the trunk: `enabled` or `disabled`.

**trunk_direction** `string`

Direction of the trunk: `inbound` or `outbound`.

**secure** `boolean`

Whether SRTP (media) and TLS (signaling) encryption is enabled.

**ipacl_uuid** `string`

IP access control list UUID (for outbound trunks).

**credential_uuid** `string`

Credentials list UUID (for outbound trunks).

**primary_uri_uuid** `string`

Primary origination URI UUID (for inbound trunks).

**fallback_uri_uuid** `string`

Fallback origination URI UUID (for inbound trunks).

```json theme={null}
  "name": "trunk_name_1",
  "trunk_id": "21784177241578",

  "trunk_status": "enabled",
  "secure": true,
  "trunk_direction": "outbound",
  "ipacl_uuid": "90b6eb07-796c-4d86-a4fd-44ed11667ddb",
  "credential_uuid": "eb07-796c-4d86-a4fd-44ed11667ddb",

}
```

chunks.title: Account limits
chunks.text:
CPS, concurrency, and trunk limits for Plivo SIP Trunking in the India and US data regions

> [!NOTE]
>
> * **What:** The account-wide CPS and concurrency limits your trunks draw on, plus the per-trunk and resource limits.
> * **When:** Check when sizing trunks, or when calls fail with hangup cause `5180` or `5190`.

Your account has two call capacity limits, and both apply at the same time. **CPS (calls per second)** caps how fast you can start new calls. **Concurrency** caps how many calls can be active at once. Both limits are account-wide: your trunks draw on the same pool as your Voice API traffic, not a separate SIP Trunking allowance.

chunks.title: Account limits
chunks.text:
Your limits depend on your data region and, in the US data region, on your plan and lifetime spend.

| Data region | Plan / lifetime voice + SIP Trunking spend | Outbound CPS | Concurrent calls |
| - | - | - | - |
| India data region | Professional | 2 (default) | 50 (default) |
| India data region | Enterprise | Set by your contract | Set by your contract |
| US data region | Free Tier — before your first payment | 1 | 2 |
| US data region | Professional — less than USD 100 | 1 | 5 |
| US data region | Professional — USD 100 to USD 500 | 2 | 10 |
| US data region | Professional — more than USD 500 | 2 | 25 |
| US data region | Enterprise | 2 | 50 |

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Outbound CPS and concurrency are single account-wide pools shared by Voice API and SIP Trunking.** An account with 2 outbound CPS can start two outbound calls per second in total, whichever product they go out on. An account with 50 concurrent calls can hold 50 calls in total across both products.

Free Tier is not a plan you select. Every US data region account starts there and moves to Professional on its first payment.

US data region accounts created before October 1, 2026 are not on the plan-based limits in the table. They have custom limits, set per account based on usage.

In the India data region, Plivo sells capacity as concurrency. Professional accounts start at 50 concurrent calls. Enterprise accounts purchase the concurrency they need, and the limit and its price are set by the contract. Your CPS is set from your concurrency limit, so when your concurrency limit changes, your CPS changes with it.

chunks.title: Account limits
chunks.section: Your call capacity limits › Trunk-level CPS
chunks.text:
Each outbound trunk also has its own CPS, allocated from the account pool.

| Level | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| Account | 1–2 CPS by plan | Total outbound calls per second across all trunks, shared with Voice API |
| Trunk | 1 CPS | Configurable per trunk, allocated from the account pool |

Both levels are enforced. You cannot exceed the account CPS limit by spreading traffic across trunks. Inbound trunks have no CPS limit of their own.

chunks.title: Account limits
chunks.section: What counts toward your concurrency limit
chunks.text:
Concurrency is the number of active calls on your account at any point in time, including calls that are still being set up.

| Call state | Counted? |
| - | - |
| **Ringing / connecting** — call initiated, still in setup | Yes |
| **Connected / in progress** — call is live | Yes |
| **Completed / ended** — call has been disconnected | No |

Every PSTN call leg counts, inbound and outbound, across SIP Trunking and Voice API. Plivo runs the same concurrency check for SIP Trunking calls as for Voice API calls. SIP-to-SIP calls and WhatsApp calls do not count toward your account concurrency limit.

chunks.title: Account limits
chunks.section: What counts toward your concurrency limit › India data region: 140-series and 160-series numbers
chunks.text: Calls placed from [140-series](/docs/voice/concepts/140-series-provisioning) and [160-series](/docs/voice/concepts/160-series-provisioning) numbers draw on a separate concurrency allocation for that series, not on your account concurrency limit. Calls from your other numbers are not affected when a series limit is reached. A SIP Trunking call rejected at a series limit carries hangup cause `5190` (`concurrent_call_limit_exceeded`), the same as an account-level breach. Plivo sets the 140-series and 160-series allocation on your account when you provision those numbers. To check or change it, ask **Buddy**, Plivo's in-console chat agent, under **Organization settings > Account limits** in the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/organization-settings/limits), or contact your account manager.

chunks.title: Account limits
chunks.section: What happens when you exceed a limit
chunks.text:
SIP Trunking rejects every call above a limit. It never queues.

| Limit | SIP Trunking | Voice API |
| - | - | - |
| **Above your trunk CPS** | **Rejected immediately** with hangup cause `5180` (`cps_limit_reached`) | Not applicable |
| **Above your account CPS** | **Rejected immediately** with hangup cause `5180` (`cps_limit_reached`) | **Queued.** The request is accepted and dialed as your rate drops |
| **Above your concurrency limit** | **Rejected immediately** with hangup cause `5190` (`concurrent_call_limit_exceeded`) | **Rejected immediately** with hangup cause `5030` (`Concurrency Limit Breached`) |

> [!WARNING]
>
> SIP Trunking never queues. Every call above a limit fails instantly — no ring, no connection, no grace period. As soon as your rate or active call count drops below the limit, new calls are accepted again.

Every rejected SIP Trunking call appears in **Logs > SIP Trunking** with its hangup cause, so you can measure the impact directly. Hangup causes `5030`, `5180`, and `5190` are the same in every data region. See [Zentrunk hangup codes](/docs/sip-trunking/troubleshooting/zentrunk-hangup-codes) for the full list.

chunks.title: Account limits
chunks.section: What happens when you exceed a limit › Concurrency alert emails
chunks.text: When calls are rejected for a concurrency breach, Plivo emails your account owner with the time window, the limit that was reached, and what to do next. Plivo sends at most one alert every 24 hours per limit.

chunks.title: Account limits
chunks.text:
| Resource | Limit |
| - | - |
| Trunks per account | 100 (recommended) |
| IP ACLs per account | Unlimited |
| Inbound trunk CPS | No limit |

chunks.title: Account limits
chunks.text:
1. To see your current concurrency limit, go to **Organization settings > Account limits** in the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/organization-settings/limits).
2. To see your usage, go to **Logs > Voice > Export > Export Concurrency Data**. The export gives minute-level concurrent call data for up to 30 days.

The export counts every concurrent call on your account: SIP Trunking and Voice API, inbound and outbound. **Logs > SIP Trunking** shows your trunk call activity, including rejected calls, for the last 30 days.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Rule of thumb:** if your 30-day peak exceeds 80% of your limit, review your capacity before you start seeing failures. Pace your PBX or dialer within your CPS, stagger bulk campaigns rather than launching them at once, and retry after a short delay when a call is rejected.

chunks.title: Account limits
chunks.text:
| Data region | How limits change |
| - | - |
| India data region | Higher concurrency is available on an Enterprise plan, in the amount your contract allows. Click **Request Enterprise** under **Organization settings > Account limits** in the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/organization-settings/limits), ask **Buddy**, Plivo's in-console chat agent, or contact your account manager |
| US data region | Limits rise automatically within 24 hours as your lifetime voice and SIP Trunking spend crosses a tier. For more than your tier allows, click **Request Enterprise** under **Organization settings > Account limits** in the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/organization-settings/limits), ask **Buddy**, or contact your account manager |

chunks.title: Zentrunk Geo Permissions
chunks.text:
Control which countries your Zentrunk trunk can route calls to

> [!NOTE]
>
> * **What:** Control which countries your Zentrunk SIP trunk can call, to prevent toll fraud from compromised trunks.
> * **When:** Toggle countries in the Console. All countries are allowed by default; blocked calls fail.

SIP trunk fraud, in which hackers gain control of an organization’s SIP trunk and make unauthorized calls, is becoming more common, and it’s often difficult to detect since call patterns can look similar to normal usage. Businesses need to take measures to avoid scenarios such as:

1. Calls placed to high-risk premium destinations
2. Overnight loss of credits
3. Calls placed from your account to unknown numbers, leading to unintended consequences

Zentrunk Geo Permissions lets Plivo SIP trunk users selectively enable or disable outbound calling to international destinations. Doing so helps organizations avoid calls to high-cost routes and prevent other fraudulent activities.

chunks.title: Zentrunk Geo Permissions
chunks.text:
You can restrict the list of countries to which users can place calls through Zentrunk. To do this, on the Plivo console, navigate to Zentrunk > [Geo Permissions](https://cx.plivo.com/geo-permissions/voice).

**Placing a country-level block:** By default, calling to all countries is allowed. You can deselect specific countries, then click Save Changes. The new country restrictions go into effect immediately. Zentrunk will not allow calls to countries that are deselected.

![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/Ac6PoKJHHxDx1U63/images/geo-permissions.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=Ac6PoKJHHxDx1U63&q=85&s=f48046ad45fed96e7b1f325247fdf019)

In the example above, calls to Spain, Sweden, and Switzerland are allowed. Calling to other countries on the list is barred.

**Placing a high-risk voice network group block:** Plivo analyzes call trends and rates of premium voice network groups for each country. We maintain a list of high-risk voice network groups. You can block calls to these groups by clicking on High Risk Permissions and making sure the toggle is Enabled, as it is by default, then clicking Save Changes. From that point on, outbound calls to preidentified risky prefix clusters are blocked. Plivo periodically updates the list of high-risk groups.

![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/-VVFcM3g7XHd8wTl/images/premium-numbers.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=-VVFcM3g7XHd8wTl&q=85&s=d1a099d580090dcf12ed45895c4b5434)

chunks.title: Zentrunk Geo Permissions
chunks.text:
If a call is placed to a destination number that belongs to a country that has not been selected in Geo Permissions, these response codes will show in your call detail report:

*SIP Response Code: 403 - Barred Country;* *Zentrunk Hangup Code: 4650*

*Description: The number has been blocked in geo permissions settings. Any calls made to this number belong to a specific country or number group and will not go through since it has been barred.*

chunks.title: SIP REFER
chunks.text:
Transfer active calls from your SIP endpoint or AI agent to another destination using SIP REFER

> [!NOTE]
>
> Send a SIP REFER from your endpoint to hand off a live call to any number — without dropping the caller or starting a new call. Works on both inbound and outbound SIP trunk calls. No account enablement required.

Use SIP REFER to hand off a live call from your AI agent (or any SIP endpoint) to a human, an IVR, or another phone number — without disconnecting the caller or initiating a new call. This is the standard mechanism Plivo customers use to escalate AI conversations to live support, route calls to specialist queues, or transfer to a backup number when an agent is unavailable.

**What you get:** zero-touch escalation, a single billing record, and no re-dial for the caller.

chunks.title: SIP REFER
chunks.text:
| | SIP REFER | Voice API `Transfer` | PHLO Transfer node |
| - | - | - | - |
| **Best for** | SIP / AI-agent endpoints | Hosted call control | No-code workflows |
| **Initiated by** | Your SIP endpoint | Plivo (via API call) | Plivo (via PHLO flow) |
| **Typical adopter** | Voice-AI builders, contact centers | App developers | Business / ops users |
| **Setup effort** | SIP endpoint must support REFER | API key only | Drag-and-drop |

This page covers SIP REFER. For the other methods, see [Voice API Transfer](/docs/voice/api/calls#transfer-a-call) and PHLO Transfer node.

chunks.title: SIP REFER
chunks.text:
> [card] [Outbound call transfer](/docs/sip-trunking/concepts/sip-refer-outbound)
>
> Your AI agent or PBX placed an outbound call and wants to hand it off to a human agent.

> [card] [Inbound call transfer](/docs/sip-trunking/concepts/sip-refer-inbound)
>
> A caller dialled your Plivo number, your AI agent answered, and wants to hand off.

chunks.title: SIP REFER
chunks.text:
In both cases, your SIP endpoint sends a REFER request mid-call. Plivo bridges the caller to the transfer target and sends your endpoint a BYE. The REFER message itself is identical — the only difference is how the initial call leg was established.

| | Outbound | Inbound |
| - | - | - |
| **Call originated by** | Your endpoint | The caller |
| **Initial INVITE direction** | Endpoint → Plivo → Customer | Customer → Plivo → Endpoint |
| **REFER sent by** | Your endpoint → Plivo | Your endpoint → Plivo |
| **Caller ID on transfer leg** | Your Plivo number | Original caller's number |
| **Typical use case** | AI-to-human handover, proactive outreach | Inbound support queues, IVR escalation |

chunks.title: SIP REFER
chunks.text:
* **SIP trunk domains only.** The `Refer-To` URI must use your SIP trunk domain (ending in `.zt.plivo.com`). Transfers to arbitrary SIP URIs or external domains are blocked.
* **No private IPs.** The transfer target cannot be a private IP address.
* **Transport.** SIP REFER works on UDP, TCP, and TLS trunks.
* **Codec re-negotiation.** Plivo handles codec negotiation between the original leg and the new transfer leg automatically.
* **Caller ID on the transfer leg.** For inbound calls, the transfer target sees the original caller's number. For outbound calls, the transfer target sees your Plivo number.
* **Chained transfers.** You can transfer the same call more than once. Each REFER starts a new transfer leg; the previous leg is replaced.
* **If the transfer target hangs up.** The entire call is terminated. The original caller is not reconnected to your endpoint.

chunks.title: SIP REFER
chunks.section: Frequently asked questions › Is the transferred leg billed separately, or as one call?
chunks.text: The original call leg and the transfer leg are billed as separate call records. You see two CDR entries: one for the original leg (from start until your endpoint is disconnected) and one for the transfer leg (from when the transfer target answers).

chunks.title: SIP REFER
chunks.section: Frequently asked questions › What caller ID does the transfer target see?
chunks.text: For **inbound calls**, the transfer target sees the original caller's number. For **outbound calls**, the transfer target sees the Plivo number you used as the caller ID on the original leg.

chunks.title: SIP REFER
chunks.section: Frequently asked questions › Will my CDR show the transfer target's number?
chunks.text: Yes. The transfer leg appears as a separate CDR entry with the transfer target's number in the `to` field. Allow up to 60 seconds for the CDR to finalise after the call ends.

chunks.title: SIP REFER
chunks.section: Frequently asked questions › Does call recording continue after the transfer?
chunks.text: Call recording on the original leg stops when your endpoint is disconnected. To record the transfer leg, configure recording on the transfer target's trunk or number separately.

chunks.title: SIP REFER
chunks.section: Frequently asked questions › Can I transfer the same call more than once?
chunks.text: Yes. You can send successive REFER requests on the same call. Each REFER replaces the current transfer leg with a new one.

chunks.title: SIP REFER
chunks.section: Frequently asked questions › Does REFER work alongside Plivo's IVR or PHLO?
chunks.text: SIP REFER is initiated by your SIP endpoint, not by Plivo. If your endpoint is connected via a Plivo SIP trunk (inbound or outbound), you can send REFER regardless of what IVR or PHLO flow was used to route the call.

chunks.title: SIP REFER
chunks.section: Frequently asked questions › What countries and number formats are supported as transfer targets?
chunks.text: The transfer target must be a valid E.164 number (for example, `+14155551234`) reachable via your SIP trunk. International destinations must be enabled on your account. See [Geo Permissions](/docs/sip-trunking/concepts/geo-permissions) to manage which countries your trunk can reach.

chunks.title: SIP REFER
chunks.section: Frequently asked questions › What happens if the transfer target is busy or does not answer?
chunks.text: Plivo sends `NOTIFY 4xx` (for example, `486 Busy Here` or `408 Request Timeout`) to your endpoint. The caller remains on your line. You can retry the REFER with a different number or continue the conversation.

chunks.title: SIP REFER
chunks.section: Frequently asked questions › Is there a limit on how many REFERs I can send?
chunks.text: REFERs count against your account's concurrent call capacity like any other call leg. See [Calls-per-second limitations](/docs/sip-trunking#calls-per-second-limitations) for details.

chunks.title: SIP REFER — Inbound Calls
chunks.text:
Transfer an inbound call from your SIP endpoint to a human agent or any phone number using SIP REFER

> [!NOTE]
>
> When your AI agent or PBX sends a SIP REFER, Plivo hands the caller off to the transfer target and disconnects your endpoint — the caller never re-dials. Use it for inbound call handoffs to a human agent.

Use this guide when **a caller dialled your Plivo number and your endpoint answered**, and you now want to transfer the call to another destination. For outbound call transfers, see [SIP REFER — Outbound Calls](/docs/sip-trunking/concepts/sip-refer-outbound).

chunks.title: SIP REFER — Inbound Calls
chunks.text:
| Requirement | Description |
| - | - |
| **Inbound SIP trunk** | An [inbound Plivo SIP trunk](https://cx.plivo.com/sip-trunking) with your SIP endpoint configured as the termination URI. |
| **Plivo phone number** | A Plivo number linked to your inbound trunk so calls route to your endpoint. |
| **REFER-capable endpoint** | Your SIP endpoint (PBX, softphone, AI agent) must support sending SIP REFER requests. |
| **Transfer destination** | A Plivo number or reachable E.164 number to transfer the caller to. |

chunks.title: SIP REFER — Inbound Calls
chunks.text:
```mermaid theme={null}
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Customer
    participant Z as Plivo (SIP Trunk)
    participant E as Your Endpoint
    participant T as Transfer Target
    C->>Z: (1) INVITE
    Z->>E: (1) INVITE
    E-->>Z: (1) 200 OK
    Z-->>C: (1) 200 OK
    Note over C,E: Call established — customer talking to endpoint
    E->>Z: (2) REFER (Refer-To: Transfer Target)
    Z-->>E: (3) 202 Accepted
    Z-->>E: (3) NOTIFY 100 Trying
    Z->>T: (4) INVITE
    T-->>Z: (4) 180 Ringing
    Z-->>E: (4) NOTIFY 180
    T-->>Z: (5) 200 OK
    Z-->>E: (5) NOTIFY 200 OK
    Z->>E: (6) BYE
    Note over C,T: Customer and Transfer Target connected
```

| Step | What happens |
| - | - |
| **(1) Call established** | The customer dials your Plivo number. Plivo routes the call to your SIP endpoint. Your endpoint answers. |
| **(2) REFER** | Your endpoint sends REFER with the transfer target's number in the `Refer-To` header. |
| **(3) Accepted** | Plivo responds `202 Accepted` and sends `NOTIFY 100 Trying`. |
| **(4) New leg** | Plivo places a new call to the transfer target. |
| **(5) Connected** | Transfer target answers. Plivo sends `NOTIFY 200 OK`. |
| **(6) BYE** | Plivo disconnects your endpoint. Customer and transfer target continue the call. |

chunks.title: SIP REFER — Inbound Calls
chunks.section: Step-by-step guide › Step 1: Set up your inbound trunk
chunks.text:
1. Go to [cx.plivo.com/sip-trunking](https://cx.plivo.com/sip-trunking) → **Inbound Trunks**
2. Create or select an inbound trunk and set your SIP endpoint as the **Primary URI**
3. Assign a Plivo number to the trunk — go to the trunk → **Phone Numbers** → link a number

chunks.title: SIP REFER — Inbound Calls
chunks.section: Step-by-step guide › Step 2: Answer the inbound call
chunks.text: When a customer dials your Plivo number, Plivo sends an INVITE to your SIP endpoint URI. Your endpoint responds `200 OK` to answer.

chunks.title: SIP REFER — Inbound Calls
chunks.section: Step-by-step guide › Step 3: Send the REFER
chunks.text:
When ready to hand off, send a REFER with the transfer target in the `Refer-To` header.

**Refer-To header format:**

```text theme={null}
Refer-To: <sip:+14155551234@XXXXXXXXXXXX.zt.plivo.com>
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> Use your **SIP trunk domain** in the `Refer-To` header (ending in `.zt.plivo.com`). Transfers to other domains or arbitrary SIP URIs are blocked.

**Example REFER message:**

```sip theme={null}
REFER sip:trunk@XXXXXXXXXXXX.zt.plivo.com SIP/2.0
Via: SIP/2.0/UDP 192.168.1.100:5060;branch=z9hG4bK-524287-1
From: <sip:endpoint@pbx.example.com>;tag=12345
To: <sip:trunk@XXXXXXXXXXXX.zt.plivo.com>;tag=67890
Call-ID: 1-12345@192.168.1.100
CSeq: 1 REFER
Contact: <sip:endpoint@192.168.1.100:5060>
Refer-To: <sip:+14155551234@XXXXXXXXXXXX.zt.plivo.com>
Max-Forwards: 70
Content-Length: 0
```

chunks.title: SIP REFER — Inbound Calls
chunks.section: Step-by-step guide › Step 4: Handle NOTIFY messages
chunks.text:
After `202 Accepted`, Plivo sends NOTIFY messages to report transfer progress. Your endpoint must respond to each NOTIFY with `200 OK`.

| NOTIFY status | Meaning | What to do |
| - | - | - |
| `SIP/2.0 100 Trying` | Plivo is calling the transfer target | Show "Transferring…" in your UI. Keep the call active. |
| `SIP/2.0 180 Ringing` | Transfer target is ringing | Optionally relay ring-back tone to the caller. |
| `SIP/2.0 200 OK` | Caller and target are connected | You may hang up your leg (or wait for Plivo's BYE). |
| `SIP/2.0 4xx` / `5xx` | Transfer failed | Caller is still on your line — retry or continue the call. |

> [!WARNING]
>
> Do not send BYE before receiving `NOTIFY 200 OK`. Sending BYE early drops the caller before the transfer completes.

chunks.title: SIP REFER — Inbound Calls
chunks.section: Step-by-step guide › Step 5: Call continues between customer and transfer target
chunks.text: Plivo bridges the caller to the transfer target and sends your endpoint a BYE. The original caller's number is preserved as the caller ID presented to the transfer target.

chunks.title: SIP REFER — Inbound Calls
chunks.text:
* **Caller ID preserved:** The transfer target sees the original caller's number, not your endpoint's SIP URI.
* **During the transfer:** The caller hears ring-back from the transfer target (180 Ringing) until the target answers.
* **If the transfer fails:** The caller remains on your leg. You can retry with a different number or continue the conversation.
* **Music on hold:** To play hold music while the transfer leg is establishing, play audio from your endpoint before sending REFER.

chunks.title: SIP REFER — Inbound Calls
chunks.text:
| Code | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `202 Accepted` | REFER accepted — transfer is in progress |
| `400 Bad Request` | Missing or malformed `Refer-To` header |
| `403 Forbidden` | `Refer-To` domain is not a valid Plivo SIP trunk domain, or transfer target is a private IP |

chunks.title: SIP REFER — Inbound Calls
chunks.text:
| Symptom | Check |
| - | - |
| **403 Forbidden** | Verify the `Refer-To` domain ends in `.zt.plivo.com`. Ensure the target is not a private IP. |
| **400 Bad Request** | Verify the `Refer-To` header uses E.164 format: `sip:+14155551234@trunk.zt.plivo.com`. |
| **202 Accepted but caller is dropped** | Your endpoint sent BYE before receiving `NOTIFY 200 OK`. Wait for `NOTIFY 200 OK` first. |
| **202 Accepted but no NOTIFY received** | Ensure your endpoint listens on the same IP/port it advertised in the `Contact` header. |
| **Transfer fails (NOTIFY 4xx/5xx)** | Check that the destination is valid, reachable, and not busy. Verify account balance. |
| **Transfer to international number returns 403** | Enable that destination under [Geo Permissions](/docs/sip-trunking/concepts/geo-permissions). |
| **No audio after transfer** | Codec mismatch between legs. Contact [Plivo Support](https://support.plivo.com) with the `Call-ID`. |
| **Transfer target sees wrong caller ID** | For inbound transfers, the original caller's number is always passed as caller ID — this is expected behaviour. |

```mermaid theme={null}
    Z->>E: (6) BYE
    Note over C,T: Customer and Transfer Target connected
```
