chunks.title: 160-Series Numbers
chunks.text:
Setup guide for BFSI entities to provision 160-series numbers for transactional and service voice communications in India

> [!NOTE]
>
> * **What:** 160-series numbers are TRAI-regulated for BFSI transactional and service voice calls in India.
> * **You must:** Register on Tata DLT and complete Plivo's header and template provisioning.
> * **If you don't:** Using them for promotional calls leads to disconnection and penalties.

chunks.title: 160-Series Numbers
chunks.text: 160-series numbers are ten-digit telephone numbers designated by the Indian Department of Telecommunications for transactional and service voice communications by regulated BFSI entities.

chunks.title: 160-Series Numbers
chunks.text:
160-series numbers are for transactional or service-related communication only. **Do not use them for marketing or promotional purposes.**

Acceptable use cases:

* Payment reminders and transaction notifications
* Account statements and balance updates
* Service alerts and system notifications related to subscribed services
* Authentication, alerts, customer support, regulatory communication, and service calls

chunks.title: 160-Series Numbers
chunks.text:
160-series numbers are allocated only to BFSI (Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance) entities that hold a valid licence or registration from a recognized financial regulator. You declare the regulator and licence number on the BFSI Customer Application Form.

| Entity Type | Governing regulator | Examples |
| - | - | - |
| Bank | RBI | Commercial banks, cooperative banks, small finance banks |
| NBFC | RBI | Non-banking financial companies |
| Insurance | IRDAI | Life, general, and health insurance providers |
| Mutual Fund / Asset Manager | SEBI | Asset management companies, mutual fund distributors |
| Payment Aggregator | RBI | Payment service providers and aggregators authorized under the PA/PG framework |
| Pension Fund | PFRDA | Pension fund managers, NPS intermediaries |
| Fintech | RBI / SEBI / IRDAI (as applicable) | Regulated financial technology businesses |
| Other BFSI | Specify regulator on the form | Other regulated financial entities (specify in the BFSI Customer Application Form) |

chunks.title: 160-Series Numbers
chunks.text:
| Role | Who it is | Responsibilities |
| - | - | - |
| Access Service Provider (VNO) | **Plivo** | Allocates the 160-series number and issues the NOC to the TM. Plivo is **neither** the PE nor the TM |
| Principal Entity (PE) | The BFSI business | Holds the regulatory licence, registers as PE on Tata DLT, owns the content templates, signs the BFSI Customer Application Form |
| Telemarketer (TM) | The entity placing the call | Holds the Tata DLT TM ID, signs the Aggregator Telemarketer Declaration, approves the Voice Header in Partner-Managed setups |

chunks.title: 160-Series Numbers
chunks.section: Roles in 160-Series Provisioning › Self-Managed vs Partner-Managed
chunks.text:
There are two possibilities depending on who places the calls:

| Setup | Description | Example |
| - | - | - |
| **Self-Managed** | The PE and TM are the **same legal entity**. The BFSI business that owns the campaign also makes the calls | A bank running its own transactional alerts and OTP calls |
| **Partner-Managed** | The PE and TM are **different entities**. A third party makes calls on behalf of the BFSI business | A contact-center provider placing OTP and reminder calls on behalf of a bank |

Both setups use the same steps below; the difference shows up during registration.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **TM registration location.** Plivo currently accepts 160-series provisioning only when the **TM entity is registered in Mumbai or Karnataka**. Entities registered elsewhere are not supported today.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **DLT operator support.** Plivo currently provisions 140 and 160-series numbers exclusively through Tata Teleservices and is in the process of onboarding additional service providers. Entities registered on other DLT platforms (Airtel, Vi, BSNL) are not supported today.

chunks.title: 160-Series Numbers
chunks.text:
| Requirement | Details |
| - | - |
| Plivo account | Active Plivo India account |
| Regulatory licence | Valid licence or registration number from your governing regulator (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA, or equivalent) |
| Tata DLT registration | PE registered on the [Tata DLT portal](https://telemarketer.tatateleservices.com/#/tmpe-common-registration-01). In Partner-Managed, the TM is registered separately; in Self-Managed, the same entity registers as both PE and TM |

The [BFSI Customer Application Form](https://www.plivo.com/downloads/Plivo_BFSI_Customer_Application_Form.docx) and the [Aggregator Telemarketer Declaration](https://www.plivo.com/downloads/Plivo_Aggregator_Telemarketer_Declaration.docx) are collected by Plivo during Step 2 below — no separate Plivo KYC is required.

chunks.title: 160-Series Numbers
chunks.section: Provisioning Process › Step 1: Tata DLT Registration
chunks.text:
**Who:** PE (and TM, if different)

Register on the [Tata Teleservices DLT portal](https://telemarketer.tatateleservices.com/#/tmpe-common-registration-01):

| Setup | What to register |
| - | - |
| Self-Managed | Register the same legal entity as both PE and TM |
| Partner-Managed | PE registers as PE; TM registers separately as TM |

Tata emails the approved PE certificate (and TM certificate where applicable) to the registered email IDs.

chunks.title: 160-Series Numbers
chunks.section: Provisioning Process › Step 2: Submit Forms to Plivo
chunks.text:
**Who:** PE and TM (you, or your partner)

1. Download the [BFSI Customer Application Form](https://www.plivo.com/downloads/Plivo_BFSI_Customer_Application_Form.docx) and the [Aggregator Telemarketer Declaration](https://www.plivo.com/downloads/Plivo_Aggregator_Telemarketer_Declaration.docx).
2. Fill in all fields. The BFSI form captures the PE's regulatory category, governing regulator, licence number, DLT registration ID, and chosen setup (Self-Managed or Partner-Managed). The TM declaration captures the TM's PAN, CIN, Tata DLT TM ID, and the PE relationship.
3. The PE signs and seals the BFSI form; the TM signs and seals the TM Declaration. In Self-Managed, the same legal entity signs both forms in its respective PE and TM capacities.
4. Submit both forms to Plivo by **emailing them to your Account Manager or raising a [Plivo Support](https://support.plivo.com) ticket** with the forms attached.

chunks.title: 160-Series Numbers
chunks.section: Provisioning Process › Step 3: Plivo Allocates the Number and Issues the NOC
chunks.text:
**Who:** Plivo

After Plivo validates both forms:

1. Plivo allocates a 160-series number to your account.
2. Plivo issues a No Objection Certificate (NOC) to the TM by replying to the same email or support ticket where the forms were shared. Plivo issues a separate NOC for **each** number procured.

chunks.title: 160-Series Numbers
chunks.section: Provisioning Process › Step 4: Voice Header Registration
chunks.text:
**Who:** PE (always — in Self-Managed, log in with your PE persona on Tata DLT)

The PE logs into the [Tata DLT portal](https://telemarketer.tatateleservices.com/#/tmpe-common-login) and submits the Voice Header registration with these fields:

![Voice Header registration by PE](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/F_qF380XLyDRnOHd/images/160-voice-header-registration.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=F_qF380XLyDRnOHd&q=85&s=fa0b1d56ab5377266701845b9a8f2040)

| Field | Value |
| - | - |
| Entity ID | Your PE ID |
| Header CLI | The 160-series number allocated by Plivo |
| Business Category | The BFSI category that matches your business on the Tata DLT portal |
| Supporting documents | Upload your business-category certificate from the governing regulator and the Plivo NOC for this number |
| Remarks and Purpose | State the transactional or service purpose of the calls |

During registration, the portal asks whether the PE and TM are the same entity:

| Setup | What to select |
| - | - |
| Self-Managed (PE = TM) | Select **PE and TM are the same** |
| Partner-Managed (PE ≠ TM) | Select **PE and TM are different** and enter the TM's Entity ID |

![Self-Managed selector](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/F_qF380XLyDRnOHd/images/160-self-managed-option.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=F_qF380XLyDRnOHd&q=85&s=a736cc7023f9d91883d6da1a7874ef32)

![Partner-Managed selector](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/F_qF380XLyDRnOHd/images/160-partner-managed-option.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=F_qF380XLyDRnOHd&q=85&s=6bf97963eb10ee24f5dfed0fd10de889)

After submission, the portal generates a Unique Registration Number (URN) for the Voice Header. In Partner-Managed, share this URN with the TM so they can locate and approve the request.

![URN generated](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/F_qF380XLyDRnOHd/images/160-urn-generated.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=F_qF380XLyDRnOHd&q=85&s=0f44c9a927292ab0370a2139c8dc2fa1)

chunks.title: 160-Series Numbers
chunks.section: Provisioning Process › Step 5: Voice Header Approval by TM (Partner-Managed only)
chunks.text:
**Who:** TM — **skip this step in Self-Managed**

In Self-Managed, the Voice Header proceeds directly to Tata review. In Partner-Managed, the TM logs into the [Tata DLT portal](https://telemarketer.tatateleservices.com/#/tmpe-common-login), opens the pending Voice Header using the URN shared by the PE, and approves it.

The TM goes to **Voice Header Registration List For TM** and reviews the pending request.

![Voice Header registration list for TM](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/F_qF380XLyDRnOHd/images/160-voice-header-list-tm.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=F_qF380XLyDRnOHd&q=85&s=fc020848730bed204ce5e7dc579be027)

The TM then accepts or rejects the request.

![TM accept or reject](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/F_qF380XLyDRnOHd/images/160-tm-accept-reject.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=F_qF380XLyDRnOHd&q=85&s=465a2b8ee0854af63f13512053b92d33)

Tata's DLT team reviews and approves the Voice Header within 3–5 business days. You receive an email once the header is approved.

chunks.title: 160-Series Numbers
chunks.section: Provisioning Process › Step 6: Voice Template Registration
chunks.text:
**Who:** PE

The PE logs into the [Tata DLT portal](https://telemarketer.tatateleservices.com/#/tmpe-common-login) and goes to **Voice** > **Voice Template Registration by PE**. Register a Voice Content Template for each message type you intend to send (for example, payment reminders, OTP delivery, transaction confirmations).

![Voice template registration](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/F_qF380XLyDRnOHd/images/160-voice-template-registration.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=F_qF380XLyDRnOHd&q=85&s=c94d60b673ff5076660871420b4585c0)

Each template defines the exact messages transmitted using the 160-series number. Once templates are approved, the number is ready for live operations.

chunks.title: 160-Series Numbers
chunks.text:
| Step | Duration |
| - | - |
| Tata DLT registration | 2–3 business days |
| Plivo number allocation and NOC issuance | 1–2 business days after form submission |
| Voice Header approval by Tata | 3–5 business days |
| Voice Template approval by Tata | 1–2 business days |
| **Total** | **\~7–14 business days** |

chunks.text: Yes. Plivo issues a separate NOC for each number procured. Upload the relevant NOC during Voice Header registration on the Tata DLT portal.

You receive notification via the DLT portal with the reason for rejection. Common reasons:

Review the reason, correct the issue, and resubmit.

chunks.title: Account and feature limits
chunks.text:
CPS, concurrency, API rate limits, and feature limits for the Voice API in the India and US data regions

> [!NOTE]
>
> * **What:** How many calls your account can have active at once, how fast you can start them, and the API and feature ceilings.
> * **When:** Check before scaling call volume, or when calls fail with `Concurrency Limit Breached`.

Your account has two call capacity limits, and both apply at the same time. **CPS (calls per second)** caps how fast you can start new calls. **Concurrency** caps how many calls can be active at once. Both limits are account-wide: Voice API and SIP Trunking draw on the same pool, not a separate allowance per product.

chunks.title: Account and feature limits
chunks.text:
Your limits depend on your data region and, in the US data region, on your plan and lifetime spend.

| Data region | Plan / lifetime voice + SIP Trunking spend | Outbound CPS | Concurrent calls |
| - | - | - | - |
| India data region | Professional | 2 (default) | 50 (default) |
| India data region | Enterprise | Set by your contract | Set by your contract |
| US data region | Free Tier — before your first payment | 1 | 2 |
| US data region | Professional — less than USD 100 | 1 | 5 |
| US data region | Professional — USD 100 to USD 500 | 2 | 10 |
| US data region | Professional — more than USD 500 | 2 | 25 |
| US data region | Enterprise | 2 | 50 |

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Outbound CPS and concurrency are single account-wide pools shared by Voice API and SIP Trunking.** An account with 2 outbound CPS can start two outbound calls per second in total, whichever product they go out on. An account with 50 concurrent calls can hold 50 calls in total across both products.

Free Tier is not a plan you select. Every US data region account starts there and moves to Professional on its first payment.

US data region accounts created before October 1, 2026 are not on the plan-based limits in the table. They have custom limits, set per account based on usage.

In the India data region, Plivo sells capacity as concurrency. Professional accounts start at 50 concurrent calls. Enterprise accounts purchase the concurrency they need, and the limit and its price are set by the contract. Your CPS is set from your concurrency limit, so when your concurrency limit changes, your CPS changes with it. Calls in the India data region are billed at a 30-second pulse; see [billing increments](/docs/faq/billing-and-invoices/billing-concepts).

**Inbound CPS is a separate limit.** Every account can accept 10 inbound calls per second by default, in every data region, and this is not affected by the table above. See [Inbound CPS](#inbound-cps).

chunks.title: Account and feature limits
chunks.section: What counts toward your concurrency limit
chunks.text:
Concurrency is the number of active calls on your account at any point in time, including calls that are still being set up.

| Call state | Counted? |
| - | - |
| **Ringing / connecting** — call initiated, still in setup | Yes |
| **Connected / in progress** — call is live | Yes |
| **Completed / ended** — call has been disconnected | No |

Every PSTN call leg counts, inbound and outbound, across Voice API and SIP Trunking. A call that starts from a [Browser SDK](/docs/voice/sdk/browser/overview) (WebRTC) or SIP endpoint counts once it is connected to the PSTN: the PSTN leg counts, the SIP leg itself does not. SIP-to-SIP calls and WhatsApp calls do not count toward your account concurrency limit.

chunks.title: Account and feature limits
chunks.section: What counts toward your concurrency limit › India data region: 140-series and 160-series numbers
chunks.text: Calls placed from [140-series](/docs/voice/concepts/140-series-provisioning) and [160-series](/docs/voice/concepts/160-series-provisioning) numbers draw on a separate concurrency allocation for that series, not on your account concurrency limit. Calls from your other numbers are not affected when a series limit is reached. When a series limit is reached, a Make a Call API request fails with HTTP status `403` and the error `Series Concurrency Limit Breached for 91160` (or `91140`), and a call dropped at dial time carries hangup cause `5030`. Plivo sets the 140-series and 160-series allocation on your account when you provision those numbers. To check or change it, ask **Buddy**, Plivo's in-console chat agent, under **Organization settings > Account limits** in the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/organization-settings/limits), or contact your account manager.

chunks.title: Account and feature limits
chunks.section: What happens when you exceed a limit
chunks.text:
The two products behave differently above CPS and the same above concurrency.

| Limit | Voice API | SIP Trunking |
| - | - | - |
| **Above your outbound CPS** | **Queued.** The request is accepted and dialed as your rate drops | **Rejected immediately** with hangup cause `5180` (`cps_limit_reached`) |
| **Above your concurrency limit** | **Rejected immediately** with hangup cause `5030` (`Concurrency Limit Breached`) | **Rejected immediately** with hangup cause `5190` (`concurrent_call_limit_exceeded`) |

> [!WARNING]
>
> Concurrency never queues. A rejected call fails instantly — no ring, no connection, no grace period. As soon as active calls drop below your limit, new calls are accepted again.

chunks.title: Account and feature limits
chunks.section: What happens when you exceed a limit › What you see when you are already at the limit

chunks.title: Account and feature limits
chunks.section: What happens when you exceed a limit › Concurrency alert emails
chunks.text: When calls are rejected for a concurrency breach, Plivo emails your account owner with the time window, the limit that was reached, and what to do next. Plivo sends at most one alert every 24 hours per limit.

chunks.title: Account and feature limits
chunks.text:
1. To see your current concurrency limit, go to **Organization settings > Account limits** in the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/organization-settings/limits).
2. To see your usage, go to **Logs > Voice > Export > Export Concurrency Data**. The export gives minute-level concurrent call data for up to 30 days.

The export counts every concurrent call on your account: Voice API and SIP Trunking, inbound and outbound.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Rule of thumb:** if your 30-day peak exceeds 80% of your limit, review your capacity before you start seeing failures. Stagger bulk campaigns rather than launching them at once, and retry after a short delay when a call is rejected.

chunks.title: Account and feature limits
chunks.text:
| Data region | How limits change |
| - | - |
| India data region | Higher concurrency is available on an Enterprise plan, in the amount your contract allows. Click **Request Enterprise** under **Organization settings > Account limits** in the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/organization-settings/limits), ask **Buddy**, Plivo's in-console chat agent, or contact your account manager |
| US data region | Limits rise automatically within 24 hours as your lifetime voice and SIP Trunking spend crosses a tier. For more than your tier allows, click **Request Enterprise** under **Organization settings > Account limits** in the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/organization-settings/limits), ask **Buddy**, or contact your account manager |

chunks.title: Account and feature limits
chunks.text:
Inbound CPS covers inbound calls to your Plivo numbers and outbound calls started from SIP and Browser SDK endpoints. Plivo treats both as inbound requests to the platform. The default inbound CPS is 10 per account. Calls above the inbound CPS are rejected, not queued.

| Scenario | Outbound SIP/browser calls in one second | Inbound calls to Plivo numbers in one second | Processed | Rejected |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| 1 | 11 | 0 | 10 | 1 |
| 2 | 0 | 11 | 10 | 1 |
| 3 | 5 | 6 | 10 | 1 |

chunks.title: Account and feature limits
chunks.text:
Plivo limits all accounts to 300 API requests per five seconds. The limit applies separately to call-initiating APIs and to all other APIs:

* **Call-initiating APIs:** Make an Outbound Call, and Add a Participant to a multiparty call
* **Non-call APIs:** all other Call APIs, Recording APIs, Conference APIs, Endpoint APIs, and Application APIs

If you send more requests than the limit allows, Plivo blocks the requests and responds with the HTTP error *429 Too Many Requests*. If you see this error, throttle your API requests and retry.

Higher API rate limits are available on an Enterprise plan. To request them, ask **Buddy**, Plivo's in-console chat agent, in the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/home).

chunks.title: Account and feature limits
chunks.text: In addition to the account-level limits, Plivo has some feature-level limits.

chunks.title: Account and feature limits
chunks.section: Feature-level limits › Time limit for calls
chunks.text: The default maximum duration for outbound and inbound calls connected using [Make a Call API](/docs/voice/api/calls/#make-a-call) and [Dial XML](/docs/voice/xml/routing#dial) is four hours starting from the time a call is answered. You can extend the limit to 86,400 seconds (24 hours).

chunks.title: Account and feature limits
chunks.text: By default, the maximum duration for call recordings is 60 seconds. For calls that you record using [Record API](/docs/voice/api/recordings) or [Record XML](/docs/voice/xml/record/), the maximum recording duration is 24 hours.

chunks.title: Account and feature limits
chunks.text:
Two limits have to do with conference calls.

* **Participants**: You can have a maximum of 20 participants in a conference room. You can set the maxMembers to be between 1 to 20.
* **Duration**: The maximum duration for a conference is 86,400 seconds (24 hours). A conference call will get disconnected after 24 hours.

Refer to the [Conference XML element](/docs/voice/xml/conference/) reference page for details.

chunks.title: Account and feature limits
chunks.text:
You can transcribe a call using the [Record API](/docs/voice/api/recordings), [Record Conference API](/docs/voice/api/recordings), [Record XML](/docs/voice/xml/record/), and [Conference XML](/docs/voice/xml/conference/).

* **Duration**: Our transcription service is limited to calls with a duration greater than 5 seconds and less than four hours.
* **Recording file size**: The maximum recording file size is 2GB.

chunks.title: Account and feature limits
chunks.section: Feature-level limits › Abandoned and short-duration call thresholds
chunks.text:
Plivo enforces monthly limits on the proportion of abandoned and short-duration calls in your traffic. When the percentage of these calls exceeds the threshold, a per-call surcharge applies to the excess calls.

| Call type | Monthly threshold | Surcharge on excess calls |
| - | - | - |
| Abandoned calls (0 seconds) | 20% | USD 0.005 per excess call |
| Short calls (≤6 seconds) | 10% | USD 0.015 per excess call |

These limits apply to both Voice API and SIP Trunking calls. For guidance on CPS rates and pacing your traffic within your CPS limit, see Outbound Call Quality and CPS in the US ([audio streaming](/docs/voice-agents/audio-streaming/deploy/us-call-quality-and-cps), [SIP trunking](/docs/voice-agents/sip-trunking/deploy/us-call-quality-and-cps)).

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Calls to India are excluded** from these thresholds and surcharges. The 20% limit and per-call charges apply only to non-India destinations.

chunks.title: Callback Configurations
chunks.text:
Configure webhook URLs and HTTP methods for voice call event notifications

> [!NOTE]
>
> * **What:** Configure webhook timeout, retry policy, and edge region for Plivo voice callbacks.
> * **How:** Append URL fragments to your callback URLs. Applies to callback URLs only, not audio URLs.

Plivo sends HTTP webhooks as callbacks during different states of a call and to many URLs, such as answer_url, fallback_url, hangup_url, action, and callback_url. To enable users to optimize for lower latency and build fault tolerance into webhook interactions, Plivo offers optional parameters that let developers configure timeouts (the timeframe Plivo has to wait to receive a response from your application server), retry policy, and edge region from which the webhook request is sent to the URL. Regions correspond to Plivo points of presence (PoP). See [SIP Trunking FAQ](/docs/sip-trunking#data-centers) for details on Plivo's global data center locations.

chunks.title: Callback Configurations
chunks.text:
Having the ability to configure callback retries and timeouts improves reliability and event recovery by letting you:

* Configure a custom timeout based on your use case.
* Set higher timeouts during network problems on your application server.
* Set shorter timeouts during an outage on your application server to ensure faster failover to your fallback URL.
* Enable retries during client-side service interruptions and delays.

chunks.title: Callback Configurations
chunks.text:
To set callback configurations for any given URL (answer_url, fallback_url, , ring_url, etc.), you need to append configuration parameters to it in the form of URL extensions (or ”[fragments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fragment_identifier)”) as key-value pairs.

* The first key-value pair should start with #
* Key and value should be separated by =
* Key-value pairs should be separated by &

For example:

```url theme={null}
https://example.com/answer_url?query=123#param1=2500&param2=5500
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Note:** If you don’t append any parameters, the default values from the tables below will apply.

chunks.title: Callback Configurations
chunks.text:
When Plivo sends an HTTP callback to your webhook URLs during events, you should capture the request (POST or GET based on the type you’ve defined for the URL) and respond with a 200 OK response. When you process the callback, you can store the data in your database.

Plivo automatically retries webhooks for a certain timeframe if an HTTP 200 status code is not returned. The timeframe Plivo has to wait to receive a response from your application server is called a timeout. This table shows the allowed and default timeouts available for webhook URLs.

| Parameter | Name | Description | Allowed Values | Default |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| ct | Connection timeout | The time in milliseconds (ms) for Plivo to wait while establishing a TCP connection | 100 – 10000 | 2000 |
| rt | Read timeout | The time in milliseconds for Plivo to wait: — to start receiving a response after sending the initial request — for delay between packets | 100 – 40000 | 40000 |
| tt | Total timeout | Upper limit on total time allowed for all timeouts, including retries on a given URL (not including fallback URL) | 100 – 55000 | 55000 |

chunks.title: Callback Configurations
chunks.text:
1. [https://example.com/answer_url?query=123#ct=2000](https://example.com/answer_url?query=123#ct=2000)\
   *Connection timeout of two seconds*

2. [https://example.com/answer_url?query=123#ct=2000&rt=3000](https://example.com/answer_url?query=123#ct=2000&rt=3000)\
   *Connection timeout of two seconds and a read timeout of three seconds*

chunks.title: Callback Configurations
chunks.text:
Plivo lets you configure the number of retries it makes for different webhook URLs and the policy it should use depending on HTTP failure status codes.

| Param | Name | Description | Allowed Values | Default |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| rc | Retry count | Number of retry attempts to be made to the same URL if the initial connection fails (not including to fallback URL) | 0 – 5 | 1 |
| rp | Retry policy | Type of failure to retry on: **4xx** → only on 4xx responses **5xx** → only on 5xx responses **ct** → TCP/TLS connection failures within the connection timeout **rt** → no response received within the read timeout **all** → all the above | Comma-separated list of values — for example, rp=ct,rt | ct,rt |

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Note:** If a partial response is received from your app server, Plivo will not make a retry attempt.

chunks.title: Callback Configurations
chunks.text:
1. [https://example.com/answer_url?query=123#rt=3000&rp=ct,rt](https://example.com/answer_url?query=123#rt=3000&rp=ct,rt)\
   *Retry on both connect and read timeout, and reduce the read timeout to three seconds.*

2. [https://example.com/answer_url?query=123#rc=3&ct=2000](https://example.com/answer_url?query=123#rc=3&ct=2000)\
   *Retry on connection failure, but with a two-second connection timeout. If there is no connection in two seconds, retry three times, for a total of four attempts to connect.*

chunks.title: Callback Configurations
chunks.text:
An edge region is the geographical region from which Plivo initiates an HTTP webhook to the answer_url, fallback_url, hangup_url, action, or callback_url URLs. Plivo maintains edge clusters in four regions: * North California (United states) * North Virginia (United States) * Frankfurt (Germany) * Singapore * Mumbai (India) To ensure minimum latency, Plivo automatically chooses the nearest region for all callbacks we initiate, but developers can configure the region for each URL using the `er` parameter: | Param | Name | Description | Allowed Values | Default | | - | - | - | - | - | | er | Edge Region | Specifies the edge region where webhooks get initiated from. This parameter needs to be either a selection strategy or a specific region. Region Selection Strategies: **nearest** → selects the region geographically closest to the location of the URL. **local** → selects the same region as the media server where the call media is hosted. Specific region: n_california, n_virginia, frankfurt, singapore, mumbai |
  • nearest
  • local
  • n_california
  • n_virginia
  • frankfurt
  • singapore
  • mumbai
| nearest |

chunks.title: Callback Configurations
chunks.text:
1. [https://example.com/answer_url?query=123#er=n_california](https://example.com/answer_url?query=123#er=n_california)\
   *The HTTP webhook to this URL from Plivo will be initiated from Plivo’s North California edge region.*

2. [https://example.com/answer_url?query=123#er=nearest](https://example.com/answer_url?query=123#er=nearest)\
   *The HTTP webhook to this URL from Plivo will be initiated from the Plivo’s edge region that is nearest to the location of the URL.*

chunks.title: Voice callbacks
chunks.text:
Voice API callback parameters and payload reference for call events

> [!NOTE]
>
> * **What:** Reference for the webhook payloads Plivo sends during call events — ring, answer, hangup, recording, and more.
> * **When:** Use it to build your webhook handlers. Validate requests and handle possible duplicate callbacks idempotently.

Plivo makes HTTP requests to webhooks during different states of a voice call. These callbacks can help you analyze the call statuses of an ongoing call and manage call flow based on the values you receive from callback events.

Webhooks are user-defined event-based HTTP callbacks that operate based on the concept of event reaction. They’re a helpful tool to use when you want to create instant and real-time notifications.

Plivo uses webhooks to make it possible to track the status of your voice calls. For every outbound and inbound call, Plivo sends a status update to a URL you configure for receiving callback events. You can read and store the information on your server for call reporting analysis.

When a webhook is triggered by an event, Plivo makes an HTTP request (POST or GET) to the endpoint URL configured for the webhook. To handle a webhook, you must create a listener (web application) that can accept these HTTP requests.

![Call Status related Webhooks](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/EvRfP72Bjs4tuRt5/images/callbacks.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=EvRfP72Bjs4tuRt5&q=85&s=7ea8cb8e18cefdc75cad48f777914f46)

chunks.title: Voice callbacks
chunks.text: For outbound calls from your web application, you can use callbacks to manage the call flow and receive status events on your application server. Plivo uses webhook callbacks in both Voice API and XML elements:

chunks.title: Voice callbacks
chunks.section: Webhooks for outbound calls › URLs specific to API request payload
chunks.text:
Webhook parameters associated with a Voice API outbound call payload are answer_url, ring_url, fallback_url, and hangup_url. answer_url is a mandatory parameter for outbound API calls; the others are optional. You can configure unique webhook URLs and set the method as either POST or GET to receive call status-related callbacks during different events.

* **answer_url** : When a call is answered by the destination number, you can control the call flow with the help of the answer_url set in the API request. Plivo invokes the answer_url specified as soon as the call is answered and expects a valid XML response with instructions to handle the call. To see how this works, you can use [https://s3.amazonaws.com/static.plivo.com/answer.xml](https://s3.amazonaws.com/static.plivo.com/answer.xml) as answer_url to test your first outgoing call:

  ```xml theme={null}
    <Response>
    <Speak>Congratulations! You've made your first outbound call!</Speak>
    </Response>
  ```

  This XML snippet gives instructions to say, “Congratulations! You’ve made your first outbound call!” to the call recipient.

* **fallback_url** : Plivo can invoke this URL if answer_url is not reachable.

* **ring_url** : Plivo can notify this URL when the call starts ringing.

* **hangup_url** : Plivo can notify this URL when the call is disconnected.

Plivo can also send parameters with an HTTP request during other events of a call so your application can act to continue the call flow or to change it based on the values it receives. For information about the parameters Plivo sends to these URLs and the possible values they can contain, refer to the Callbacks section under [Make an outbound call](/docs/voice/api/calls/#make-a-call) in our Voice API Reference documentation.

chunks.title: Voice callbacks
chunks.section: Webhooks for outbound calls › URLs specific to XML response from the answer_url of outbound Call API
chunks.text:
The URLs most commonly associated with an XML response from the answer_url are action and callbackUrl.

* **action** : Plivo expects XML instructions to carry forward the call in response to action requests, which are typically invoked at the end of an XML element’s execution, such as when an IVR input is received from the caller during a GetInput XML execution.
* **callbackUrl** : No XML instructions are expected in response to these requests. They serve as webhooks to notify your application server of important events during the course of an XML element’s execution, such as when a conference participant is muted or unmuted.

For more information about the callback parameters sent to action and callbackUrl, refer to the XML elements sections in the XML reference documentation for elements such as [Conference](/docs/voice/xml/conference/), [Dial](/docs/voice/xml/routing#dial), [GetInput](/docs/voice/xml/input#getinput), and [GetDigits](/docs/voice/xml/input#getdigits).

chunks.title: Voice callbacks
chunks.text:
You can use webhooks with Plivo numbers to receive callbacks for incoming calls. When a voice-enabled Plivo phone number receives an incoming call, Plivo sends an HTTP request callback (either POST or GET depending on the method set for the webhook) to the URL specified in the application.

In the callback, all the information related to the inbound call is either in the POST request’s body or the GET request’s query parameters. Here are details about the URLs associated with an inbound call to a Plivo number:

chunks.title: Voice callbacks
chunks.section: Webhooks for inbound calls › URLs specific to the Plivo number’s Voice app
chunks.text:
The URLs associated with API payload are Primary Answer URL, Fallback Answer URL, and Hangup URL.

* **Primary Answer URL** is a mandatory field for a voice application assigned to a Plivo number; the other URLs are optional. You can configure these fields with unique webhook URLs and set the method as either POST or GET to receive call status-related callbacks during different events.
* **Fallback Answer URL** : Plivo invokes this URL if the Primary Answer URL is not reachable.
* **Hangup URL** is an optional URL that Plivo can notify when the call is disconnected.

For more information about the parameters you can send to these URLs and the possible values they can contain, refer to the [XML request section](/docs/voice/xml/overview#request-parameters) of our XML Reference documentation.

chunks.title: Voice callbacks
chunks.section: Webhooks for inbound calls › URLs specific to the XML response from the answer_url
chunks.text:
The URLs associated with the XML response from the answer_url are action and callbackUrl.

* **action** : XML instructions to carry forward the call are expected in response to these requests. These requests are typically invoked at the end of an XML element’s execution, such as when an IVR input is received from the caller during a GetInput XML execution.
* **callbackUrl** : No XML instructions are expected in response to these requests. Such requests serve as webhooks to notify your application server of important events during the course of an XML element’s execution, such as when a conference participant is muted or unmuted.

Check the [receive an incoming call guide](/docs/voice/use-cases/receive-incoming-calls) for more information about how to receive an incoming call on a voice-enabled Plivo phone number.

chunks.title: Voice callbacks
chunks.section: Handling callbacks in your web application
chunks.text:
To handle callbacks in your application, your endpoint should capture HTTP requests and respond to them.

When Plivo sends HTTP request callbacks to a webhook during an event, you should capture the request (POST or GET based on the type you’ve defined for the URL) and respond with a *200 OK* response. To process the callback, you can store the data in your database.

Plivo automatically retries webhooks for a certain timeframe if an HTTP 200 status code is not returned. Check the [Configurable Callback Retries guide](/docs/voice/concepts/callback-configurations/) for more information about callback timeouts and retries.

chunks.title: Voice callbacks
chunks.text: Plivo may send the same callback multiple times due to network issues or retries. Your application should handle duplicate callbacks gracefully.

chunks.title: Voice callbacks
chunks.text:
1. **Use CallUUID as idempotency key**: Each call has a unique `CallUUID`. Track processed callbacks by this ID.

2. **Store callback state**: Before processing, check if you've already handled this callback.

3. **Make operations idempotent**: Design your callback handlers so that processing the same callback twice has no additional effect.

chunks.title: Voice callbacks
chunks.text:
```python theme={null}
import redis
from flask import Flask, request

app = Flask(__name__)
redis_client = redis.Redis()

@app.route('/hangup', methods=['POST'])
def handle_hangup():
    call_uuid = request.form.get('CallUUID')

    # Check if already processed
    cache_key = f"callback:hangup:{call_uuid}"
    if redis_client.get(cache_key):
        return 'OK', 200  # Already processed, skip

    # Mark as processing (with TTL to auto-expire)
    redis_client.setex(cache_key, 86400, 'processed')

    # Process the callback
    save_call_record(call_uuid, request.form)

    return 'OK', 200
```

chunks.title: Voice callbacks
chunks.section: Handling duplicate callbacks (Idempotency) › Idempotency for Different Callback Types
chunks.text:
| Callback | Idempotency Key | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `hangup_url` | `CallUUID` | Call ended - safe to process once |
| `ring_url` | `CallUUID` | May fire multiple times for parallel dial |
| `action` URL | `CallUUID` + element context | Same action can be reached via retry |
| `recordingCallbackUrl` | `RecordingID` | Recording ready notification |
| `status_callback_url` (streams) | `StreamID` + event type | Stream status updates |

chunks.title: Voice callbacks
chunks.text: To avoid spoof attacks, you should validate the callbacks that your server URL receives. All requests made by Plivo to your server URLs include X-Plivo-Signature-V3, X-Plivo-Signature-Ma-V3, and X-Plivo-Signature-V3-Nonce HTTP headers. You can use these signatures to validate that the request is from Plivo. Read more about signature validation in our [Signature Validation guide](/docs/voice/concepts/signature-validation/).

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.text:
Register your business identity with US carriers to build trust and reduce spam flagging on outbound calls

> [!NOTE]
>
> * **What:** Register your US business with carriers so outbound calls display your business name instead of a spam flag.
> * **When:** Early-access beta, US numbers only. It reduces spam flagging but doesn't guarantee it.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Caller Reputation is currently in **early access beta** and available only for **US local and toll-free numbers**.

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.text:
Caller Reputation lets you register your business identity with major US carrier networks so your outbound calls from US local and toll-free numbers are recognized as legitimate. This reduces the chance your calls are flagged as spam or go unanswered.

Registration works in two steps, in this order:

1. **Register your business** on your Business Profile. Plivo submits your business details to each carrier network for vetting. Each network approves or rejects your business independently.
2. **Enable numbers** under that profile. Once at least one carrier network approves your business, numbers attach quickly — typically within hours.

When Caller Reputation is active on a number, calls from that number display your registered business name on supported devices.

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.text:
| Carrier key | Network | Status |
| - | - | - |
| `at&t` | AT&T | Supported |
| `t-mobile` | T-Mobile | Supported |
| `verizon` | Verizon | Not supported yet. Accepted in requests — if you pass it, its leg is reported as `NOT_SUPPORTED`, and the request never fails because of it |

API responses report each carrier network you registered with in `caller_reputation_by_carrier`. Omitting `caller_reputation_carriers` registers all supported networks (`at&t` and `t-mobile`); `verizon` appears only if you explicitly passed it.

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.text:
| Item | Detail |
| - | - |
| Current rates | **AT&T network: USD 12 per business per month. T-Mobile network: no charge currently.** Rates can change and can differ by carrier network, including for networks added later |
| Billing unit | Per **business** (one EIN/profile) — not per number. A business registered with both AT&T and T-Mobile today carries one monthly charge (the AT&T rate) |
| Multiple numbers | Numbers sharing the same business profile are covered under the same registration. Adding more numbers does not add charges |
| Multiple businesses | Each distinct business (EIN) on your account bills separately |
| When you're charged | Where a network carries a charge, it starts when that network **approves** your business. Registrations that fail validation or are not approved are **not** charged |
| Renewal | Recurring monthly. The charge is for the full month and is **not** prorated |
| Cancellation | Deregistering a carrier network (see [Deregister your business](#deregister-your-business)) stops that network's future billing. Mid-cycle cancellations are **not** refunded or prorated. Releasing numbers does **not** stop billing — the registration, and its charge, stay active until you deregister |
| Re-enabling | Registering again after you deregister creates a new registration — charges (where a network carries one) start again on approval |

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.text:
Before setting up Caller Reputation, you need:

* A Plivo account
* One or more US local or toll-free phone numbers rented through Plivo
* Your business details ready:
  * **EIN** (US-issued, 9 digits)
  * **Business address** (including a 2-character US state code)
  * **Business website**
  * **Contact information** (first name, last name, title, business email, and phone in E.164 format)

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.section: How to set up Caller Reputation › Step 1: Register your business
chunks.text:
Register your business on your Business Profile — the same profile used for 10DLC registration. You can register in either of two ways:

* **On an existing profile:** call the [Update Profile API](/docs/messaging/api/10dlc/profile#update-a-profile) with `enable_caller_reputation` set to `true`.
* **While creating a profile:** pass the same fields to the [Create Profile API](/docs/messaging/api/10dlc/profile#create-a-profile) to create the profile and register the business in a single call.

| Parameter | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `enable_caller_reputation` | Yes | Set to `true` to register your business |
| `caller_reputation_carriers` | No | Array of carrier networks to register with: `at&t`, `t-mobile`, `verizon`. Omit or pass an empty array to register with all supported networks (`at&t` and `t-mobile`). `verizon` is optional — pass it only if you want its `NOT_SUPPORTED` leg tracked in responses |
| `url` | No | One callback URL for all Caller Reputation events on this profile — business and number. See [Status callbacks](#status-callbacks) |
| `method` | No | `GET` or `POST` (default: `POST`) |

Plivo validates your profile synchronously — EIN (9 digits, US-issued), company name, full address, website, business email, and an authorized contact with an E.164 phone. If anything is missing, the API returns one `400` listing every failure, and nothing is submitted for vetting.

If validation passes, Plivo submits your business to each requested carrier network. Each network's status moves to `PENDING` and resolves independently to `APPROVED` or `FAILED` — one network's rejection never blocks another.

```json theme={null}
{
  "api_id": "d8f2869c-6879-11f1-aaed-a238457c948e",
  "profile": {
    "profile_uuid": "8444eccc-5af9-404d-a46f-d2fd31cd74de",
    "company_name": "Acme Software Inc",
    "enable_caller_reputation": true,
    "caller_reputation_status": "PENDING",
    "caller_reputation_by_carrier": {
      "at&t":     { "status": "PENDING", "reason_code": null, "reason": null, "updated_at": "2026-08-20T09:14:03Z" },
      "t-mobile": { "status": "PENDING", "reason_code": null, "reason": null, "updated_at": "2026-08-20T09:14:03Z" },
      "verizon":  { "status": "NOT_SUPPORTED", "reason_code": "CARRIER_NOT_SUPPORTED", "reason": "Verizon is not currently supported for Caller Reputation on Plivo.", "updated_at": null }
    },
    "caller_reputation_updated_at": "2026-08-20T09:14:03Z"
  }
}
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> If you pass a carrier value that isn't recognized — for example, a misspelling like `tmobile` — the request still succeeds. Plivo does not submit anything for that value and reports it in the response with status `FAILED` and reason code `CARRIER_NOT_RECOGNIZED`. Check `caller_reputation_by_carrier` in every response rather than relying on the HTTP status code alone.

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.section: How to set up Caller Reputation › Step 2: Wait for business approval
chunks.text:
Business vetting takes up to **2 business days**. Check status with the [Retrieve Profile API](/docs/messaging/api/10dlc/profile#retrieve-a-profile), or receive a callback per carrier network if you set `url`.

A number can attach only to a carrier network whose business status is `APPROVED`. You don't need every network approved — one is enough to start enabling numbers on that network.

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.section: How to set up Caller Reputation › Step 3: Enable Caller Reputation on your numbers

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.section: How to set up Caller Reputation › Step 4: Confirm activation
chunks.text: Call the [Get Account Phone Number](/docs/numbers/account-phone-numbers#get-an-account-phone-number) endpoint to check the number's status. The response returns both a merged `caller_reputation_status` and a per-carrier breakdown in `caller_reputation_by_carrier`. Attached networks move from `PENDING` to `ACTIVE` when registration completes.

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.section: Status values › Business status (on the profile)
chunks.text:
Each carrier network moves through these states independently:

| Status | Description |
| - | - |
| `NOT_REGISTERED` | Your business is not registered with this network |
| `PENDING` | Submitted and being vetted by the carrier network |
| `APPROVED` | Your business is approved — numbers can attach on this network, and any charge for this network starts |
| `FAILED` | The registration was rejected. Read `reason_code` and `reason`, fix your profile, and register again |
| `NOT_SUPPORTED` | Plivo doesn't offer this carrier network yet (Verizon). Informational only |

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.section: Status values › Number status (on the phone number)
chunks.text:
| Status | Description |
| - | - |
| `NOT_REGISTERED` | The number is not attached on this network. `reason_code` and `reason` explain why — for example, the business is still pending on this network |
| `PENDING` | The number is attached and awaiting confirmation from the carrier network |
| `ACTIVE` | Registration complete — your business name displays on outbound calls on this network |
| `FAILED` | The carrier network rejected this number. A number-level failure is specific to the number, not your business vetting |
| `NOT_SUPPORTED` | Plivo doesn't offer this carrier network yet (Verizon) |

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.text:
`caller_reputation_status` is a single summary across carrier networks. For the business: `APPROVED` > `PENDING` > `FAILED` > `NOT_REGISTERED`. For a number: `ACTIVE` > `PENDING` > `FAILED` > `NOT_REGISTERED`. `NOT_SUPPORTED` never affects the merged value.

Because in-progress and successful states outrank `FAILED`, a single network's failure can be hidden in the merged field. **Always read `caller_reputation_by_carrier` to see each network's real status**, not just the merged value.

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.text:
Every carrier entry that isn't healthy carries a machine-readable `reason_code` alongside the human-readable `reason`, in API responses and callbacks:

| Code | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `CARRIER_NOT_SUPPORTED` | The carrier network is recognized but not offered on Plivo yet (Verizon) |
| `CARRIER_NOT_RECOGNIZED` | The value you passed in `caller_reputation_carriers` isn't a recognized carrier network. Nothing was submitted for it |
| `BUSINESS_PENDING` | Number not attached: your business registration on this network is still pending. Retry after approval |
| `BUSINESS_FAILED` | Number not attached: your business registration on this network failed. Fix your profile and register again |
| `BUSINESS_NOT_REGISTERED` | Number not attached: your business isn't registered on this network. Register it on the profile first |
| `VENDOR_REJECTED` | The carrier network rejected the registration during vetting. The network's explanation is in `reason` |

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.text:
Set `url` (and optionally `method`) on your profile to receive one callback stream for all Caller Reputation events — business and number — on that profile. This replaces the earlier per-number callback configuration.

Callbacks are form-encoded `POST` requests (or `GET`, per your `method`) signed with [V3 signatures](/docs/voice/concepts/signature-validation) — validate `X-Plivo-Signature-V3`, `X-Plivo-Signature-V3-Nonce`, and `X-Plivo-Signature-Ma-V3` headers.

| Event | `Endpoint` | `Status` | When |
| - | - | - | - |
| Business resolved | `caller_reputation_business` | `approved` / `failed` | A carrier network resolves your business registration |
| Business deregistered | `caller_reputation_business` | `deregistered` | You deregister — fires once per deregistered network |
| Number resolved | `caller_reputation_number` | `active` / `failed` | A number resolves on a carrier network |

```text theme={null}
Endpoint=caller_reputation_business
Status=failed
ProfileUUID=8444eccc-5af9-404d-a46f-d2fd31cd74de
Carrier=at&t
ReasonCode=VENDOR_REJECTED
Reason=Business name could not be verified.
ResourceCreationTime=2026-08-20 09:14:03.412 +0000 UTC
ResourceUpdatedTime=2026-08-22 16:02:11.006 +0000 UTC
```

Number events add `Number` in E.164 format with a leading `+` (for example, `+14155550123`). `ReasonCode` and `Reason` appear only on `failed` events.

Delivery is at-least-once: respond with a `2xx` within 5 seconds, or Plivo retries up to 3 times (after 60, 120, and 240 seconds). Your endpoint must be HTTPS. Deduplicate on the combination of `ProfileUUID`, `Endpoint`, `Number`, `Carrier`, `Status`, and `ResourceUpdatedTime`. As a polling fallback, filter profiles with `GET /Profile/?caller_reputation_status=FAILED`.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The `caller_reputation_callback_url` and `caller_reputation_callback_method` parameters on Update Account Phone Number are **deprecated**. Plivo accepts them during the migration period and ignores them after. Set `url` and `method` on the profile instead.

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.section: Fix a failed registration and retry
chunks.text:
**Business failed on a network:** read `reason_code` and `reason` from `caller_reputation_by_carrier` on the profile — the reason persists, so you can read it any time. Fix your profile with the [Update Profile API](/docs/messaging/api/10dlc/profile#update-a-profile), then call it again with `enable_caller_reputation` set to `true`. Plivo retries only the networks that failed — networks that are already approved or pending are not affected, and retrying does not add a charge for a network that's already registered.

**Number not attached on a network:** the number's `caller_reputation_by_carrier` entry tells you why (`BUSINESS_PENDING`, `BUSINESS_FAILED`, or `BUSINESS_NOT_REGISTERED`). Resolve the business state on the profile, then call [Update Account Phone Number](/docs/numbers/account-phone-numbers#update-an-account-phone-number) again with `caller_reputation` set to `enabled`. Networks that are already attached are not affected.

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.text:
To stop Caller Reputation — and its billing — deregister the business on the profile:

1. Disable `caller_reputation` on every number under the profile for the networks you're deregistering.
2. Call the [Update Profile API](/docs/messaging/api/10dlc/profile#update-a-profile) with `enable_caller_reputation` set to `false`. Pass `caller_reputation_carriers` to deregister specific networks, or omit it to deregister all.

If numbers are still enrolled on a network you're deregistering, the API returns a `400` naming the count — Plivo never silently removes branding from numbers with live traffic. Once deregistered, that network's status returns to `NOT_REGISTERED` and any charge for that network stops. Registering again later creates a new registration.

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.text:
These problems return an HTTP `400` immediately. Fix them and resubmit.

| Error message | Description |
| - | - |
| `Profile is missing fields required for caller_reputation: ...` | Your profile is missing required business details. The message lists every missing or invalid field — fix them all in one update |
| `No registered business found for the provided profile_uuid. Enable caller_reputation on the profile first.` | You tried to enable a number under a profile with no registered business |
| `Business registration for the provided profile_uuid is still pending on all carriers. Retry after the business is approved.` | No carrier network has approved your business yet, so no number can attach |
| `Disable caller_reputation on all numbers under this profile first. N number(s) are still enrolled.` | You tried to deregister a business that still has enrolled numbers |
| `This profile has a registered Caller Reputation business. Disable caller_reputation on the profile first.` | You tried to delete a profile with a registered business |
| `caller_reputation is only supported for US numbers` | The phone number is not a US number. Caller Reputation supports US local and toll-free numbers only |
| `profile_uuid is required when caller_reputation is enabled` | You set `caller_reputation` to `enabled` on a number but did not provide a `profile_uuid` |

chunks.title: Caller Reputation
chunks.text:
**How much does Caller Reputation cost?**
Currently USD 12 per business per month for the AT&T network; the T-Mobile network carries no charge today. Billing is per business (one EIN), not per number — a business registered with both networks today pays one monthly charge. Rates can change and can differ by carrier network. See [Pricing](#pricing).

**When am I charged?**
Where a network carries a charge, it starts when that network approves your business. Registrations that fail validation or are never approved are not charged.

**How do I stop being charged?**
Deregister the business — disable Caller Reputation on the profile's numbers, then set `enable_caller_reputation` to `false` on the profile. Releasing numbers alone does **not** stop billing.

**Can I register with only one carrier network?**
Yes. Pass `caller_reputation_carriers` with just that network — for example, `["at&t"]`. You pay only for the networks you register with.

**Can I use the same profile for multiple numbers?**
Yes. You can link a single business profile to as many Plivo numbers as you need. All linked numbers display the same business name and are covered under the same registration.

**Can I add a number while my business is still pending?**
The number attaches on any network that has already approved your business. Networks still pending are reported as `NOT_REGISTERED` with reason code `BUSINESS_PENDING` — retry those after approval. If no network is approved yet, the request returns a `400`.

**How long does activation take?**
Business vetting takes up to 2 business days per carrier network. Once a network approves your business, numbers attach the same day — typically within hours.

**I enrolled numbers before this change. Do I need to do anything?**
No. Plivo migrates existing registrations to profile-level businesses automatically. Your per-carrier statuses appear on your profile, and your numbers stay enrolled.

**Does Caller Reputation guarantee my calls won't be flagged as spam?**
No. Caller Reputation registers your business identity with supported carrier networks, which helps establish trust. Call behavior, volume patterns, and recipient feedback can still influence spam classification by carriers and device-level apps.

chunks.title: Carrier Failover
chunks.text:
How Plivo ensures uninterrupted outbound calling with automatic carrier failover

> [!NOTE]
>
> * **What:** Automatically reroutes outbound calls to an alternate carrier when the primary route fails or degrades.
> * **When:** Automatic for most countries with no setup. In India it requires a configured fallback (High Availability) number.

How Plivo ensures uninterrupted outbound calling with automatic carrier failover.

Carrier outages, network congestion, and route degradation can disrupt outbound calls. Carrier failover eliminates this risk by automatically rerouting calls through an alternate carrier when the primary route is unavailable — keeping your calls connected without any interruption.

chunks.title: Carrier Failover
chunks.text:
Plivo maintains multiple carrier routes for every destination. When you place an outbound call, Plivo monitors the call route in real time. If the primary carrier fails or degrades, Plivo reroutes the call through an alternate carrier instantly.

| Scenario | What happens |
| - | - |
| **Carrier outage** | Primary carrier is down or unreachable — calls reroute through an alternate carrier. |
| **Network congestion** | High call volume causes drops on the primary route — calls shift to a less congested carrier. |
| **Route quality degradation** | Call quality drops below acceptable thresholds — calls switch to a higher-quality route. |

This is fully automatic — no configuration, no code changes, and no manual action required. Failover is transparent to both your application and your customer. India calls behave slightly differently — a retried call shows the fallback caller ID (see below).

chunks.title: Carrier Failover
chunks.text:
For most countries, Plivo handles carrier failover entirely behind the scenes. India is different.

Indian telecom regulations tie phone numbers to specific carriers. Plivo cannot silently reroute calls through a different carrier's number without explicit provisioning. To get failover coverage for India numbers, you need to set up **High Availability (HA)** numbers.

chunks.title: Carrier Failover
chunks.section: India — Additional Setup Required › What Are HA Numbers?
chunks.text:
High Availability pairs your primary India number with a backup number from a different carrier. If the primary number or its carrier becomes unreachable, calls automatically reroute through the fallback number — no code changes needed in your application.

1. You enable HA on an India local number (new or existing).
2. Plivo provisions a second number from a different carrier and adds it as an active rental on your account.
3. Plivo monitors the primary number in real time. If a failure or congestion is detected, calls reroute through the fallback number automatically.

Failover covers both Voice API calls and ZenTrunk domestic India trunk calls (calls placed from an India number to an India destination). In both cases, if the first carrier attempt fails, Plivo retries the call once through the fallback number instead of failing it.

chunks.title: Carrier Failover
chunks.section: India — Additional Setup Required › What Happens on a Retried Call
chunks.text:
1. **Your customer sees the fallback caller ID**, not the original `from` number, on the retried call.
2. Plivo generates **one CDR and one hangup callback per call** — the retry isn't reported as a second call.
3. Retried calls take slightly longer to connect or fail than first-attempt calls.
4. On a retried ZenTrunk call, the CDR's `from_number` records the fallback caller ID, not the number you originally sent.

chunks.title: Carrier Failover
chunks.section: India — Additional Setup Required › When Plivo Retries a Call
chunks.text:
Plivo retries a call only when the first attempt fails because of a carrier fault — not when the failure is a genuine call outcome.

| First attempt result | Retried? |
| - | - |
| The carrier rejects or can't complete the call | Yes |
| The called party is busy, or the caller cancels the call | No |
| The called party is temporarily unavailable after ringing starts | No |
| The called party is temporarily unavailable with no ringing | Yes |
| The request times out | Yes |

chunks.title: Carrier Failover
chunks.section: India — Additional Setup Required › Track Failover on Your Hangup Callback
chunks.text:
Voice API calls report failover through the `CarrierFailoverTriggered` parameter on the [hangup callback](/docs/voice/api/calls#callbacks) (`hangup_url`). Plivo sends `CarrierFailoverTriggered=true` only when a failover was attempted on the call. The parameter is omitted otherwise — never sent as `false` — so existing integrations and the normal payload shape are unaffected. The Call Details API doesn't return this field.

```text Example hangup callback (failover attempted) theme={null}
CallUUID=aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee
Event=Hangup
CallStatus=no-answer
CarrierFailoverTriggered=true
```

ZenTrunk has no webhook callbacks. To identify retried trunk calls, check the CDR's `from_number` for the fallback caller ID.

chunks.title: Carrier Failover
chunks.section: India — Additional Setup Required › Enable HA When Buying a New Number
chunks.text:
1. Go to **Phone Numbers > Buy Number** in the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/phone-numbers/search/).
2. Search for an India local number.
3. On the Details page, scroll to **High Availability**.
4. Check **Enable high availability backup number**.
5. Complete the purchase — Plivo provisions a fallback number and bills it automatically.

chunks.title: Carrier Failover
chunks.section: India — Additional Setup Required › Enable HA on an Existing Number
chunks.text:
1. Go to **Phone Numbers > Active Numbers** in the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/active-phone-numbers/).
2. Click the number you want to upgrade.
3. Scroll to the **High Availability** section.
4. Check **Enable high availability backup number** and click **Save**.
5. The **Fallback Number** appears in your number details once provisioned.

chunks.title: Carrier Failover
chunks.text:
Enabling HA rents a second number from a different carrier. This fallback number is added as a separate active rental on your Plivo account and billed at the standard monthly rate for India local numbers — in addition to your primary number.

The fallback number is visible under **Phone Numbers > Active Numbers** alongside your other rentals.

chunks.title: Carrier Failover
chunks.section: Frequently Asked Questions › Do I need to change my application code?
chunks.text: No. Carrier failover is automatic and transparent. Your application continues to use the same Plivo APIs and number configuration without any changes. For India HA numbers, failover is also automatic once you enable it — no code changes required.

chunks.title: Carrier Failover
chunks.section: Frequently Asked Questions › How can I see which fallback number is assigned to my India number?
chunks.text: Go to **Phone Numbers > Active Numbers** in the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/active-phone-numbers/) and click on the primary number. The **Fallback Number** field shows the assigned backup number.

chunks.title: Carrier Failover
chunks.section: Frequently Asked Questions › Does carrier failover cover incoming calls?
chunks.text: Carrier failover applies to outbound calls. Incoming call behavior follows your standard number configuration.

chunks.title: Carrier Failover
chunks.section: Frequently Asked Questions › Do I need HA numbers outside India?
chunks.text: No. Plivo handles carrier failover automatically for all countries other than India. HA numbers are only needed for India due to regulatory requirements that tie numbers to specific carriers.

chunks.title: Features
chunks.text:
Overview of Plivo voice features — recording, conferencing, IVR, DTMF, and more

> [!NOTE]
>
> Overview of Plivo Voice API capabilities: call queueing, global conferencing and multiparty calls, text-to-speech and audio playback, DTMF and speech input, call recording and voicemail, and machine detection.

Here are some of the key features Plivo’s Voice API platform supports.

chunks.title: Features
chunks.text: Make multiple calls with a single API request. We handle call queuing for you so you don’t have to worry about building the workflow yourself. By default, all your calls get queued on the Plivo platform in sequential order, and are initiated according to the CPS (calls per second) set for your account.

chunks.title: Features
chunks.text: Integrate multiparty calls and audio conferencing into your applications, or build advanced contact center functionality. Plivo provides conference APIs, conference XML, and multiparty calls using ’s wide array of features that help you integrate your contact center and calls from anywhere across the globe.

chunks.title: Features
chunks.text: Speak dynamic text in 28 accents across various languages. Choose from an array of SSML voices powered by Amazon Polly.

chunks.title: Features
chunks.text: Play prerecorded audio files at any time during a call. Create prompts, announcements, or music on hold.

chunks.title: Features
chunks.text: Record, store, and retrieve calls at any time. Recordings are dual-channel by default and stored encrypted.

chunks.title: Features
chunks.text: Collect digits from a user’s keypad during a call and control your call flow based on those inputs.

chunks.title: Features
chunks.text: Build intelligent voice-driven interactions, including conversational IVR and form fills. Automatically recognize speech as text on your voice calls in real time.

chunks.title: Features
chunks.text: Detect whether an outbound voice call was answered by a human or an answering machine. Leave a voicemail message if the call is answered by an answering machine and connect the call to an agent if it’s answered by a human.

chunks.title: Features
