chunks.title: Screen Incoming Calls
chunks.section: Create a Rails controller to screen incoming calls
chunks.text:
Change to the project directory and run this command to create a Rails controller to screen incoming calls.

```shell theme={null}
$ rails generate controller Plivo voice
```

This command generates a controller named plivo_controller in the app/controllers/ directory, and a view will be generated in app/views/plivo directory. We can delete the view as we don’t need it.

```shell theme={null}
$ rm app/views/plivo/voice.html.erb
```

Open the file app/controllers/plivo_controller.rb and paste this code in the PlivoController class:

```rb theme={null}
include Plivo
include Plivo::XML
include Plivo::Exceptions

class PlivoController < ApplicationController
 def screen
    blacklist = ['<phone_number1>', '<phone_number2>', '<phone_number3>']

    from_number = params[:From]
    r = Response.new()

    if blacklist.include? from_number
        # Specify the reason for hangup
        params = {
            reason: 'rejected'
        }
        r.addHangup(params)
    else
        r.addSpeak('Hello, how are you today')
    end
    xml = Plivo::PlivoXML.new(r)
    render xml: xml.to_xml
 end
end
```

Replace the phone number placeholders with actual phone numbers (for example, 12025551234).

chunks.title: Supervisor Coaching
chunks.text: Implement supervisor coaching for call center agents using multiparty calls

chunks.title: Supervisor Coaching
chunks.text:
Supervisors in call centers need to coach agents to cultivate an effective team. Coaching involves supervisors listening in on live calls and advising agents without customers’ knowledge. A supervisor can also take over a call and talk to a customer directly. This guide shows how to implement supervisor coaching using Plivo‘s multiparty call (MPC) feature. We’ll look at four tasks:

* Connecting a customer and an agent
* Agent adding supervisor to a call
* Supervisor joining call
* Supervisor taking over call

chunks.title: Supervisor Coaching
chunks.text: To get started, you need a Plivo account — [sign up](https://cx.plivo.com/signup) with your work email address if you don’t have one already. You must have a voice-enabled Plivo phone number to receive incoming calls; you can rent numbers from the [Numbers](https://cx.plivo.com/phone-numbers) page of the Plivo console, or by using the Numbers API. If this is your first time using Plivo APIs, follow our instructions to set up a Node.js development environment and a web server and safely expose that server to the internet.

chunks.title: Supervisor Coaching
chunks.text:
Consider the case of a call center where customers call a hotline number to connect with a customer support representative using a web app powered by [Plivo Browser SDK](/docs/voice/sdk/browser/overview). The call flow goes like this:

1. Customer dials in from the browser app to talk to an agent.
2. The customer is added to a multiparty call.
3. The agent is added to the same multiparty call.

![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/EvRfP72Bjs4tuRt5/images/connect-customer-agent.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=EvRfP72Bjs4tuRt5&q=85&s=f2861d4a19f82fb06d34b9b35f72a6b7)

Here’s what that process looks like in Python.

```py theme={null}
from flask import Flask, Response, request, make_response
import plivo
from plivo import plivoxml

app=Flask(__name__)

music_url = "https://s3.amazonaws.com/plivocloud/music.mp3"
client = plivo.RestClient(auth_id="<auth_id>", auth_token="<auth_token>")

# Add customer to the MPC. You can assign this to the Plivo app of the endpoint mapped to the customer in the browser app
@app.route("/add/customer/", methods=["GET", "POST"])
def multipartycall_add_customer():
   mpc_name = "test"
   mpc_params = {
       "content": mpc_name,
       "role": "Customer",
       "status_callback_url": "https://<ngrok_identifier>.ngrok.io/add/agent/",
       "status_callback_method": "POST",
       "wait_music_url": music_url,
       "wait_music_method": "GET",
   }
   mpc_element = plivoxml.MultiPartyCallElement(**mpc_params)
   res = plivoxml.ResponseElement()
   res.add(mpc_element)
   return Response(res.to_string(), mimetype="application/xml")

# Add agent to the MPC to talk to the customer
@app.route("/customer/callback/", methods=["GET", "POST"])
def multipartycall_add_agent():
   mpc_EventName = request.form.get("EventName")
   mpc_MPCUUID = request.form.get("MPCUUID")
   mpc_ParticipantCallFrom = request.form.get("ParticipantCallFrom")
   if mpc_EventName == "MPCInitialized":
       call_params = {
           'role': "Agent",
           'uuid': mpc_MPCUUID,
           'start_mpc_on_enter': True,
           'from_': mpc_ParticipantCallFrom, # Customer number as caller ID
           'to_': "sip:websdk171107061912@phone.plivo.com", #Agent's endpoint username or phone number
           'call_status_callback_url': "https://<ngrok_identifier>.ngrok.io/agent/callback/",
           'call_status_callback_method': 'POST',
           "enter_sound": "none"
       }
       try:
           response = client.multi_party_calls.add_participant(**call_params)
       except Exception as e:
           response = client.multi_party_calls.stop(uuid=mpc_MPCUUID)
   return 'ok'

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(host="0.0.0.0", debug=True)
```

Replace the auth placeholders with your authentication credentials from the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/home).

chunks.title: Supervisor Coaching
chunks.section: Agent adds supervisor to a call
chunks.text:
1. The previous example was a simple case that involved just a customer and an agent. If the call center wants to provide supervisor coaching, agents can add a supervisor to an ongoing multiparty call like this:

   1. The agent clicks an Add Supervisor button on the dialer web app on which they’re  talking to the customer.
   2. The supervisor is added to the multiparty call using Plivo’s [Add Participant API](/docs/voice/api/multiparty-calls#add-a-participant).
   3. By default, only the agent will be able to hear the supervisor. You can override this by changing the coachMode parameter to `false`.

![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/NFI9_HRHTMInDf93/images/agent-adds-supervisor.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=NFI9_HRHTMInDf93&q=85&s=20920516240f6a10fbc69f2d17aa7cf9)

Here’s what that process looks like in Python.

```py theme={null}
from flask import Flask, Response, request, make_response
import plivo
from plivo import plivoxml

app=Flask(__name__)

music_url = "https://s3.amazonaws.com/plivocloud/music.mp3"
client = plivo.RestClient(auth_id="<auth_id>", auth_token="<auth_token>")

@app.route("/mpc/customer/", methods=["GET", "POST"])
def multipartycall_customer():
  ....
  ....

# Add agent to the MPC to talk to the customer
@app.route("/customer/callback/", methods=["GET", "POST"])
def multipartycall_agent():
   ....
   ....

# Agent clicks "Add supervisor to the call" option to add them to the ongoing MPC
@app.route("/add_supervisor/<mpc_MPCUUID>", methods=["GET", "POST"])
def add_supervisor(mpc_MPCUUID):
   call_params = {
       'role': "Supervisor",
       'uuid': mpc_MPCUUID, # you can get this from status_callback_url
       'dial_music': 'None',
       'from_': "<caller_id>", # Agent number as caller ID; you can get this from status_callback_url
       'to_': "sip:browsersdkdemo438313651789286059@phone.plivo.com", #Supervisor Phone number goes here
       'call_status_callback_url': "https://<ngrok_identifier>.ngrok.io/supervisor/callback/",
       'call_status_callback_method': 'POST',
   }
   response = client.multi_party_calls.add_participant(**call_params)
   return str(response)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(host="0.0.0.0", debug=True)
```

chunks.title: Supervisor Coaching
chunks.text:
Not all supervisor calls are initiated by agents — supervisors can jump in themselves. Here’s how this process — often called call barging — works:

1. An agent is talking to a customer on an ongoing multiparty call.
2. A supervisor, who is monitoring all the live calls on the call center web dashboard, clicks on a Join the Call button next to the longest call in the queue.
3. The supervisor can then listen to the call and coach the agent.

![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/sqGJ0ONkT5kTuesy/images/supervisor-joins-call.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=sqGJ0ONkT5kTuesy&q=85&s=22065bb2c0074ac4851a029240319f35)

Here’s what that process looks like in Python.

```py theme={null}
from flask import Flask, Response, request, make_response
import plivo
from plivo import plivoxml

app=Flask(__name__)

music_url = "https://s3.amazonaws.com/plivocloud/music.mp3"
client = plivo.RestClient(auth_id="<auth_id>", auth_token="<auth_token>")

@app.route("/mpc/customer/", methods=["GET", "POST"])
def multipartycall_customer():
    ....
    ....

# Add agent to the MPC to talk to the customer
@app.route("/customer/callback/", methods=["GET", "POST"])
def multipartycall_agent():
    ....
    ....

# Agent clicks "Add supervisor to the call" option to add them to the ongoing MPC
@app.route("/add_supervisor/", methods=["GET", "POST"])
def add_supervisor():
    ....
    ....

# Supervisor clicks "Join the call" option to be added to the ongoing MPC
@app.route("/coach_the_agent/<mpc_MPCUUID>", methods=["GET", "POST"])
def join_specific_mpc(mpc_MPCUUID):
   mpc_name = "test" # MPC name of the call to which the supervisor wishes to join; you can get this from status_callback_url
   mpc_params = {
       "content": mpc_name,
       "role": "Supervisor",
       "coach_mode": True, # The supervisor can talk to only the agent.
       "status_callback_url": "https://<ngrok_identifier>.ngrok.io/supervisor/callback/",
       "status_callback_method": "POST",
       "enter_sound": "none",
   }
   mpc_element = plivoxml.MultiPartyCallElement(**mpc_params)
   res = plivoxml.ResponseElement()
   res.add(mpc_element)
   return Response(res.to_string(), mimetype="application/xml")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(host="0.0.0.0", debug=True)
```

chunks.title: Supervisor Coaching
chunks.text:
Depending on what they hear, sometimes supervisors want to talk to both the customer and the agent. Here’s how that process might go.

1. An agent is talking to a customer on an ongoing multiparty call.
2. The supervisor is monitoring all live calls on the call center web dashboard.
3. The supervisor clicks on the Take Over the Call button of a specific call, and can then take over the call and talk to both the customer and the agent.

![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/sqGJ0ONkT5kTuesy/images/supervisor-takes-over.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=sqGJ0ONkT5kTuesy&q=85&s=217fc00263fc5eaa970e3f13aad1e0a3)

Here’s what that process looks like in Python.

```py theme={null}
from flask import Flask, Response, request, make_response
import plivo
from plivo import plivoxml

app=Flask(__name__)

music_url = "https://s3.amazonaws.com/plivocloud/music.mp3"
client = plivo.RestClient(auth_id="<auth_id>", auth_token="<auth_token>")

@app.route("/mpc/customer/", methods=["GET", "POST"])
def multipartycall_customer():
    ....
    ....

# Add agent to the MPC to talk to the customer
@app.route("/customer/callback/", methods=["GET", "POST"])
def multipartycall_agent():
    ....
    ....

# Agent clicks "Add supervisor to the call" option to add them to the ongoing MPC
@app.route("/add_supervisor/", methods=["GET", "POST"])
def add_supervisor():
    ....
    ....

# Supervisor clicks "Join the call" option to be added to the ongoing MPC
@app.route("/coach_the_agent/", methods=["GET", "POST"])
def join_specific_mpc():
    ....
    ....

# Supervisor clicks "Take over the call" option to be added to the ongoing MPC
@app.route("/talk_to_customer/", methods=["GET", "POST"])
def talk_to_customer():
   mpc_name = "test" # MPC name of the call to which the supervisor wishes to join; you can get this from status_callback_url
   mpc_params = {
       "content": mpc_name,
       "role": "Supervisor",
       "coach_mode": false, # The supervisor can talk to only the agent
       "status_callback_url": "https://<ngrok_identifier>.ngrok.io/supervisor/callback/",
       "status_callback_method": "POST",
       "enter_sound": "none",
   }
   mpc_element = plivoxml.MultiPartyCallElement(**mpc_params)
   res = plivoxml.ResponseElement()
   res.add(mpc_element)
   return Response(res.to_string(), mimetype="application/xml")

if __name__ == "__main__":
   app.run(host="0.0.0.0", debug=True)
```

As you can see, Plivo makes it easy to set up and manage multiparty calls. With these capabilities, you can run your own call center, manage call transfers, coach agents, and much more. For more details, see our [Multiparty Call API reference](/docs/voice/api/multiparty-calls) page.

chunks.title: Transfer to Human Agent
chunks.text:
When to hand an AI-handled call to a human agent, and how to choose between DID forward, SIP auth forward, and a Multiparty Call.

> [!NOTE]
>
> * **What:** Hand an AI-handled call to a human agent by phone, SIP, or Multiparty Call. Only a Multiparty Call does warm transfer.
> * **Watch out:** A SIP transfer needs [two Plivo IP ranges whitelisted](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/sip-auth-forward/#what-your-contact-center-must-do), not one.

When your AI agent hits an escalation, a query it can't handle, or a fallback, it hands the caller to a human agent. This page helps you pick how. Each option has its own page with the XML, API calls, and setup, and [Troubleshooting](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/troubleshooting/) covers failed transfers.

The video walks through all three options in about a minute. Select a chapter to jump to it.

<video />

Video chapters

chunks.title: Transfer to Human Agent
chunks.section: When to Transfer to a Human Agent
chunks.text:
Transfer the caller to a human agent when your AI agent detects an escalation trigger, for example:

* The caller asks for a human.
* The caller's intent is unclear.
* The query is one your AI agent can't handle.
* Your AI agent hits a fallback.

A transfer is either cold or warm:

* **Cold transfer:** the caller is connected to the human agent, and your AI agent leaves the call without briefing them.
* **Warm transfer:** your AI agent briefs the human agent first, while the caller is on hold. Then the caller is connected.

chunks.title: Transfer to Human Agent
chunks.text:
![Three options. Option 1, DID forward: Plivo dials the human agent's phone number. Option 2, SIP auth forward: Plivo dials the contact center over SIP with credentials. Option 3, Multiparty Call: the human agent is added as a participant.](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/9zIRdvx4doyoicBb/images/transfer-to-human-agent/transfer-options-light.svg?fit=max&auto=format&n=9zIRdvx4doyoicBb&q=85&s=a6e87f34a25eda293532c413564ac53d)

| Option | What It Does | Best For | Warm Transfer |
| - | - | - | - |
| **[Option 1: DID Forward](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/did-forward/)** | Transfer to a regular phone number | Simple call centers, agents on PSTN phones, no SIP infrastructure | No |
| **[Option 2: SIP Auth Forward](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/sip-auth-forward/)** (recommended) | Transfer to a SIP endpoint (softphone, contact center, PBX) with credentials | Modern contact centers, softphone-based agents, lower latency | No |
| **[Option 3: Multiparty Call](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/multiparty-call/)** | Put the caller, your AI agent, and the human agent in one Multiparty Call (MPC) | Warm transfer, and transfers that don't wait for your AI agent's WebSocket to close | Yes |

chunks.title: Transfer to Human Agent
chunks.text:
![Three questions in order. Should the AI agent brief the human agent first? Yes: Option 3. Does the human agent answer on a phone? Yes: Option 1. Does the human agent use a SIP endpoint? Yes: Option 2.](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/9zIRdvx4doyoicBb/images/transfer-to-human-agent/transfer-chooser-light.svg?fit=max&auto=format&n=9zIRdvx4doyoicBb&q=85&s=9d1383d6f487832620a26b8ad22c28a4)

Pick the option recommended for your situation:

* **Your AI agent should brief the human agent before the caller joins (warm transfer):** [Option 3, Multiparty Call](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/multiparty-call/#warm-transfer-with-a-multiparty-call). Options 1 and 2 can't do a warm transfer. Option 2 can still [pass the call's context in SIP headers](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/sip-auth-forward/#pass-call-context-to-the-human-agent).
* **Your human agents answer on regular phone numbers:** [Option 1, DID forward](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/did-forward/).
* **Your human agents use a SIP contact center, softphone, or PBX:** [Option 2, SIP auth forward](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/sip-auth-forward/).

Option 3 only works if your own server controls the call. It puts the caller in a Multiparty Call, then uses the Plivo API to add the human agent and remove the AI agent. If another platform answers calls on your Plivo number for you, use Option 1 or 2.

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent by DID Forward
chunks.text:
Transfer an AI-handled call to a human agent's phone number with Dial XML and the Number element.

> [!NOTE]
>
> * **What:** Transfer a call from your AI agent to a human agent's phone number with `<Dial>` and `<Number>`.
> * **Watch out:** On a `<Stream>` with `keepCallAlive="true"`, [close your WebSocket](#if-your-call-is-on-a-live-audio-stream) when you transfer.

The simplest transfer. When your AI agent decides to transfer, return this XML. Plivo dials the phone number in `<Number>`:

```xml theme={null}
<Response>
    <Speak>Connecting you to a human agent now.</Speak>
    <Dial>
        <Number>+14155551234</Number>
    </Dial>
</Response>
```

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent by DID Forward
chunks.text:
![DID forward in five steps. 1: the caller is on a call with your AI agent. 2: your app returns Dial with Number to Plivo. 3: Plivo calls the phone number. 4: the human agent answers. 5: the caller now talks to the human agent.](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/9zIRdvx4doyoicBb/images/transfer-to-human-agent/did-forward-sequence-light.svg?fit=max&auto=format&n=9zIRdvx4doyoicBb&q=85&s=5d967fbd27014698000817d0a846d48d)

* Plivo originates an outbound call from your AI agent's leg to the human agent's phone number
* When the human agent answers, the two legs are bridged
* The caller and the human agent are connected, and your AI agent leaves the call

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent by DID Forward
chunks.text:
**Pros**

* **Works with any phone** - mobile, landline, or a softphone with a DID
* **Simple to set up** - needs nothing from your network team

**Cons**

* **Outbound call cost** - billed for the full duration of the transferred call
* **Agents need a real phone number**
* **Less flexibility** - no custom SIP headers, no routing to specific agent IDs or queues
* **No warm transfer** - your AI agent can't brief the human agent before the caller is connected. For that, use [Option 3: Multiparty Call](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/multiparty-call/)

> [!TIP]
>
> A DID forward is also the fastest way to prove a transfer problem is *not* your application. If a transfer to a phone number connects but a SIP transfer to the same team doesn't, the fault is on the SIP path — the firewall or the credentials — not in your XML.

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent by DID Forward
chunks.section: If Your Call Is on a Live Audio Stream
chunks.text:
This applies when your AI agent runs over [audio streaming](/docs/voice/xml/audio-streaming/) and the call is on a `<Stream>` with `keepCallAlive="true"`.

With `keepCallAlive="true"`, [the `<Stream>` element runs exclusively and subsequent XML executes only after the stream disconnects](/docs/voice/xml/audio-streaming/). Your transfer XML is subsequent XML, so it does not run while the stream is still open. If the WebSocket never closes, the transfer never runs.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Close your bot's WebSocket when you decide to transfer. Keep `keepCallAlive="true"` — closing the socket is what lets the call continue to your transfer XML, not removing the attribute.

![When your AI agent closes its WebSocket. Too early: the call ends; fix by adding Wait right after Stream. On time: the transfer works. Stays open: the transfer never runs; fix by closing the WebSocket when you transfer, or use Option 3.](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/9zIRdvx4doyoicBb/images/transfer-to-human-agent/websocket-close-window-light.svg?fit=max&auto=format&n=9zIRdvx4doyoicBb&q=85&s=4146a9d4b85d1ce4c46c8e9e2fc29f59)

Add a `<Wait>` right after `<Stream>` in your answer XML. If your AI agent closes its WebSocket before your transfer arrives, the call waits for it instead of ending:

```xml theme={null}
<Response>
    <Stream bidirectional="true" keepCallAlive="true">wss://your-ai-agent.example.com/stream</Stream>
    <Wait length="30"/>
</Response>
```

Set `length` to cover the time between your AI agent closing its WebSocket and your server calling [Transfer a Call](/docs/voice/api/calls/#transfer-a-call). See the [Wait](/docs/voice/xml/routing/#wait) reference for its attributes.

If you stop the stream through the API rather than closing the socket, **trigger the transfer first, then send** `DELETE /v1/Account/{auth_id}/Call/{call_uuid}/Stream/`. Stopping the stream first lets the leg continue to the end of the XML document it is already running, which can end the call instead of transferring it.

`streamTimeout` defaults to `86400` seconds. Set it to a realistic ceiling for your call shape so a stream that never closes cannot hold a call open.

If transfers still drop the call or never run, use [Option 3: Multiparty Call](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/multiparty-call/) instead. In a Multiparty Call, the caller's call doesn't run `<Stream>`, so nothing waits for the WebSocket to close.

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent by DID Forward
chunks.text: Instead of waiting for your answer URL to return Dial XML, you can trigger the transfer programmatically with the [Transfer a Call API](/docs/voice/api/calls/#transfer-a-call), which points a live call leg at a new URL. That URL returns the same `<Dial>` XML shown above. For SIP auth forward, include `sipAuthUsername` and `sipAuthPassword` on `<User>`. For a warm transfer, where your AI agent briefs the human agent before the caller is connected, use [Option 3: Multiparty Call](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/multiparty-call/#warm-transfer-with-a-multiparty-call).

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent with a Multiparty Call
chunks.text:
Hand an AI-handled call to a human agent inside a Multiparty Call, as a cold transfer or a warm transfer where the AI agent briefs the human agent.

> [!NOTE]
>
> * **What:** Put the caller, your AI agent, and the human agent in one Multiparty Call (MPC), for a cold or warm transfer.
> * **Watch out:** In a warm transfer, [hold the caller, don't mute them](#warm-transfer-with-a-multiparty-call).

Put the caller and your AI agent in a [Multiparty Call](/docs/voice/xml/multiparty-call/) (MPC). Your AI agent joins as a participant with the `ai-agent` role. When you transfer, the human agent joins as another participant. Use it for two cases:

* **The transfer doesn't wait for your AI agent's WebSocket to close.** The caller's call runs `<MultiPartyCall>`, not `<Stream>`, so nothing holds the transfer back.
* **Warm transfer.** Your AI agent stays in the MPC and briefs the human agent while the caller is on hold, then leaves.

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent with a Multiparty Call
chunks.section: How a Multiparty Call Transfer Works
chunks.text:
![Cold transfer in three steps. 1: the AI agent answers the caller. 2: the human agent joins the Multiparty Call. 3: the AI agent is removed and the caller talks to the human agent.](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/9zIRdvx4doyoicBb/images/transfer-to-human-agent/mpc-cold-transfer-light.svg?fit=max&auto=format&n=9zIRdvx4doyoicBb&q=85&s=5a31a7ba6828c056fd95b526b1635758)

* The caller joins the MPC, usually through their answer XML.
* Your server adds your AI agent to the MPC through the [Add a Participant](/docs/voice/api/multiparty-calls/#add-a-participant) API. Your AI agent connects over WebSocket, the same way it does with `<Stream>`: it receives `start` and `media` events and sends audio back with `playAudio` ([Stream Event Protocol](/docs/voice-agents/audio-streaming/concepts/audio-streaming-reference/)).
* Either can join first. You can add your AI agent first, then add the caller with Add a Participant and the `customer` role, so your AI agent is ready when they answer.
* To transfer, your server adds the human agent, at a phone number or a SIP endpoint.
* Your server removes your AI agent with the [Kick a Participant](/docs/voice/api/multiparty-calls/#kick-a-participant) API. The caller and the human agent stay connected.
* When the human agent hangs up, your server ends the MPC with the [End a Multiparty Call](/docs/voice/api/multiparty-calls/#end-a-multiparty-call) API.

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent with a Multiparty Call
chunks.text:
**Pros**

* **No wait on your WebSocket** - the human agent joins while your AI agent's WebSocket is still open
* **Warm transfer** - your AI agent can brief the human agent before the caller is connected
* **Same AI agent code** - an AI agent built for `<Stream>` connects with the same events

**Cons**

* **More work on your server** - it tracks each participant's `MemberID` and makes an API call for each step of the transfer
* **Your server must control the call** - it puts the caller in the MPC, so it doesn't fit an AI platform that serves the answer URL for you

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent with a Multiparty Call
chunks.section: Set Up a Multiparty Call Transfer
chunks.text:
These steps start with the caller. Return this answer XML for the call. Give each call its own MPC name, because [Add a Participant](/docs/voice/api/multiparty-calls/#add-a-participant) joins any ongoing MPC with the same name.

```xml theme={null}
<Response>
    <MultiPartyCall role="customer" stayAlone="true" endMpcOnExit="true"
        statusCallbackUrl="https://example.com/mpc-events"
        statusCallbackEvents="participant-state-changes">
        call-1234
    </MultiPartyCall>
</Response>
```

* `stayAlone="true"` keeps the caller in the MPC while they're its only participant, before your AI agent joins.
* `endMpcOnExit="true"` ends the MPC when the caller hangs up.
* `participant-state-changes` sends a `ParticipantJoin` event to `statusCallbackUrl` each time a participant joins. Save the `MemberID` from each one. You need the caller's to hold them and your AI agent's to remove it. The event parameters are listed in [Status Callback Parameters](/docs/voice/xml/multiparty-call/#status-callback-parameters).

**1. Add your AI agent.** When the caller's `ParticipantJoin` arrives, add your AI agent with the `ai-agent` role. `to` is required, but Plivo doesn't dial it for an `ai-agent` participant: set it to any Plivo number on your account. Set `ai_agent_stream_content_type` to the audio format your AI agent already uses on `<Stream>`. The default is `audio/x-l16;rate=8000`.

```bash theme={null}
curl -X POST "https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/MultiPartyCall/name_call-1234/Participant/" \
  -u '<auth_id>:<auth_token>' \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "role": "ai-agent",
    "from": "+14151234567",
    "to": "<any_plivo_number_on_your_account>",
    "ai_agent_stream_service_url": "wss://your-ai-agent.example.com/stream",
    "ai_agent_stream_content_type": "audio/x-l16;rate=8000"
  }'
```

**2. Add the human agent.** When your AI agent decides to transfer, add the human agent with the `agent` role. Set `to` to a phone number or a SIP endpoint.

```bash theme={null}
curl -X POST "https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/MultiPartyCall/name_call-1234/Participant/" \
  -u '<auth_id>:<auth_token>' \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "role": "agent",
    "from": "+14151234567",
    "to": "+14155551234"
  }'
```

**3. Remove your AI agent.** When the human agent's `ParticipantJoin` arrives, kick your AI agent. This is a cold transfer.

```bash theme={null}
curl -X DELETE "https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/MultiPartyCall/name_call-1234/Participant/<ai_agent_member_id>/" \
  -u '<auth_id>:<auth_token>'
```

**4. End the MPC when the human agent hangs up.** When the human agent's `ParticipantExit` arrives, end the MPC with [End a Multiparty Call](/docs/voice/api/multiparty-calls/#end-a-multiparty-call). Without this, the caller stays alone in the MPC after the human agent hangs up, because `stayAlone` is `true`.

If the human agent doesn't answer, no `ParticipantJoin` arrives for them. Your AI agent is still in the call, so it can tell the caller or try another human agent. To get the result of each dial, add `add-participant-api-events` to `statusCallbackEvents`.

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent with a Multiparty Call
chunks.section: Warm Transfer with a Multiparty Call
chunks.text:
![Warm transfer in three steps. 1: the AI agent answers the caller. 2: the caller waits on hold while the AI agent briefs the human agent. 3: the caller is taken off hold, the AI agent is removed, and the caller talks to the human agent.](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/9zIRdvx4doyoicBb/images/transfer-to-human-agent/mpc-warm-transfer-light.svg?fit=max&auto=format&n=9zIRdvx4doyoicBb&q=85&s=aebade69736d8c5d73bfb49bf19903ba)

In a warm transfer, your AI agent briefs the human agent before the caller is connected. Use the setup above and hold the caller around step 2:

1. Hold the caller: update the caller's participant with `hold` set to `true`.
2. Add the human agent (step 2 above).
3. Your AI agent briefs the human agent. They hear each other, and the caller hears neither.
4. Unhold the caller: update the caller's participant with `hold` set to `false`.
5. Remove your AI agent (step 3 above). The caller and the human agent are now connected.

```bash theme={null}
curl -X POST "https://api.plivo.com/v1/Account/{auth_id}/MultiPartyCall/name_call-1234/Participant/<caller_member_id>/" \
  -u '<auth_id>:<auth_token>' \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"hold": true}'
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> Hold the caller. Don't mute them. A muted participant can't be heard but still hears everyone in the MPC, so a muted caller hears your AI agent brief the human agent. A held caller hears none of the briefing, and nobody hears them.

To play your own hold music, set `customerHoldMusicUrl` on `<MultiPartyCall>`. The URL must return XML with `Play`, `Speak`, or `Wait` elements ([Custom Hold Music](/docs/voice/xml/multiparty-call/#custom-hold-music)). A URL that returns an audio file directly leaves the held caller in silence.

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent by SIP Auth Forward
chunks.text:
Transfer an AI-handled call to a SIP contact center, softphone, or PBX with credentials, including the firewall setup the contact center needs.

> [!NOTE]
>
> * **What:** Transfer a call from your AI agent to a SIP endpoint, such as your contact center, with `<Dial>` and `<User>`.
> * **Watch out:** A SIP transfer needs [two Plivo IP ranges whitelisted](#what-your-contact-center-must-do), not one.

You'll do most of this in your own application. The firewall and SIP settings at the far end aren't yours to change — they belong to whoever runs your contact center. Those are collected in [What Your Contact Center Must Do](#what-your-contact-center-must-do), which you can send them directly.

Most modern contact center software (Five9, Genesys, NICE, Talkdesk, custom WebRTC apps, etc.) accepts inbound SIP calls. When your AI agent decides to transfer, return this XML. Plivo calls the SIP address in `<User>`:

```xml theme={null}
<Response>
    <Speak>Connecting you to a human agent now.</Speak>
    <Dial>
        <User sipAuthUsername="<sip_username>" sipAuthPassword="<sip_password>">
            sip:agent@your-contact-center.example.com
        </User>
    </Dial>
</Response>
```

Give `<User>` a SIP URI with a hostname, as shown. Every example in the [Dial XML reference](/docs/voice/xml/routing/) uses this form.

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent by SIP Auth Forward
chunks.section: How a SIP Auth Forward Works
chunks.text:
![SIP auth forward in five steps. 1: the caller is on a call with your AI agent. 2: your app returns Dial with User to Plivo. 3: Plivo calls the SIP address. 4: the human agent answers. 5: the caller now talks to the human agent.](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/9zIRdvx4doyoicBb/images/transfer-to-human-agent/sip-auth-forward-sequence-light.svg?fit=max&auto=format&n=9zIRdvx4doyoicBb&q=85&s=3de5794f50bd90bc0228b7739ea002a7)

* Plivo sends an initial SIP INVITE to your contact center's SIP endpoint **without** credentials
* If the contact center responds with `401 Unauthorized` or `407 Proxy Authentication Required`, the outbound SBC re-sends the INVITE with the supplied `sipAuthUsername` / `sipAuthPassword`
* Contact center validates credentials; call connects
* Caller and agent are bridged

`sipAuthPassword` is 8-128 characters, and is required whenever `sipAuthUsername` is set.

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent by SIP Auth Forward
chunks.section: Pass Call Context to the Human Agent
chunks.text:
Your AI agent can't brief the human agent on this path, but it can send what it learned with the call. Add [`sipHeaders`](/docs/voice/xml/routing/) to `<User>` with the call's context, such as the reason for the transfer or an order number. Your contact center receives them on the incoming call and can show them to the human agent when it rings.

```xml theme={null}
<Response>
    <Dial>
        <User sipAuthUsername="<sip_username>" sipAuthPassword="<sip_password>"
              sipHeaders="Reason=refund,OrderId=1234">
            sip:agent@your-contact-center.example.com
        </User>
    </Dial>
</Response>
```

* Each header arrives prefixed with `X-PH-`, so `Reason=refund` arrives as `X-PH-Reason`. The [Dial reference](/docs/voice/xml/routing/) lists the one exception, for calls that came in over SIP authentication.
* Use only letters and digits in header names and values ([Pass Custom Headers](/docs/voice/use-cases/pass-custom-headers/)).
* Headers with reserved prefixes (`PH-`, `Plivo`, `FS-`, `SipAuth`, `ZT-`, `Twilio`) and the name `ClientRegion` are silently dropped. See [SIP Authentication](/docs/voice/concepts/sip-authentication/) for the full list.

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent by SIP Auth Forward
chunks.section: Trade-offs of a SIP Auth Forward
chunks.text:
**Pros**

* **Lower cost** - single SIP termination charge, no PSTN minutes
* **Lower latency** - direct SIP, no PSTN intermediary
* **More flexibility** - [pass the call's context in SIP headers](#pass-call-context-to-the-human-agent), route to specific agent IDs or queues
* **Better for AI workflows** - agents are typically already on softphones or contact center software

**Cons**

* **Needs your contact center's cooperation** - its firewall opened to Plivo for call setup and audio, and digest credentials if it uses them. Work you cannot do yourself, often behind a change-control queue you do not control
* **No warm transfer** - your AI agent can't brief the human agent before the caller is connected, though it can [pass the call's context in SIP headers](#pass-call-context-to-the-human-agent). For a spoken briefing, use [Option 3: Multiparty Call](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/multiparty-call/)
* **Subtler failure modes** - most of the [Troubleshooting](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/troubleshooting/#troubleshooting) table is specific to this path

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent by SIP Auth Forward
chunks.section: Set Up a SIP Auth Forward
chunks.text:
**1. Get your contact center's SIP endpoint**

Find the SIP URI provided by your contact center software (e.g., `sip:queue-1@your-cc.example.com`). Most platforms expose this in their admin dashboard.

**2. Get authentication credentials**

Most SIP-based contact center software requires digest authentication. Get the username and password from your contact center setup.

**3. Open the firewall at your contact center**

If your contact center filters inbound traffic by IP address, it has to whitelist Plivo for both call setup and audio first. Send them [What Your Contact Center Must Do](#what-your-contact-center-must-do) — this is the one part you cannot do yourself.

**4. Update your AI agent's transfer logic**

When your agent decides to transfer, return a `<Dial>` XML response with the `<User>` element. Set `sipAuthUsername` and `sipAuthPassword` to the credentials from Step 2. Point the SIP URI to your contact center endpoint.

**5. Test**

Trigger a transfer from your AI agent and confirm three things: the human agent's phone rings, both sides can hear each other, and your Dial action URL receives `DialStatus=completed`. If authentication fails, the call ends with hangup cause `sip_auth_failed` (code `4240`).

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent by SIP Auth Forward
chunks.section: If Your Call Is on a Live Audio Stream
chunks.text:
This applies when your AI agent runs over [audio streaming](/docs/voice/xml/audio-streaming/) and the call is on a `<Stream>` with `keepCallAlive="true"`.

With `keepCallAlive="true"`, [the `<Stream>` element runs exclusively and subsequent XML executes only after the stream disconnects](/docs/voice/xml/audio-streaming/). Your transfer XML is subsequent XML, so it does not run while the stream is still open. If the WebSocket never closes, the transfer never runs.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Close your bot's WebSocket when you decide to transfer. Keep `keepCallAlive="true"` — closing the socket is what lets the call continue to your transfer XML, not removing the attribute.

![When your AI agent closes its WebSocket. Too early: the call ends; fix by adding Wait right after Stream. On time: the transfer works. Stays open: the transfer never runs; fix by closing the WebSocket when you transfer, or use Option 3.](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/9zIRdvx4doyoicBb/images/transfer-to-human-agent/websocket-close-window-light.svg?fit=max&auto=format&n=9zIRdvx4doyoicBb&q=85&s=4146a9d4b85d1ce4c46c8e9e2fc29f59)

Add a `<Wait>` right after `<Stream>` in your answer XML. If your AI agent closes its WebSocket before your transfer arrives, the call waits for it instead of ending:

```xml theme={null}
<Response>
    <Stream bidirectional="true" keepCallAlive="true">wss://your-ai-agent.example.com/stream</Stream>
    <Wait length="30"/>
</Response>
```

Set `length` to cover the time between your AI agent closing its WebSocket and your server calling [Transfer a Call](/docs/voice/api/calls/#transfer-a-call). See the [Wait](/docs/voice/xml/routing/#wait) reference for its attributes.

If you stop the stream through the API rather than closing the socket, **trigger the transfer first, then send** `DELETE /v1/Account/{auth_id}/Call/{call_uuid}/Stream/`. Stopping the stream first lets the leg continue to the end of the XML document it is already running, which can end the call instead of transferring it.

`streamTimeout` defaults to `86400` seconds. Set it to a realistic ceiling for your call shape so a stream that never closes cannot hold a call open.

If transfers still drop the call or never run, use [Option 3: Multiparty Call](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/multiparty-call/) instead. In a Multiparty Call, the caller's call doesn't run `<Stream>`, so nothing waits for the WebSocket to close.

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent by SIP Auth Forward
chunks.text: Instead of waiting for your answer URL to return Dial XML, you can trigger the transfer programmatically with the [Transfer a Call API](/docs/voice/api/calls/#transfer-a-call), which points a live call leg at a new URL. That URL returns the same `<Dial>` XML shown above. For SIP auth forward, include `sipAuthUsername` and `sipAuthPassword` on `<User>`. For a warm transfer, where your AI agent briefs the human agent before the caller is connected, use [Option 3: Multiparty Call](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/multiparty-call/#warm-transfer-with-a-multiparty-call).

chunks.title: Transfer to a Human Agent by SIP Auth Forward
chunks.section: What Your Contact Center Must Do
chunks.text:
Send this list to whoever runs your contact center. Their system must:

* Whitelist Plivo's [External SIP endpoints](/docs/voice/concepts/firewall-network-configuration/#external-sip-endpoints) for call setup and [RTP media servers](/docs/voice/concepts/firewall-network-configuration/#rtp-media-servers) for audio, if its firewall filters by IP address. Credentials don't replace this: they get the call accepted, but the audio still has to reach the contact center
* Issue the SIP credentials you put in `sipAuthUsername` and `sipAuthPassword`, if it authenticates inbound calls
* Advertise a **public** IP address in its `Contact` header and SDP
* Offer **PCMU or PCMA**
* Whitelist Plivo without pinning the rule to a source port

If it can't whitelist Plivo, transfer to one of its phone numbers with [Option 1: DID forward](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/did-forward/). What breaks when an item is missing is on the [Troubleshooting](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/troubleshooting/#troubleshooting) page.

chunks.title: Troubleshoot Transfer to Human Agent
chunks.text:
Test an AI-to-human transfer, read its hangup causes and Dial status, and fix failed, silent, or stuck transfers.

> [!NOTE]
>
> * **What:** Test a transfer from your AI agent to a human agent, and fix one that fails or has no audio.
> * **Start with:** a transfer to a phone number. If it connects, the fault is on the SIP path.

The setup for each option is on its own page: [DID forward](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/did-forward/), [SIP auth forward](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/sip-auth-forward/), and [Multiparty Call](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/multiparty-call/).

chunks.title: Troubleshoot Transfer to Human Agent
chunks.text:
**1. Transfer to a phone number first**

Point a test transfer at a phone number that reaches the same team. If this connects, your XML, your application, and your Plivo account are all working — which narrows any later failure to the SIP path.

**2. Transfer to the SIP endpoint**

Run the same transfer against your SIP endpoint. A failure here, after the phone number transfer succeeded, points at the firewall or the SIP credentials rather than at your agent logic.

**3. Check audio in both directions**

Speak from each end. Audio in one direction only means the RTP media ranges are whitelisted in one direction only.

**4. Confirm your application reads DialStatus**

Your Dial action URL should receive `DialStatus` and `DialHangupCause`, so your application can fall back or inform the caller when a handoff fails.

chunks.title: Troubleshoot Transfer to Human Agent
chunks.text:
When a transfer fails, the Dial action URL and hangup callback include specific values:

| HangupCauseName | Code | DialStatus | Meaning |
| - | - | - | - |
| `sip_auth_failed` | `4240` | `failed` | SIP credentials were rejected by the remote endpoint |
| `sip_auth_timeout` | `4250` | `timeout` | Remote endpoint did not respond to the digest challenge |
| `no-answer` | — | `no-answer` | Agent did not pick up within the dial timeout |
| `busy` | — | `busy` | Agent endpoint is busy |

Your agent application receives `DialStatus` and `DialHangupCause` on the Dial action URL, so it can detect a failed handoff and respond (e.g., retry with a different endpoint, fall back to a phone number, or inform the caller). Every hangup code is listed in [Hangup Causes](/docs/voice/troubleshooting/hangup-causes/).

chunks.title: Troubleshoot Transfer to Human Agent
chunks.text:
| Issue | Solution |
| - | - |
| Transfer never arrives, and nothing appears in your contact center's logs | Only the RTP media ranges are whitelisted, so the INVITE is dropped before it arrives. Whitelist the [External SIP endpoints](/docs/voice/concepts/firewall-network-configuration/#external-sip-endpoints) on port 5060, and confirm your endpoint is listening on that port |
| The Dial action URL reports an empty `DialBLegUUID` | Nobody answered, so no B-leg was created. Check the SIP URI in `<User>` against the [Dial XML reference](/docs/voice/xml/routing/), then check that your endpoint is reachable |
| Transfer fails with `sip_auth_failed` (`4240`) | Verify the SIP credentials match exactly. Check your contact center's auth realm. Some platforms authenticate by IP address instead of digest — if yours does, whitelist Plivo's addresses rather than sending credentials |
| Transfer fails with `sip_auth_timeout` (`4250`) | Your endpoint is unreachable, or its SIP service isn't running. Check both before re-testing credentials |
| Agent answers, but there's no audio | Configure your SIP endpoint to advertise its **public** IP address. A private address in its `Contact` header or SDP leaves Plivo's audio with nowhere to send to |
| Call is rejected before the agent's phone rings | No shared audio codec. Offer PCMU or PCMA on your SIP endpoint |
| Audio works in one direction only | The RTP media ranges are whitelisted in one direction only. Add a rule for each direction |
| Call connects, but the line stays open after one side hangs up | Plivo's in-dialog `BYE` may be sent from a different source port than the one that opened the dialog. A firewall rule pinned to source port 5060 drops it. Whitelist Plivo's addresses without pinning a source port |
| Transfer XML doesn't run while your AI agent's `<Stream>` with `keepCallAlive="true"` is open | Close your AI agent's WebSocket when it decides to transfer. If transfers still drop the call or never run, use a [Multiparty Call](/docs/voice/use-cases/transfer-to-human-agent/multiparty-call/) |
| In a Multiparty Call warm transfer, the caller hears your AI agent brief the human agent | Hold the caller with `hold` set to `true`, not `mute`. A muted participant still hears everyone in the Multiparty Call |
| In a Multiparty Call, the held caller hears silence instead of hold music | Make your `customerHoldMusicUrl` return XML with a `<Play>` element, not an audio file. See [Custom Hold Music](/docs/voice/xml/multiparty-call/#custom-hold-music) |
| Caller hears silence during ring | Use the `dialMusic` attribute on `<Dial>` to play hold music while the agent is being reached |

chunks.title: Voice Alerts
chunks.text: Send automated voice call alerts with audio playback and keypress responses

chunks.title: Voice Alerts
chunks.text:
This guide shows how to make voice calls to alert customers to critical issues that require immediate attention. You can play recorded audio when the call recipient answers or use text-to-speech. You can then take action based on a dialpad key they press in response. You can set different actions if the call is not answered, if the line is busy, or if you reach voicemail.

You can send voice alerts either by using our PHLO visual workflow builder or our APIs and XML documents. Follow the instructions in one of the tabs below.

chunks.title: Voice Alerts
chunks.text: Here’s how to use Plivo APIs and XML to implement voice alerts.

chunks.title: Voice Alerts
chunks.text:
![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/GjxgkWYDEc2_LVPj/images/outbound-calls.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=GjxgkWYDEc2_LVPj&q=85&s=f8b62e42991d9fd92d93eab071cb4124)

Plivo requests an answer URL when the call is answered (step 4) and expects the file at that address to hold a valid XML response from the application with instructions on how to handle the call. To see how this works, you can use [https://s3.amazonaws.com/static.plivo.com/alert.xml](https://s3.amazonaws.com/static.plivo.com/alert.xml) as an answer URL to test your first outgoing call. The file contains this XML code:

```xml theme={null}
<Response>
<Speak>Your database is out of memory. Press 1 to resolve or 2 to escalate.</Speak>
</Response>
```

This code instructs Plivo to say, “Your database is out of memory. Press 1 to resolve or 2 to escalate” to the call recipient. You can find the entire list of valid Plivo XML verbs in our [XML Reference](/docs/voice/xml/overview/) documentation.

chunks.text: To get started, you need a Plivo account —  [sign up](https://cx.plivo.com/signup) with your work email address if you don’t have one already. If this is your first time using Plivo APIs, follow our instructions to set up a Node.js development environment.

chunks.text: To get started, you need a Plivo account —  [sign up](https://cx.plivo.com/signup) with your work email address if you don’t have one already. If this is your first time using Plivo APIs, follow our instructions to set up a Ruby development environment.

chunks.title: Voice Alerts
chunks.section: Create a voice alerts application in Ruby
chunks.text:
Create a file called `make_call.rb` and paste into it this code.

```ruby theme={null}
require 'rubygems'
require 'plivo'

include Plivo
include Plivo::Exceptions

api = RestClient.new("<auth_id>","<auth_token>")

begin
  response = api.calls.create(
    '<caller_id>',
    ['<destination_number>'],
    'https://s3.amazonaws.com/static.plivo.com/alert.xml'
  )
  puts response
rescue PlivoRESTError => e
  puts 'Exception: ' + e.message
end
```

Replace the auth placeholders with your authentication credentials from the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/home). Replace the phone number placeholders with actual phone numbers in [E.164 format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) (for example, +12025551234).

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Note:**
> We recommend that you store your credentials in the `auth_id` and `auth_token` environment variables, to avoid the possibility of accidentally committing them to source control. If you do this, you can initialize the client with no arguments and Plivo will automatically fetch the values from the environment variables. You can use `ENV` to store environment variables and fetch them when initializing the client.

chunks.title: Voice Alerts
chunks.text:
Save the file and run it.

```shell theme={null}
$ ruby make_call.rb
```

chunks.title: Voice Alerts
chunks.text:
This guide shows how to make voice calls to alert customers to critical issues that require immediate attention. You can play recorded audio when the call recipient answers or use text-to-speech. You can then take action based on a dialpad key they press in response. You can set different actions if the call is not answered, if the line is busy, or if you reach voicemail.

You can send voice alerts either by using our PHLO visual workflow builder or our APIs and XML documents. Follow the instructions in one of the tabs below.

chunks.title: Voice Alerts/Notifications Broadcasting
chunks.text: To get started, you need a Plivo account —  [sign up](https://cx.plivo.com/signup) with your work email address if you don’t have one already. If this is your first time using Plivo APIs, follow our instructions to set up a Ruby development environment and a web server and safely expose that server to the internet.

chunks.title: Voice Alerts/Notifications Broadcasting
chunks.text:
Create a file called `broadcast.rb` and paste into it this code.

```ruby theme={null}
require 'rubygems'
require 'plivo'

include Plivo
include Plivo::Exceptions

api = RestClient.new("<auth_id>","<auth_token>")

begin
  response = api.calls.create(
    '<caller_id>',
    ['<destination_number1>', '<destination_number2>'],
    'https://s3.amazonaws.com/static.plivo.com/broadcast.xml'
  )
  puts response
rescue PlivoRESTError => e
  puts 'Exception: ' + e.message
end
```

Replace the auth placeholders with your authentication credentials from the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/home). Replace the phone number placeholders with actual phone numbers in [E.164 format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) (for example, +12025551234). Destination numbers may also be SIP endpoints, in which case each destination_number placeholder must be a valid SIP URI — for example, sip:[john1234@phone.plivo.com](mailto:john1234@phone.plivo.com).

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Note:** We recommend that you store your credentials in the `auth_id` and `auth_token` environment variables, so as to avoid the possibility of accidentally committing them to source control. If you do this, you can initialize the client with no arguments and it will automatically fetch them from the environment variables. You can use `ENV` to store environment variables and fetch them when initializing the client.

chunks.title: Voice Alerts/Notifications Broadcasting
chunks.text:
Save the file and run it.

```shell theme={null}
ruby broadcast.rb
```

chunks.title: Voice Notifications
chunks.text: Send audio notifications via voice calls with text-to-speech or recordings

chunks.title: Voice Notifications
chunks.text:
This guide shows how to send audio notifications using voice calls. You can play recorded audio when the call recipient answers or use text-to-speech, as we show here, combining static text with dynamic information that Plivo gets from a variable.

You can use voice notification for use cases such as:

* Order notification
* Booking status
* Delivery status
* Flight cancellation/rescheduling
* Two-factor authentication/one-time password
* New offer notification
* Account balance notification

Implement voice notification either by using our PHLO visual workflow builder or our APIs and XML documents. Follow the instructions in one of the tabs below.

chunks.title: Voice Notifications

chunks.section: Create a voice notification application in Ruby
chunks.text:
Create a file called `make_call.rb` and paste into it this code.

```rb theme={null}
require 'rubygems'
require 'plivo'

include Plivo
include Plivo::Exceptions

api = RestClient.new("<auth_id>","<auth_token>")

begin
  response = api.calls.create(
    '<caller_id>',
    ['<destination_number>'],
    'https://s3.amazonaws.com/static.plivo.com/notification.xml'
  )
  puts response
rescue PlivoRESTError => e
  puts 'Exception: ' + e.message
end
```

Replace the auth placeholders with your authentication credentials from the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/home). Replace the phone number placeholders with actual phone numbers in [E.164 format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) (for example, +12025551234).

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Note:**
> We recommend that you store your credentials in the `auth_id` and `auth_token` environment variables, to avoid the possibility of accidentally committing them to source control. If you do this, you can initialize the client with no arguments and Plivo will automatically fetch the values from the environment variables. You can use `ENV` to store environment variables and fetch them when initializing the client.

chunks.title: Voice Notifications
chunks.text:
Save the file and run it.

```shell theme={null}
$ ruby make_call.rb
```

chunks.title: Voice OTP
chunks.text: Verify phone numbers with voice one-time passwords using text-to-speech

chunks.title: Voice OTP
chunks.text:
This guide shows how to use a voice one-time password (OTP) to verify a mobile number. We first make a call to the phone number to be verified and use text-to-speech to read a random sequence of digits to the call recipients. The user then confirms the digits by entering them using dialpad keypresses. Voice OTP is commonly used to verify new user registrations for an app or website.

You can send a voice OTP either by using our PHLO visual workflow builder or our APIs and XML documents. Follow the instructions in one of the tabs below.

chunks.text: To get started, you need a Plivo account —  [sign up](https://cx.plivo.com/signup) with your work email address if you don’t have one already. If this is your first time using Plivo APIs, follow our instructions to set up a Ruby development environment.

chunks.title: Voice OTP
chunks.text:
Change to the project directory and run this command to create a Rails controller for the voice OTP application.

```shell theme={null}
$ rails generate controller Plivo voice
```

It generates a controller named plivo_controller in the app/controllers/ directory and a respective view in app/views/plivo. We can delete the view as we don‘t need it.

```shell theme={null}
$ rm app/views/plivo/voice.html.erb
```

chunks.title: Voice OTP
chunks.text:
Edit app/controllers/plivo_controller.rb file and add this code.

```ruby theme={null}
include Plivo
require 'redis'
require 'json'
include Plivo::Exceptions

class PlivoController < ApplicationController
	def dispatch_otp
		redis = Redis.new(host: "localhost")
		code = rand(999_999)
		dst_number = params[:dst_number]

		api = RestClient.new("<auth_id>","<auth_token>")
		begin
			response = api.calls.create(
				'<caller_id>',
				[dst_number],
				"https://<yourdomain>.com/answer_url/#{code}"
			)
			puts response
		end
		redis.setex(dst_number, 60, code) # Verification code is valid for 1 min
		puts JSON.pretty_generate({ :status=> 'success', :message=> 'verification initiated' })
	rescue PlivoRESTError => e
		puts 'Exception: ' + e.message
	end

	def verify_otp
		redis = Redis.new(host: "localhost")
		code = params[:otp]
		number = params[:number]
		original_code = redis.get(number)
		if original_code == code
			redis.del(number)  # verification successful, delete the code
			puts JSON.pretty_generate( { :status=> 'success', :message=> 'Codes match — number verified'})
		elsif original_code != code
			puts JSON.pretty_generate({ :status => "failure", :message=> 'Codes do not match — number not verified' })
		else
			puts JSON.pretty_generate( { :status=> 'rejected', :message=> 'Number not found' })
		end
	end
end
```

Replace the auth placeholders with your authentication credentials from the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/home). Replace the phone number placeholder with an actual phone number in [E.164 format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) (for example, +12025551234).

**Note:**
We recommend that you store your credentials in the `auth_id` and `auth_token` environment variables, to avoid the possibility of accidentally committing them to source control. If you do this, you can initialize the client with no arguments and Plivo will automatically fetch the values from the environment variables. You can use `ENV` to store environment variables and fetch them when initializing the client.

chunks.title: Voice Surveys
chunks.text:
Plivo lets you automate voice surveys for use cases such as collecting feedback from customers and conducting polling on political issues. You can set up multiple levels of questions and walk users through different paths depending on the keys they press in response to your questions, and save the responses for analysis.

You can implement voice surveys either by using our PHLO visual workflow builder or our APIs and XML documents. Follow the instructions in one of the tabs below.

chunks.title: Voice Surveys

chunks.text:
Plivo lets you automate voice surveys for use cases such as collecting feedback from customers and conducting polling on political issues. You can set up multiple levels of questions and walk users through different paths depending on the keys they press in response to your questions, and save the responses for analysis.

You can implement voice surveys either by using our PHLO visual workflow builder or our APIs and XML documents. Follow the instructions in one of the tabs below.

chunks.title: Voice Surveys
chunks.section: Create a voice survey application in Ruby
chunks.text:
Change to the project directory and run this command to create a Rails controller.

```shell theme={null}
$ rails generate controller Plivo voice
```

This generates a controller named plivo_controller in the app/controllers/ directory and a respective view  in app/views/plivo. We can delete the view as we will not need it.

```shell theme={null}
$ rm app/views/plivo/voice.html.erb
```

Edit app/controllers/plivo_controller.rb and add this code in the PlivoController class.

```ruby theme={null}
include Plivo
include Plivo::XML
include Plivo::Exceptions

class PlivoController < ApplicationController
  # Message that Plivo reads when the call recipient answers
  $question1 = "Hi, this is a call from Plivo. How would you rate your overall satisfaction with our services? Press 1 if you're satisfied or 2 to suggest improvements"
  $question2 = "How would you rate your satisfaction with our customer service? Press 1 if you're satisfied or 2 to suggest improvements"
  # Message that Plivo reads when the recipient provides negative feedback
  $negative_feedback = "We're sorry about your bad experience. One of our representatives will get in touch with you"
  # Message that Plivo reads when the caller does nothing
  $noinput_message = "Sorry, I didn't catch that. Please hang up and try again"
  # This is the message that Plivo reads when the caller inputs a wrong number.
  $wronginput_message = "Sorry, that's not a valid entry"
  def survey
    r = Response.new()

    getinput_action_url = "https://<yourdomain>.com/ivr/firstbranch/"
    params = {
        action: getinput_action_url,
        method: 'POST',
        digitEndTimeout: '5',
        inputType:'dtmf',
        redirect:'true'
    }
    getinput = r.addGetInput(params)
    getinput.addSpeak($question1)
    r.addSpeak($noinput_message)

    xml = PlivoXML.new(r)
    render xml: xml.to_xml
  end
  def firstbranch
    digit = params[:Digits]
    r = Response.new()

    if (digit == "1")
        getinput_action_url = "https://<yourdomain>.com/ivr/secondbranch/"
        params = {
            action: getinput_action_url,
            method: 'POST',
            digitEndTimeout: '5',
            inputType:'dtmf',
            redirect:'true'
        }
        getinput = r.addGetInput(params)
        getinput.addSpeak($question2)
        r.addSpeak($noinput_message)

    elsif (digit == "2")
        r.addSpeak($negative_feedback)
    else
        r.addSpeak($wronginput_message)
    end

    xml = PlivoXML.new(r)
    render xml: xml.to_xml
  end
  def secondbranch
    digit = params[:Digits]

    r = Response.new()

    if (digit == "1")
        body = "Thank you for participating in the survey"
        params = {
            'language'=> "en-GB"
        }

        r.addSpeak(body,params)
    elsif (digit == "2")
        r.addSpeak($negative_feedback)
    else
        r.addSpeak($wronginput_message)
    end

    xml = PlivoXML.new(r)
    render xml: xml.to_xml
  end
end
```

Replace the auth placeholders with your authentication credentials from the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/home). Replace the phone number placeholders with actual phone numbers in [E.164 format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) (for example, +12025551234).

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Note:** We recommend that you store your credentials in the `auth_id` and `auth_token` environment variables, to avoid the possibility of accidentally committing them to source control. If you do this, you can initialize the client with no arguments and Plivo will automatically fetch the values from the environment variables. You can use `ENV` to store environment variables and fetch them when initializing the client.

Add a route for the inbound function in the PlivoController class. Edit config/routes.rb and add these lines after the inbound route.

```shell theme={null}
get 'plivo/survey'
get 'plivo/firstbranch'
get 'plivo/secondbranch'
```

Start the Rails server.

```shell theme={null}
$ rails server
```

You should see your basic server application in action at  [http://localhost:3000/plivo/survey/](http://localhost:3000/plivo/survey/).

Set up ngrok to expose your local server to the internet.

chunks.title: Voice Surveys
chunks.section: Create a voice survey application in PHP
chunks.text:
Create a file called `survey.py` and paste into it this code.

```py theme={null}
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
from flask import Flask, Response, request, url_for
from plivo import plivoxml

# Message that Plivo reads when the call recipient answers
question1 = "Hi, this is a call from Plivo. How would you rate your overall satisfaction with our services? Press 1 if you're satisfied or 2 to suggest improvements"
question2 = "How would you rate your satisfaction with our customer service? Press 1 if you're satisfied or 2 to suggest improvements"
# Message that Plivo reads when the recipient provides negative feedback
negative_feedback = "We're sorry about your bad experience, One of our representatives will get in touch with you"
# Message that Plivo reads when the caller does nothing
noinput_message = "Sorry, I didn't catch that. Please hang up and try again"
# Message that Plivo reads when the caller enters an invalid number
wronginput_message = "Sorry, that's not a valid entry"

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route('/survey/', methods=['GET','POST'])
def ivr():
    response = plivoxml.ResponseElement()
    getinput_action_url = "https://<yourdomain>.com/firstbranch/"
    response.add(plivoxml.GetInputElement().
        set_action(getinput_action_url).
        set_method('POST').
        set_input_type('dtmf').
        set_digit_end_timeout(5).
        set_redirect(True).add(
            plivoxml.SpeakElement(question1)))
    response.add(plivoxml.SpeakElement(noinput_message))
    return Response(response.to_string(), mimetype='application/xml')

@app.route('/survey/firstbranch/', methods=['GET','POST'])
def firstbranch():
    response = plivoxml.ResponseElement()
    digit = request.values.get('Digits')
    if digit == "1":
        # Read out a text.
        getinput_action_url = "https://<yourdomain>.com/secondbranch/"
        response.add(plivoxml.GetInputElement().
            set_action(getinput_action_url).
            set_method('POST').
            set_input_type('dtmf').
            set_digit_end_timeout(5).
            set_redirect(True).add(
                plivoxml.SpeakElement(question2)))
        response.add(plivoxml.SpeakElement(noinput_message))

    elif digit == "2":
        response.add_speak(negative_feedback)

    else:
        response.add_speak(wronginput_message)
    return Response(response.to_string(), mimetype='application/xml')

@app.route('/ivr/secondbranch/', methods=['GET','POST'])
def secondbranch():
    response = plivoxml.ResponseElement()
    digit = request.values.get('Digits')

    if digit == "1":
        text = u"Thank you for participating in the survey"
        params = {
            'language': "en-GB",
        }
        response.add_speak(text,**params)

    elif digit == "2":
        response.add_speak(negative_feedback)

    else:
        response.add_speak(wronginput_message)
    return Response(response.to_string(), mimetype='application/xml')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(host='0.0.0.0', debug=True)
```

Replace the auth placeholders with your authentication credentials from the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/home). Replace the phone number placeholders with actual phone numbers in [E.164 format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) (for example, +12025551234).

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Note:** We recommend that you store your credentials in the `auth_id` and `auth_token` environment variables, to avoid the possibility of accidentally committing them to source control. If you do this, you can initialize the client with no arguments and Plivo will automatically fetch the values from the environment variables. You can use `os module(os.environ)` to store environment variables and fetch them when initializing the client.

Save the file and run it.

```shell theme={null}
python survey.py
```

You should see your basic server application in action at [http://localhost:5000/survey/](http://localhost:5000/survey/).

Set up ngrok to expose your local server to the internet.

chunks.title: Voicemail
chunks.section: Create a Plivo application for voicemail
chunks.text:
Associate the Express server you created with Plivo by creating a Plivo application. Visit Voice > [Applications](https://cx.plivo.com/xml-applications) in the Plivo console and click on **Add New Application**, or use Plivo’s [Application API](/docs/account/api/application/#create-an-application).

Give your application a name — we called ours `Voicemail`. Enter the server URL you want to use (for example `https://<yourdomain>.com/voicemail/`) in the `Answer URL` field and set the method to `GET`.  Click **Create Application** to save your application.

![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/Ac6PoKJHHxDx1U63/images/create-voicemail.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=Ac6PoKJHHxDx1U63&q=85&s=d8832f8460c2440a038cd67d04337883)

chunks.title: Voicemail
chunks.section: Assign a Plivo number to your application
chunks.text:
Navigate to the [Numbers](https://cx.plivo.com/phone-numbers) page and select the phone number you want to use for this application.

From the Application Type drop-down, select `XML Application`.

From the Plivo Application drop-down, select `Voicemail` (the name we gave the application).

Click **Update Number** to save.

![](https://mintcdn.com/plivo/Ac6PoKJHHxDx1U63/images/assign-voicemail.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=Ac6PoKJHHxDx1U63&q=85&s=56accdebff950282e34af43446d227cb)

You must have a voice-enabled Plivo phone number to receive incoming calls; you can rent numbers from the [Numbers](https://cx.plivo.com/phone-numbers) page of the Plivo console, or by using the [Numbers API](/docs/numbers/). If this is your first time using Plivo APIs, follow our instructions to set up a Ruby development environment and a web server and safely expose that server to the internet.

chunks.title: Voicemail
chunks.section: Create a Rails controller to implement voicemail
chunks.text:
Change to the project directory and run this command to create a Rails controller for inbound calls.

```shell theme={null}
$ rails generate controller Plivo voice
```

This command generates a controller named plivo_controller in the app/controllers/ directory and a respective view in app/views/plivo. We can delete the view as we do not need it.

```shell theme={null}
$ rm app/views/plivo/voice.html.erb
```

Edit app/controllers/plivo_controller.rb and paste this code into the PlivoController class.

```ruby theme={null}
include Plivo
include Plivo::XML
include Plivo::Exceptions

class PlivoController < ApplicationController
	def voicemail
		response = Response.new

		first_speak_body = 'Please leave a message after the beep. Press the star key when done.'
		response.addSpeak(first_speak_body)

		params = {
			action: 'https://www.foo.com/get_recording/',
			maxLength: '30',
			finishOnKey: '*'
		}
		response.addRecord(params)

		second_speak_body = 'Recording not received.'
		response.addSpeak(second_speak_body)
				xml = PlivoXML.new(response)
		render xml: xml.to_xml
	end
end
```

chunks.title: Voicemail
chunks.section: Create a Rails controller to implement voicemail › Add a route
chunks.text:
To add a route for the inbound function in the PlivoController class, edit config/routes.rb and add this line after the inbound route.

```shell theme={null}
get 'plivo/voicemail'
```

Start the Rails server

```shell theme={null}
$ rails server
```

You should see your basic server application in action at [http://localhost:3000/plivo/voicemail/](http://localhost:3000/plivo/voicemail/).

chunks.title: Voicemail
chunks.section: Create a Flask server to implement voicemail
chunks.text:
Create a file called `voicemail.py` and paste into it this code.

```py theme={null}
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
from flask import Flask, Response, request, url_for
from plivo import plivoxml

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route('/voicemail/', methods=['GET','POST'])
def voicemail():
    response = plivoxml.ResponseElement()
    response.add(
        plivoxml.SpeakElement(
            'Please leave a message. Press the star key when you\'re done'))
    response.add(
        plivoxml.RecordElement(
            action='https://<yourdomain>.com/get_recording/',
            max_length=30,
            finish_on_key='*'))
    response.add(plivoxml.SpeakElement('Recording not received'))
    return Response(response.to_string(), mimetype='application/xml')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(host='0.0.0.0', debug=True)
```

Save the file and run it.

```shell theme={null}
$ python voicemail.py
```

You should see your basic server application in action at [http://localhost:5000/voicemail/](http://localhost:5000/voicemail/).

chunks.title: Voicemail Transcription
chunks.section: Create a Rails controller to implement voicemail transcription
chunks.text:
Change to the project directory and run this command to create a Rails controller for inbound calls.

```shell theme={null}
$ rails generate controller Plivo voice
```

This command generates a controller named plivo_controller in the app/controllers/ directory and a respective view in app/views/plivo. We can delete the view as we do not need it.

```shell theme={null}
$ rm app/views/plivo/voice.html.erb
```

Edit app/controllers/plivo_controller.rb and paste this code into the PlivoController class.

```ruby theme={null}
include Plivo
include Plivo::XML
include Plivo::Exceptions

class PlivoController < ApplicationController
  skip_before_action :verify_authenticity_token
	def voicemail
		response = Response.new
		response.addSpeak('Please leave a message after the beep. Press the star key when you\'re done.')
		params = {
      		transcriptionType: 'auto',
      		transcriptionUrl: url_for(action: 'transcriptionUrl', controller: 'plivo', only_path: false, protocol: 'https'),
			action: url_for(action: 'actionUrl', controller: 'plivo', only_path: false, protocol: 'https'),
			maxLength: '30',
			finishOnKey: '*'
		}
		response.addRecord(params)

		second_speak_body = 'Recording not received.'
		response.addSpeak(second_speak_body)
				xml = PlivoXML.new(response)
		render xml: xml.to_xml
	end

  def transcriptionUrl
    response = params
		api = RestClient.new("<auth_id>","<auth_token>")
		message_response = api.messages.create(
			src: "<sender_id>",
			dst: "<destination_number>",
			text: "You have a new transcription: "+params[:transcription]
		)
		puts message_response
		puts response
    render status: :ok, json: @controller.to_json
  end

  def actionUrl
    response = params
    puts response
    render status: :ok , json: @controller.to_json
  end
end
```

Replace the auth placeholders with your authentication credentials from the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/home). Replace the phone number placeholders with actual phone numbers in [E.164 format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) (for example, +12025551234).

  post 'plivo/actionUrl'

chunks.title: Voicemail Transcription
chunks.section: Create a Flask server to implement voicemail transcription
chunks.text:
Create a file called `voicemail.py` and paste into it this code.

```py theme={null}
from flask import Flask, Response, url_for, request
import json
import plivo
from plivo import plivoxml

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route('/voicemail/', methods=['GET', 'POST'])
def voicemail():
    response = plivoxml.ResponseElement()
    response.add(plivoxml.SpeakElement("Please leave a message. Press the star key when you\'re done"))
    response.add(plivoxml.RecordElement(transcription_type='auto',
                 transcription_url=url_for('transcription_url',
                 _external=True), action=url_for('action_url',
                 _external=True), max_length=30, finish_on_key='*'))

    response.add(plivoxml.SpeakElement('Recording not received'))
    return Response(response.to_string(), mimetype='application/xml')

@app.route('/transcription-url/', methods=['GET', 'POST'])
def transcription_url():
    form_values = json.dumps(request.form, indent=4)
    print form_values

    client = plivo.RestClient('<auth_id>', '<auth_token>')
    response = client.messages.create(src='<sender_id>',
            dst='<destination_number>',
            text='You have a new transcription: '+ request.form['transcription'])
    print response
    return ('OK', 200)

@app.route('/action-url/', methods=['GET', 'POST'])
def action_url():
    form_values = json.dumps(request.form, indent=4)
    print form_values
    return ('OK', 200)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(host='0.0.0.0', debug=True)
```

Replace the auth placeholders with your authentication credentials from the [Plivo console](https://cx.plivo.com/home). Replace the phone number placeholders with actual phone numbers in [E.164 format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.164) (for example, +12025551234).

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Note:** We recommend that you store your credentials in the `auth_id` and `auth_token` environment variables, to avoid the possibility of accidentally committing them to source control. If you do this, you can initialize the client with no arguments and Plivo will automatically fetch the values from the environment variables. You can use `os module(os.environ)` to store environment variables and fetch them when initializing the client.

Save the file and run it.

```shell theme={null}
$ python voicemail.py
```

You should see your basic server application in action at [http://localhost:5000/voicemail/](http://localhost:5000/voicemail/).

Set up ngrok to expose your local server to the internet.
